10.1111/eff.70054: ABSTRACT Stream flows are widely regarded as a master variable affecting fish assemblages, with extreme events (e.g., floods, droughts) reorganising assemblages. Although assemblage turnover (temporal beta diversity) is common following hydrologic extremes, we have limited knowledge on how hydrologic extremes influence assemblage turnover across a broad spatial extent. In this study, we analysed time-series counts of stream fish assemblages at 34 sites in the conterminous US to characterise the relationship between assemblage turnover with high- and low-flow anomalies. We found that flow anomalies were equally important in explaining fish assemblage turnover when analysed across study sites. One-year lag effects of flow extremes were equally important to current-year effects. Temporal changes in relative abundance were a stronger factor of fish assemblage turnover than assemblage composition (i.e., species loss and gain). Species with the greatest contributions to assemblage turnover tended to be fluvial species that were locally abundant. Our study showed that neither high nor low flows influence stream fish assemblage turnover consistently across sites, suggesting context dependence. Further research with additional sites across ecoregions could identify factors determining this context dependency, which will help stream fish management under climate-change-induced hydrologic uncertainty and increasing human demand for water.
10.1111/fme.70134: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems in the Eastern Himalayan Region of India-a global biodiversity hotspot-are threatened by invasive alien fish species perhaps facilitated by exotic aquaculture, the aquarium trade, climate change, and inadequate regulation. The invasion of alien species disrupts native biodiversity, causes ecological imbalances, and threatens livelihoods dependent on freshwater resources. To address this, the present study develops an integrated management framework by synthesizing and adapting global biosecurity protocols, policy tools, and community-led conservation. The framework integrates three pillars: (1) advanced biosecurity, with real-time monitoring and predictive modeling for early detection; (2) strengthened, context-sensitive policies to regulate high-risk species trade and aquaculture while respecting local economies; and (3) community empowerment through stewardship programs using traditional knowledge, sustainable livelihoods, and awareness. Recognizing the region's unique geological history and the convergence of two biodiversity hotspots in Northeast India, the framework's strength lies in its tailored design, which explicitly leverages local communities and their traditional practices to provide culturally grounded, sustainable solutions. By fostering regional collaboration, using technology, and engaging communities, this approach aims to disrupt invasion pathways, protect biodiversity, and enhance ecosystem resilience, thereby contributing to global conservation goals.
10.1002/jaa2.70061: ABSTRACT A four-component stochastic frontier model is applied separately to nine broadly classified species group panels of U.S. aquaculture farms covering the years 2007 to 2017 to identify both time-varying and persistent inefficiencies for catfish, trout, “other” food fish, bait fish, ornamental fish, sport fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and “other” aquaculture products. We find considerable efficiency gaps in aquaculture production driven primarily by growers' persistent inefficiencies; average overall technical efficiency ranges from 43.8% to 53.7% for “other” aquaculture products and trout, respectively. This finding suggests that increased extension efforts promoting best planning practices for potential entrants can significantly improve U.S. aquaculture efficiency.
10.1111/fog.70095: ABSTRACT Phytoplankton primary production is essential to coastal food webs. However, the roles of different nutrient sources in semienclosed bays characterized by strong seasonal variability in physical conditions and nutrient availability are not well understood. We investigated seasonal variations in phytoplankton biomass and primary productivity over 2 years (June 2021-November 2023) at a shellfish aquaculture site in Miyazu Bay, Japan, where nutrients are supplied via offshore seawater intrusion and river discharge as well as submarine groundwater discharge (SGD). Vertically integrated chlorophyll a (Chl-a) and electron transport rate-based primary production were highest in winter, coinciding with elevated dissolved inorganic nutrient concentrations associated with offshore water inputs. However, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity declined in winter due to reduced solar radiation, indicating that phytoplankton biomass accumulated under nutrient-rich conditions despite light limitation. Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) within the water column was governed primarily by surface PAR rather than by the light attenuation coefficient, which was low and showed no seasonality. In contrast, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity peaked in summer, when surface nutrient concentrations were low but solar radiation was high. Geochemical tracers ( 222 Rn and 224 Ra) revealed continuous inputs of nutrient-rich groundwater near the seabed, suggesting that SGD may supplement nutrient availability during nutrient-depleted summer conditions. Size-fractionated analyses revealed that small phytoplankton (< 20 μm) dominated biomass and production throughout the year. These results also highlight SGD as a relatively persistent nutrient pathway that may supplement nutrient availability under light-rich but nutrient-poor summer conditions.
10.12688/f1000research.194150.1: Abstract* Fishery products are prone to quality deterioration during post-harvest handling and distribution. Therefore, the development of a sustainable cold chain requires the integration of facility planning, distribution efficiency, coastal zone management, and socio-ecological considerations. This study aims to synthesize these approaches and identify gaps in their integration. A systematic review was conducted through a literature search in the Scopus database, with reporting guided by PRISMA 2020. The initial search yielded 396 records; 222 records were retained after applying the publication year restriction of 2016-2026. Screening for document type, language, and access resulted in 134 records for title and abstract evaluation. A total of 37 publications proceeded to the eligibility assessment stage, and 12 publications were reported in a qualitative-thematic synthesis based on four research questions. The synthesis identified four main themes: location-allocation optimization and low-emission distribution; coastal spatial-ecological planning; facility accessibility and socioeconomic resilience; and carbon traceability and accountability. The results show that technical, ecological, and social approaches make complementary contributions, but their integration into a single fisheries cold chain planning model has not been comprehensively demonstrated in the reviewed literature. This study proposes a Coastal Cold Chain Integration Triad Framework that links spatial-ecological suitability, facility location-allocation optimization, and socio-ecological resilience and supply chain integrity. This framework provides a conceptual basis for research and planning in sustainable fisheries logistics, with a need for further empirical testing.
10.31961/eltikom.v10i2.2125: Current government aid programs in the fisheries sector often rely on reactive and uniform approaches, which may result in inefficient resource allocation. This study proposes an integrated dual-model machine learning framework to support more targeted fisheries aid allocation. The framework addresses two policy needs: predicting future vulnerability risk among capture fishers and estimating the success potential of aquaculture farmers. Data were obtained from the Integrated Fishery Reporting Application, comprising 625 aquaculture farmer records and 437 fisher records across 28 sub-districts in Lebak Regency, Banten, Indonesia. A Random Forest classifier was employed to classify fisher vulnerability into three categories: Low, Mid, and High Risk, while a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) regression model was used to predict survival rate as a proxy for farmer success potential. The optimized Random Forest model achieved a weighted F1-score of 0.8862, with recall values of 0.9268 for Mid Risk and 0.8889 for High Risk. The GBM model achieved an R-squared (R²) of 0.7585 and an RMSE of 6.0033 on the test data. These results indicate the potential of the framework to provide quantitative support for risk identification and aid prioritization. However, the findings are limited to data from a single regency and have not been evaluated through direct field implementation or policy intervention. Therefore, the framework should be considered an empirically evaluated decision-support approach rather than a fully validated policy tool.
10.3390/ani16233721: The Mekong Delta of Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia’s most important food-producing regions, supporting intensive rice cultivation, globally significant aquaculture, and diverse inland and rice-field fisheries that contribute to food security, rural livelihoods, and ecosystem functioning. However, hydraulic engineering, agricultural intensification, aquaculture expansion, urbanization, upstream river development, and climate-related pressures have progressively altered the hydrological and ecological processes sustaining these interconnected systems. This review synthesizes evidence on the transformation of rice-field fisheries and aquatic animal production in the Lower Mekong Basin, with particular emphasis on the Mekong Delta, and evaluates how effectively pollution governance addresses cumulative pressures on aquatic ecosystems. Peer-reviewed studies, official statistics, policy and legal documents, Mekong River Commission reports, and international institutional publications were assessed through a systematic critical review combining evidence mapping with structured narrative synthesis. The synthesis reveals a marked transition from hydrologically connected, multispecies production landscapes toward increasingly specialized rice and aquaculture systems. In the Mekong Delta region, recorded inland wild-fish catch declined from approximately 165,000 tonnes in 1995 to 30,000 tonnes in 2024, while aquaculture production increased more than eightfold, from approximately 78,000 to 650,000 tonnes, and rice production more than doubled, from 3.5 to 7.6 million tonnes. These contrasting trends coincided with high-dyke development, reduced floodplain connectivity, altered sediment and flow regimes, habitat modification, and greater agrochemical dependence. Major pollution pressures include nutrient and organic enrichment, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, domestic and industrial wastewater, micro-plastics, and acid-sulfate-soil drainage. Nevertheless, fishery decline cannot be attributed to pollution alone, because hydropower development, migration barriers, fishing pressure, habitat fragmentation, altered flood pulses, sediment deficits, and interact across spatial and temporal scales. Although Vietnam has established increasingly comprehensive fisheries, environment, water-resource, regional-planning, and climate-adaptation frameworks, implementation remains fragmented. Priority actions include integrated basin-to-field monitoring, cumulative-risk assessment, pollution prevention at source, stronger discharge controls, restoration of seasonal floodplain connectivity, protection of aquatic refuges, community co-management, and wider adoption of context-appropriate floating-rice, rice-fish, and rice-shrimp systems in this Delta region.
10.1111/jfb.70743: Abstract Traditional fisheries stock assessments incorporate life history data (e.g., mortality, growth, maturity), indices of abundance, and catch data into models to determine stock status and estimate biological reference points. However, obtaining these data in an accurate and timely manner can be challenging. While genetic techniques have been used for over 50 years to identify independent stocks, recent genomic innovations now allow for the generation of multiple stock assessment data inputs. Specifically, DNA extracted from non-lethally sampled tissue (e.g., fin clips) can be analyzed to monitor population structure and levels of connectivity, to estimate absolute abundance, to assess the age composition of landed or discarded catch, and to estimate sex ratios. Through standardized, adaptable, and minimally invasive methods to collect data necessary for robust stock assessments, genomic tools have the potential to provide a relatively comprehensive and cost-effective approach for long-term monitoring. The enhanced integration of next-generation genomic data into stock assessments will improve the accuracy and efficiency of fisheries assessment and management, ultimately supporting the sustainable use of marine resources.
10.32815/jpm.v7i2.3170: Purpose: This community engagement activity aimed to introduce Smart Costing based on Activity-Based Costing (ABC) to the Fish-Processing MSME Group in Domas Village, Pontang District, Serang Regency, and to improve participants’ understanding of financial recordkeeping and production cost calculation. Method: The activity took place on 22 October 2026 and included educational sessions and practical exercises on calculating production costs. Evaluation was qualitative, based on the implementation information provided by the community engagement team. Numerical pre-test and post-test scores and the exact number of individual participants were not available. Practical Applications: The activity introduced participants to more structured production-cost calculation. Follow-up collaboration is planned to support more orderly financial records, consistent production-cost calculations, and business development. Conclusion: The activity was reported to have run smoothly, with a reported change in participants’ understanding before and after the education. Since detailed evaluation records were unavailable, the magnitude of the change cannot be quantified. Continued mentoring is proposed to support application of the learning in daily business practices.
10.3390/microplastics5040238: Contaminants in commercially important fish provide relevant information on environmental exposure in coastal urban systems. This study investigated materials detected in the gastrointestinal tracts of croaker (Micropogonias furnieri) and horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) marketed in Santos, Brazil, and Maputo, Mozambique, integrating microscopy combined with Raman spectroscopy (µ-Raman), frequency analysis, and correspondence analysis with market categories and market-associated socioeconomic profiles. µ-Raman analysis included 68 spectral acquisitions, yielding 124 component assignments, including carbonaceous materials, synthetic polymers, cellulosic materials, pigments, dyes, and other chemical signatures. Carbon and graphite were the most frequent components, while polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyester-related materials predominated among synthetic polymers. Both study areas showed comparable spectral-occurrence patterns, particularly for PET, graphite, and cellulosic materials. Global chi-square tests showed no statistically significant dependence between material occurrence and either market categories or socioeconomic profiles. However, adjusted standardized residuals and correspondence analysis revealed localized distributional patterns involving specific materials and market categories, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than causal relationships. Integrating µ-Raman spectroscopy and multivariate analysis provides a useful framework for characterizing chemically diverse materials associated with gastrointestinal exposure in commercially important fish. Nevertheless, their occurrence in gastrointestinal tissues provides evidence of environmental exposure and may be relevant to ecological risk, which requires dedicated toxicological assessment. Because we analyzed only gastrointestinal tissues, the findings do not demonstrate contamination of edible muscle tissues, human dietary exposure, or health risk.
10.56557/upjoz/2026/v47i225956: Aquaculture is central to aquatic-food supply, yet expansion can intensify pressures associated with feed ingredients, energy consumption, nutrient discharge, disease, biodiversity and unequal access to technology. Contemporary innovation encompasses recirculating aquaculture systems, biofloc and integrated multi-trophic production, precision sensing and artificial intelligence, alternative feeds, molecular health tools, and environmentally informed siting. Their sustainability implications cannot be established from technological novelty or production efficiency alone. This critical narrative review evaluates these approaches across biological performance, resource accounting, commercial feasibility, welfare, environmental effects and governance. Peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional evidence published principally from 2015 to 12 September 2026 were examined, alongside influential earlier work. The synthesis finds comparatively strong mechanistic evidence for controlled water treatment, nutrient transformation, selective breeding and established vaccination programmes, but greater uncertainty about their net benefits across complete production chains. Recirculation can reduce water withdrawals and permit effluent capture while increasing dependence on reliable electricity and treatment infrastructure. Biofloc and extractive co-culture can retain or recover nutrients, although their effects depend on suspended solids, microbial stability, species compatibility, harvesting and system boundaries. Digital methods improve observation and predictive capability, yet farm-scale prospective validation, transferability and independent cost-benefit assessments remain limited. Novel feed ingredients may ease pressure on forage fish without necessarily reducing land use, processing energy or nutrient competition. Evidence on seaweed-based carbon benefits and broad ecosystem services is particularly context dependent. The review proposes a decision framework in which technologies are compared against a realistic baseline using life-cycle impacts, nutrient budgets, health and welfare outcomes, economic resilience and distributive effects. Priority research involves multi-cycle commercial comparisons, interoperable monitoring, causal field evaluation and integrated environmental-economic appraisal. Sustainable aquaculture is therefore best advanced through context-specific combinations of technologies, rather than a universal ranking of ‘smart’ solutions.
10.32815/jpm.v7i2.3098: Purpose: Rural Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) operating aquaculture units often face severe financial vulnerabilities and loss of Village Native Income (PADes) due to recurring night-time fish poaching and asset theft. This study evaluates and optimizes the existing CCTV infrastructure at BUMDes Marga Jaya, East Lampung, through a participatory community empowerment framework. Method: Executed under a 40-day Thematic Community Service (KKN-T) program by ITS NU Lampung, this project combined descriptive qualitative case study methods with a 4-stage community engagement strategy involving socialization, participatory technical auditing, hands-on training for four primary BUMDes operators/guards, and SOP formalization. Practical Applications: The program successfully upgraded network configurations, eliminated blind spots, conducted mobile app training, established bi-weekly maintenance SOPs, and integrated off-grid UPS/solar planning approved through village development deliberations. Conclusion: Combining optimized real-time CCTV technology with intensive community capacity building achieved zero theft incidents, enhanced internal labor discipline, and established a scalable model demonstrating how higher education partnerships bridge the digital divide for rural enterprise sustainability.

10.1021/acs.est.6c09109: Abstract Marine plastic pollution is an increasing environmental concern, yet aquaculture’s contribution remains poorly quantified despite its rapid expansion and reliance on plastic infrastructure. Limited data on plastic stocks, flows, losses, and end-of-life (EOL) management constrain effective mitigation and circularity strategies. This study presents a system-wide assessment of plastic use and management in Norway’s sea-based Atlantic salmon aquaculture industry. A static Material Flow Analysis (MFA), informed by data from equipment manufacturers, suppliers, operators, and waste-management stakeholders, quantifies plastic stocks and flows across equipment deployment, use, repair, replacement, environmental losses, and end-of-life treatment. The results indicate annual marine plastic losses of approximately 2737 t, corresponding to 1.2-1.7 kg per tonne of salmon produced. Feed pipes, walkway components, and consumable ropes dominate leakage. Approximately 37,400 t of end-of-life plastics are collected annually, with 42% directed to incineration with energy recovery, 22% landfilled, and limited recovery through recycling. These findings highlight substantial opportunities to strengthen collection, recycling, and resource recovery. This first comprehensive national-scale assessment establishes a quantitative baseline for monitoring and policy development. It demonstrates MFA’s utility for identifying leakage hotspots and supporting Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and circular economy strategies to reduce plastic pollution from aquaculture.
10.3390/agronomy16232356: Aquaculture ponds are an important anthropogenic source of CH4, and rice-fish co-culture has been proposed as a mitigation strategy; but the performance of different rice varieties in mitigating the CH4 emission from the ponds and the morphological traits of low-emission varieties remain unclear. A two-year (2024-2025) field experiment was conducted with three replicate ponds per treatment, each pond containing one plot of each variety; the plot served as the experimental unit. The six rice varieties were then compared for their effect on CH4 emission from aquaculture ponds. The results showed that co-culturing with different rice varieties significantly reduced CH4 emissions by 24.2-43.9% and 25.1-41.8% respectively in 2024 and 2025, compared with fish monoculture. Co-culturing with different rice varieties showed varying effects on CH4 emissions, and the rice variety ZGY1578 (Zhegengyou 1578) consistently showed the lowest CH4 emissions among the six varieties across both years. Accumulated CH4 emissions showed a negative correlation with the abundance of pmoA in the sediment and the radial oxygen loss (ROL) rate of rice roots and a positive correlation with plant-mediated CH4 emission, indicating that the variation among rice varieties was associated with methanotrophic abundance, root oxygen release and plant-mediated transport. Random forest analysis showed the highest variable importance of root number for predicting pmoA abundance, and root weight and root length were positively associated with ROL. Tiller number positively affected plant-mediated CH4 emission, whereas root number and root weight decreased it. Rice varieties with well-developed root systems showed strong rhizospheric CH4 oxidation and low plant-mediated CH4 emission, while excessive tillering promoted plant-mediated CH4 emission. High ROL, dense root systems, and moderate tillering were associated with low-emission rice varieties. These findings provide a basis for breeding low-emission rice varieties to reduce CH4 emission from aquaculture ponds by constructing rice-fish co-culture systems.
10.1093/mmy/myag132: Abstract Sporothrix brasiliensis is an emerging zoonotic fungal pathogen that has transformed sporotrichosis in Brazil from a sapronotic ‘gardener’s disease’ into a major zoonotic epidemic in South America. Here, ITS metabarcoding of 989 fish from coastal southern Brazil detected S. brasiliensis-compatible reads in 67.3% of pooled samples, and culture recovered viable isolates from selected samples. Genome typing placed fish-and bird-derived isolates within S. brasiliensis clinical Brazilian lineages, implicating aquatic-coastal interfaces in the ecology of this expanding pathogen.
10.3390/ani16233718: Fermented Pangasius by-products may replace conventional feed ingredients, but such substitutions alter several dietary nutrients simultaneously. We compared laying performance, egg quality, yolk cholesterol, selected fatty acids, and hematology in 150 Hisex Brown hens allocated to 30 cages (five replicate cages per diet) during a 60-day trial. Diets comprised a basal control (P0), four formulations containing 0.5-2.0% fermented Pangasius by-product extract with sugar-palm starch as partial replacement for soybean meal and fish meal (P1-P4), and a pigment-reference diet (P5). Cage-level outcomes were assessed by one-way ANOVA and Tukey comparisons. Hen-day egg production differed among diets (p = 0.0053): P3 (79.76%) and P4 (80.36%) exceeded P0 (61.91%). Feed conversion did not differ significantly (p = 0.294). Mean yolk cholesterol was 1384.1 mg/100 g dry matter in P0 and 995.6 mg/100 g in P4. The final worksheet identified EPA, DHA, linoleic acid, and oleic acid as measured; ALA and arachidonic acid were estimated and excluded from measured outcomes. Derived group omega totals and yolk n-6: n-3 ratios were withdrawn. Because the substitution changed multiple diet components, findings describe complete-diet associations, not an isolated ingredient effect or an optimal inclusion level.
10.1111/jfb.70724: Abstract The deep-sea catsharks in the genus Apristurus (Pentanchidae) constitute one of the most species-rich yet least resolved elasmobranch lineages. Herein, we utilised a systematic literature search to synthesise current knowledge on their diversity, morphology, phylogeny, distribution, ecology, reproduction and threats, and outline priorities for research aligned with the UN Decade of Ocean Science. The genus currently comprises 43 described extant species and three extinct taxa. Morphologically, Apristurus species share cephalic dorso-ventral compression, broad spatulate snouts and diagnostic labial-furrow states; meristics (including vertebral counts) and egg-capsule morphology provide additional taxonomic signal. Morphological ratios and fin shapes are also valuable for identification. Phylogenetic evidence generally supports monophyly of the genus and recovery of three species groups ( brunneus, spongiceps, longicephalus ), although some recent morphology-led hypotheses warrant further genomic testing. Apristurus is circumglobal (excluding polar seas and the Mediterranean), occupies depths ca. 24-2652 m and functions primarily as a generalist mesopredator, with region- and species-specific trophic specialisation. Reproductive ecology is oviparous; egg capsules commonly aggregate on structurally complex substrates (e.g., sponges and corals) where local hydrodynamics likely enhance embryonic ventilation. Fossil egg cases at cold seeps indicate long-standing associations with complex deep-sea habitats. Major threats to the genus arise from deep-sea trawl bycatch and emerging seabed industries. Threats are exacerbated by genus life-history traits (prolonged development, low fecundity) which imply high sensitivity, though many species remain listed as Least Concern owing to a paucity of data due to the depths at which the genus lives. Key research gaps identified include the need for a robust, integrative taxonomy; publicly accessible genetic reference libraries; in situ behavioural and life-history observations; quantification of bycatch and post-release mortality; and assessment of climate and mining impacts on nursery habitats. We provide a consolidated baseline of information to assist with accelerated discovery, identification and conservation of Apristurus across its global range.
10.3390/fishes11120686: Mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi) refuse artificial diets, but some individuals can be domesticated. To identify candidate molecular pathways and preliminary genomic loci associated with feed domestication difficulty, we compared easily domesticable (group T) and difficult-to-domesticate (group W) mandarin fish using brain transcriptome sequencing (n = 15 per group) and whole-genome resequencing (n = 30 per group). Transcriptome analysis identified 761 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with down-regulated genes predominating in group T. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed nominally significant positive enrichment of neurotransmitter transporter activity, sodium symporter activity, and Wnt signaling in group T, while cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction was down-regulated. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified the MEtan module as negatively correlated with growth-performance traits associated with domestication outcome and enriched in nucleosome, chromatin, and protein-DNA complex. Resequencing yielded 2,650,994 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), with intergroup differential SNPs annotated to 14,956 genes. Multi-omics integration prioritized 32 candidate genes across neural signaling/transport, chromatin/nucleosome, immune/inflammation, steroid/lipid metabolism, and cell structure/other; core candidates included slc1a5, gpr84, olfml2bb, and histone family genes. Notably, SNPs in gpr84 and olfml2bb showed nominal differences between groups. These findings suggest that enhanced neurotransmitter recycling and synaptic plasticity, lower neuroimmune activation, and chromatin regulation are associated with feed domestication success, providing preliminary candidate loci that require validation in larger, independent populations and should not yet be regarded as established markers for marker-assisted selection in easily domesticable mandarin fish.
10.3390/fishes11120685: Growth rate represents a core economic trait that determines both aquaculture production performance and market value of the foxface rabbitfish (Siganus vulpinus). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying growth variation in this species remain largely uncharacterized. In this study, full-sibling S. vulpinus individuals reared under identical controlled conditions were stratified into a rapid-growth (RG) and a slow-growth (SG) group based on growth performance, and skeletal muscle transcriptome sequencing was conducted to identify growth-related candidate genes. A total of 24,036 expressed genes were detected across both groups, with 13,663 genes co-expressed in the two groups. Differential expression analysis revealed 707 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 329 upregulated and 378 downregulated genes in the RG group relative to the SG group. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses showed that these DEGs were primarily enriched in biological processes associated with energy metabolism, protein turnover, amino acid metabolism, cytoskeletal organization, and muscle structural maintenance. Notably, the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway was significantly overrepresented, implying that carbohydrate metabolism and ATP provision are key contributors to muscle growth variation in S. vulpinus. Within the DEG set, S. vulpinus Eno3 was significantly upregulated in the RG group and identified as a core gene implicated in the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway. Bioinformatic characterization demonstrated that S. vulpinus Eno3 harbors a 1305 bp open reading frame (ORF) encoding 435 amino acids, and possesses the canonical conserved structural features of the enolase protein family. Phylogenetic analysis, conserved motif identification, functional domain annotation, and multiple sequence alignment collectively confirmed that S. vulpinus Eno3 is evolutionarily conserved and likely functions as a β-enolase isoform involved in glycolytic regulation. These findings indicate that S. vulpinus Eno3 may contribute to rapid muscle growth by modulating glycolytic flux, ATP generation, and metabolic intermediate availability. Collectively, this study provides valuable candidate gene resources and a theoretical foundation for deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying growth variation, and supports the future development of molecular breeding programs for S. vulpinus.
10.3390/fishes11120684: Abandoned, lost, or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) poses persistent environmental and management challenges. This study evaluated six direct gillnet marking methods and four gear-accounting units for South Korea’s fishing gear deposit system. The marking-type assessment combined previously derived AHP weights, preferences from 145 fishers and eight gear companies, and detachment observations from 1856 markings on nine net panels. At a common two-cycle endpoint, the textile double-sided tape fiber label ranked first (0.829), followed by the ultrasonic-welded (0.823) and gel-type tape labels (0.817). Using each gillnet’s last available observation changed the leading method to ultrasonic welding (0.718), while excluding swimming crab observations changed it to the gel-type label. For marking units, net-panel ranked first under equal expert-stakeholder weighting, whereas expert AHP alone favored weight. The results identify context-specific candidates for further field testing, not universally superior technologies or evidence of deposit-system effectiveness.
10.3390/fishes11120683: Aromatase (Cyp19a1), which converts testosterone to 17β-estradiol, plays a critical role in ovarian differentiation in teleosts. However, the transcriptional mechanisms regulating cyp19a1 during gonadal sex differentiation in Japanese eel (Anguilla japonica) remain unclear. We investigated the effects of Adrenal 4 binding protein/Steroidogenic factor 1 (Ad4bp/Sf-1) and Forkhead box L2 (Foxl2) and Foxl3 paralogs, and follicle-stimulating hormone (Fsh) signaling on cyp19a1 transcription using luciferase reporter assays in HEK293T and JTC-35 cells. Ad4bp/Sf-1, Foxl2a, or Fsh signaling alone did not activate the full-length (-5292/+38) cyp19a1 5′-flanking region, whereas combinations of these factors increased transcriptional activity. The simultaneous presence of Ad4bp/Sf-1, Foxl2a, and Fsh signaling produced the highest transcriptional activity in HEK293T cells. Co-transfection of Foxl2b with Foxl2a tended to reduce relative luciferase luminescence compared with Foxl2a alone, whereas Foxl3a and Foxl3b showed transcriptional activation potential under the experimental conditions used. Foxl3a, in particular, exhibited markedly high transcriptional activity in both cell lines despite the testis-biased expression of foxl3a and foxl3b in vivo. Deletion analysis showed that factor-dependent activation was markedly reduced by deletion to -847/+38 and abolished when the -847/+38 region was removed. Putative Ad4bp/Sf-1 and Foxl2 binding sites and a cAMP-responsive element were identified within this proximal region, suggesting that it may contribute to transcriptional responses to multiple regulatory factors. These findings provide insights into the potential combinatorial regulation of the Japanese eel cyp19a1 promoter and the distinct transcriptional regulatory properties of Foxl2 and Foxl3 paralogs under heterologous reporter assay conditions.

10.3389/fmars.2026.1888907: Offshore wind site selection requires transparent comparison of resource quality, marine exposure, engineering constraints, and project-scale characteristics. Previous multi-criteria studies often rely on expert-assigned weights, while project databases may combine observed, modelled, reanalysis-derived, and planned values without clearly distinguishing their provenance. This study applies a revised Principal Component Analysis-Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method (PCA-FCEM) workflow to the comparative technical screening of 16 European offshore wind projects and candidate sites. Following a full audit of the original database, project-year duplicates are retained only as an audit trail and the main analysis is conducted at project/site level using five consistently defined criteria: archived mean wind speed, archived wave-exposure indicator, mean water depth, minimum distance to shoreline, and installed/planned/reference project capacity. PCA is used as an exploratory objective-weighting device; three retained components explain 92.42% of total variance, and criterion weights are derived from retained-component communalities. Continuous fuzzy memberships on five suitability grades then yield comparative screening scores. Hollandse Kust Zuid ranks first (3.696), followed by Gennaker (3.672) and Kriegers Flak (3.597), whereas Sørvest F ranks lowest (2.350) because strong wind potential is offset by high wave exposure, greater water depth, and remoteness. The screening profiles also inform follow-up risk priorities: greater wave exposure and water depth motivate foundation, structural-load, and installation assessments, while greater remoteness highlights logistics and weather-window planning needs. Weight and fuzzy-partition perturbations preserve high rank agreement (minimum Spearman ρ = 0.938 and 0.982, respectively), while a non-compensatory max-min stress test produces substantially different ordering (ρ = 0.357). The framework is therefore presented as a transparent screening tool rather than a definitive investment or development-readiness ranking. A complete provenance audit and reanalysis workbook is supplied as Supplementary Data S1 . Holding FCEM inputs and membership/aggregation rules fixed, Entropy-FCEM and CRITIC-FCEM yield Spearman rank correlations of 0.679 and 0.894 with the PCA-based ranking, showing that conclusions are sensitive to the weighting strategy.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1946690: Introduction Protecting and restoring blue carbon ecosystems is an important nature-based solution for mitigating global warming and promoting sustainable coastal development. As blue carbon projects enter carbon markets, credit credibility is critical to realising their climate and financial benefits. Methods This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game model involving project developers, third-party verifiers, and government regulators to examine blue carbon credit governance under rent-seeking. The model distinguishes low-effort verification of genuine projects from collusive verification of fraudulent projects and combines stability analysis with numerical simulations to examine strategic interactions and policy effects. Results Results show that credible governance need not depend on sustained intensive regulation. Increasing development subsidies and reputational benefits for both parties to give compliance a payoff advantage is key to achieving an ideal governance state. Under these conditions, this state can be maintained even as regulatory intensity declines. Moreover, the incentive-based policy achieves the ideal state under all three initial conditions, while the combined incentive -fine policy further accelerates convergence. Discussion This study advances understanding of the evolutionary mechanisms underlying blue carbon credit governance and informs the selection of policy instruments and the design of policy packages.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1886191: This study investigates the non-linear dynamic response and fatigue damage accumulation of a monopile offshore wind turbine support structure under combined wind, wave, and current loading. Wave-current interaction is incorporated directly into the Morison hydrodynamic force model, and its effects on stress response and fatigue damage are quantified across nine load cases spanning three wind-speed levels and three current-velocity levels. Results show that linear superposition of environmental loads underestimates stress amplitude by 7.6% to 23.1% relative to the coupled approach, with the largest discrepancies concentrated near the mudline. At the critical mudline section, coupled fatigue damage reaches 0.912 over the 25-year design life, compared to 0.768 under uncoupled loading, corresponding to a fatigue life overestimation of approximately 19%. A Kriging surrogate model trained on coupled-simulation data achieves an R² of 0.968 and is employed in a constrained optimization to minimize fatigue-equivalent stress. The wave-current difference-frequency coupling produces a spectral reshaping effect that amplifies low-frequency fatigue cycles beyond what amplitude scaling alone would predict, and this mechanism is not captured by linear superposition. The optimized design reduces fatigue-equivalent stress by 24.2% and structural mass by 7.7%, while extending predicted fatigue life from 27.4 to 36.1 years. These findings suggest that accounting for wave-current non-linearity in both fatigue assessment and structural optimization produces more physically consistent design outcomes.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2040572: Introduction Blue carbon credits are increasingly advocated as a way to finance the conservation and restoration of coastal ecosystems; however, the development of carbon markets does not necessarily guarantee credible climate mitigation. This article examines the legal governance of blue carbon credits in China's national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction market. Methods Combining doctrinal legal analysis, institutional comparison, and qualitative risk assessment, the study operationalizes a six-part framework covering additionality, quantification accuracy, permanence, leakage control, prevention of double counting, and independent validation, verification, and transparency. This analysis reviews China's CCER regulatory framework and the Ecological and Environmental Code, along with the methodologies for mangrove afforestation, coastal salt marsh restoration, and seagrass bed restoration. Results It finds that existing rules establish basic safeguards for project eligibility, carbon accounting, third-party verification, and centralized registration; however, they do not fully address the interaction between pre-existing conservation obligations and additionality, baseline uncertainty, long-term reversal liability, cross-mechanism information coordination, and ecological accountability. These gaps show that neither formal compliance with regulatory requirements nor project registration is sufficient to ensure the environmental integrity of issued credits. Discussion The article recommends more specific eligibility requirements, stronger monitoring, reporting, and verification, enforceable reversal-risk management, better-coordinated information systems, and clearer legal responsibilities that integrate carbon credit governance with marine ecosystem protection. The article concludes that effective blue carbon governance must move beyond market expansion and toward life-cycle legal safeguards that can secure credible and durable mitigation outcomes while also supporting marine ecosystem conservation.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1977826: Two strong-wind events along the Yellow Sea coast produced opposite water-level responses despite comparable peak wind speeds. We combined paired buoy-ADCP observations with ERA5 winds and CMEMS sea level to examine the shared and site-dependent responses and their relation to regional coastal adjustment. Maximum 10-min mean wind speeds ranged from 15.8 to 17.0 m s -1 . E01 exceeded 10.8 m s -1 for 47 -48 h and accumulated an eastward alongshore stress impulse of +12.67 to +13.87 N h m -2 , whereas E08 exceeded the threshold for 21 -23 h and accumulated a westward impulse of -3.03 to -2.37 N h m -2 . Cross-shore stress impulses were similar and directed offshore. The pressure-derived water-level anomalies showed approximately 0.47 m of setdown during E01 and 0.32-0.33 m of setup during E08 at both stations. Alongshore transport anomalies within the observed core layer were eastward in E01 and westward in E08, while cross-shore responses differed between sites. CMEMS reproduced the subtidal water-level variations (r=0.982 -0.997), and extremum times increased with distance from Rizhao to Shidao. During E08, pressure gradients near the observation sites continued to develop after local wind weakening. These observations link shared water-level and alongshore-transport responses with contrasting forcing histories and regional adjustment, while revealing local differences in cross-shore transport. Tidal and hydrographic differences between the two events may also have influenced these responses.
10.17977/2580-2402.1277: The escalation of production capacity within the aquaculture sector triggers an accumulation of solid waste that degrades water quality, a condition establishing fundamental operational constraints for conventional mechanical filtration systems in recirculating aquaculture systems. Hydrocyclone separators emerge as a promising economically viable technological alternative; however, investigations regarding their specific optimization for managing fishery particulates with low density margins remain profoundly limited. This computational investigation implements a computational fluid dynamics framework, coupling the Reynolds stress model with the discrete phase model, to quantify the separation performance of a modified hydrocyclone design across ten variations of inlet flow rates. Through validation against benchmark data, the simulation outputs reveal that the degree of vortex maturity is absolutely governed by the fluid injection velocity. The minimum flow rate proves inadequate to construct a coherent forced vortex core, whereas the maximum flow condition conversely generates a dual peak Rankine vortex structure manifesting spatial asymmetry. In stark contrast to fundamental theoretical probabilities, the cumulative separation efficacy exhibits a negative correlation with increasing flow rates, characterized by an efficiency degradation from 72% to 64%. This physical reality confirms that an inlet momentum exceeding the optimal threshold escalates local turbulence and reduces particle retention duration, which in turn comprehensively disrupts the effectiveness of the centrifugal separation mechanism.
10.71317/kjard.2.11.2026.1099: The northern Arabian Sea along Pakistan's 1,001 km coastline represents a biologically productive yet increasingly threatened marine ecosystem, supporting over 500 cataloged fish species of substantial commercial and ecological importance. Escalating anthropogenic pressures, including overfishing, illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, habitat degradation, and the intensifying Arabian Sea Oxygen Minimum Zone (OMZ), have severely altered fish community structures and precipitated declines in key commercial stocks. Traditional monitoring approaches, reliant on catch landings, net trawling, and morphological taxonomy, are constrained by phenotypic plasticity, cryptic speciation, specimen damage, and an inability to identify early life stages or processed products. This review synthesizes the transformative potential of two complementary molecular technologies environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding and population genomics for biodiversity assessment and sustainable fisheries management along the Pakistan coast. eDNA metabarcoding enables non-invasive, high-throughput, multi-taxa community profiling through mitochondrial markers (COI, Cyt b, 12S/16S rRNA), facilitating detection of elusive, endangered, and cryptic species, including remnant sawfish populations and coral-associated assemblages in Astola Island MPA. Population genomics, leveraging SNPs and mitochondrial sequencing, resolves stock boundaries, genetic diversity, and demographic histories, revealing distinct Evolutionary Significant Units in silver pomfret (Pampus argenteus) and genetic connectivity patterns in Spanish mackerel (Scomberomorus commerson). Integrated applications extend to seafood traceability via DNA-based QR codes, IUU fishing detection, and Blue Economy policy alignment with SDG 14. Key challenges include eDNA degradation under high temperatures, PCR bias, incomplete regional reference databases, and infrastructural capacity gaps. Strategic multi-institutional partnerships and sustained investment are essential for operational implementation, offering a paradigm shift toward resilient, evidence-based fisheries governance in Pakistan.
10.1111/jfd.70328: ABSTRACT Hyperostosis in wild fishes remains poorly documented and quantitative information on its size-related onset and anatomical distribution in Oligoplites palometa (Cuvier, 1832) is limited. We quantified hyperostosis prevalence and described its skeletal distribution across size classes in O. palometa from two estuarine systems on the coast of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Guanabara Bay and Sepetiba Bay). A total of 31 specimens ranging from 45 to 510 mm TL were examined by radiography, followed by excision and morphometric analysis of the unaffected and affected bones. Hyperostosis was observed in all examined individuals ≥ 315 mm TL, whereas none was detected in specimens ≤ 82 mm. No individuals between 82 and 315 mm total length (TL) were available, limiting the assessment of the onset and progression of hyperostosis within this size range. Hyperostoses were detected in the cranium, cleithrum, dorsal pterygiophores and anal pterygiophores, with the cleithrum showing the highest prevalence (80.64%), followed by dorsal pterygiophores (77.41%), anal pterygiophores (67.7%) and cranium (61.29%). These findings indicate a consistent size-related pattern of skeletal involvement, highlighting the importance of population size structure when evaluating hyperostosis in wild fish populations.
10.1111/jfd.70326: ABSTRACT Climate change is expected to increase seawater salinity, potentially altering the physiological responses of marine organisms. In salmonids, elevated salinity has been associated with outbreaks of infectious diseases; however, the mechanisms linking salinity with intestinal epithelial dysfunction and bacterial invasion remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of increased sodium chloride concentrations on the integrity of the rainbow trout intestinal epithelial cell line RTgutGC and its relationship with P. salmonis translocation. Cells cultured under control (8 g/L NaCl) or hyperosmotic conditions (16 and 20 g/L NaCl) were assessed for cytotoxicity, epithelial integrity, permeability, bacterial translocation, and gene expression. Hyperosmotic conditions significantly increased epithelial permeability and reduced barrier integrity, as evidenced by altered paracellular permeability to Dextran FITC and modulation of tight junction-related genes, including cld-3 and zo-1 . Salinity also induced the expression of osmoregulatory ( tsc22 and nka ) and immune-related genes ( il-1β and il-10 ), indicating activation of response to osmotic stress. Importantly, elevated salinity significantly enhanced the translocation of P. salmonis across the epithelial monolayer, whereas no bacterial translocation was detected under control conditions. Moreover, high salinity increased infection-associated cytotoxicity, mainly at 20 g/L NaCl. Together, these findings demonstrate that increased sodium chloride concentration compromises intestinal epithelial barrier function while promoting P. salmonis translocation. These results provide mechanistic evidence linking climate-driven changes in seawater salinity with increased epithelial susceptibility to bacterial pathogens and suggest that osmotic stress may represent an important environmental factor influencing the pathogenesis of piscirickettsiosis in salmonids.
10.1111/jfd.70325: ABSTRACT Tilapia lake virus is a major constraint to sustainable Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) production, yet effective antiviral interventions remain limited. We evaluated the antiviral potential of procyanidin against tilapia lake virus (TiLV) using complementary cell-based and in vivo challenge models involving 300 Nile tilapia. Procyanidin displayed a concentration-dependent safety profile, with a non-cytotoxic concentration of 0.0128 mg/mL in E-11 cells and an estimated LC 10 of 0.6528 mg/mL in fish. At the selected cellular concentration, procyanidin prevented virus-associated cytopathic effects and reduced TiLV RNA in culture supernatants to below the RT-qPCR detection limit. In vivo, procyanidin administration 24 h before or after viral challenge increased survival from 43.33% in untreated infected fish to 80.00% and 73.33%, respectively, corresponding to relative percent survival values of 64.44% and 52.22%. Treatment also reduced brain viral load by up to 3.12 log 10 units and was associated with qualitatively better-preserved brain and liver histoarchitecture. Hepatic transcriptional profiling revealed distinct treatment-associated expression patterns across inflammatory, innate immune recognition, antigen presentation, cellular immunity and antiviral interferon signalling pathways, with pre-treatment producing the strongest induction of several antiviral genes. Together, these findings identify procyanidin as a candidate antiviral compound against tilapia lake virus, with in vitro antiviral activity accompanied in vivo by improved survival, reduced brain viral load and treatment-associated changes in hepatic immune-gene expression, although the underlying protective mechanism remains to be established.
10.1163/15718085-20261060: Abstract The Chinese Fisheries Law was adopted in January 1986 and came into force on 1 July 1986. Four amendments and one revision have been made to the document since then. A revision in 2025 reflects China’s commitment to enhancing fisheries quality, efficiency, and green development. Initially, this article provides a brief overview of the Law, and then it evaluates some key changes in the revision of 2025. It concludes by pointing out some concerns that remain in the Law following the recent revision.
10.1111/1365-2656.70408: Abstract Spatial population synchrony, broadly defined as the correlated temporal dynamics of a population metric (e.g. abundance, biomass or growth rates) across sampled areas, is a central theme in ecology. Here, we investigated spatial synchrony in the abundance of 38 fish species from the Jirau Reservoir, a large impoundment in the Amazonian basin, over a decade. We combined cross-correlation at zero lag, tail dependence, synchrony networks, species traits and wavelets to investigate asymmetry, geography and the temporal structure of spatial synchrony. We found that 12 species exhibited significant river-wide synchrony, with no asymmetrical or spatial patterns of within-river synchrony. Water level synchrony, dispersal difficulty and density dependence explained little of the variation in within-river synchrony. However, wavelet analyses showed that the strength of river-wide synchrony varied across temporal scales, and some species also shifted in the dominant timescale of synchrony over time. Furthermore, key species traits such as migratory strategy, body size and trophic level were not significantly correlated with river-wide synchrony levels. These findings underscore the necessity of using multifaceted analytical approaches to understand and manage fish populations in human-altered aquatic ecosystems, where local factors may override broad-scale drivers.
10.63249/j-sh.v1i2.167: This study analyzes fishers' compliance with and perceptions of licensing documents at the Marine and Fisheries Resources Surveillance Office (PSDKP), Takalar Station, which operates within the working area of PSDKP Bitung. The objectives were: (1) to describe fishers' compliance with the procedures for issuing licensing documents and (2) to describe fishers' perceptions of licensing documents through an assessment of service quality. The study employed a descriptive design with a survey approach. A purposive sample of 30 adult fishers (aged 18-59 years) who were applying for or had previously applied for licenses was selected. The instrument was a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Compliance was measured using 20 statements representing 10 indicators of public service compliance assessment based on Ombudsman Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia Number 22 of 2016. Perceived service quality was measured using 16 statements representing the eight elements of the Service Quality Perception Survey (SPKP) (Constitutional Court of the Republic of Indonesia, 2023). Data were analyzed descriptively through frequency and percentage tabulation. The results show that fishers' compliance is very high; variation appeared only in the habit of reading written information on notice boards or service media (27 always; 3 rarely). Fishers' perceptions were also predominantly positive: information was easy to understand, requirements and procedures were clear, the service flow was easy to follow, completion time matched the estimate and was relatively short, facilities were comfortable and adequate, and officers were responsive in consultations and complaint handling. Regarding costs, all respondents considered the fees to be in accordance with regulations, yet seven respondents sometimes felt that the cost of processing was quite burdensome. It is concluded that licensing services at PSDKP Takalar are effective in fostering compliance and positive perceptions, with recommendations to strengthen the dissemination of written information and to mitigate indirect cost burdens so that services become more inclusive. These findings are relevant to improving licensing governance.
10.9734/ajrcos/2026/v19i11936: Fish diseases can compromise aquaculture production through reduced growth, deteriorating fish quality and increased mortality. Conventional disease identification often depends on time-consuming manual inspection. This study compared convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures containing two, three and four convolutional layers for classifying five fish disease categories and healthy fish. A dataset of 1,600 images was assembled from existing repositories and selected websites. The images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels and divided into training, validation and testing subsets at an 80:10:10 ratio. The models were trained for 100 epochs using a batch size of 32, with rotation and contrast augmentation applied to the training images. Model performance was assessed through classification accuracy, training and validation curves, and class-level evaluation measures. Across five executions, average test accuracies were 91.13%, 95.73% and 95.27% for the two-, three- and four-layer CNNs, respectively. The three-layer CNN showed comparatively stable training and validation behaviour, whereas the other architectures displayed less stable generalisation or indications of overfitting. Two additional baseline models were evaluated on the same dataset: fine-tuned VGG16 achieved 96.41% accuracy, and a VGG16-Random Forest hybrid achieved 93.56%. Among the three CNN architectures examined, the three-layer model provided the highest average accuracy and a favourable balance between classification performance and architectural depth on the dataset used.
10.63249/j-sh.v1i2.166: Fish Landing Bases (PPI) play a strategic role in supporting capture fisheries, improving fishers' livelihoods, and strengthening coastal economic development. This study aimed to analyze the implementation of the policy on the utilization of the Lonrae Fish Landing Base (PPI) in Bone Regency using the policy implementation framework proposed by Van Meter and Van Horn. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed through in-depth interviews, field observations, documentation, and secondary data analysis. Informants consisted of representatives from the Provincial Marine and Fisheries Office, the Bone Regency Fisheries Office, PPI management, fishers, and local community members. The findings indicate that the implementation of the policy has generally progressed in accordance with its intended objectives, particularly in improving fisheries services and supporting local economic activities. The policy benefits from clear objectives, positive implementer commitment, supportive social conditions, and relatively effective inter-agency coordination. However, its effectiveness is constrained by limited financial resources, insufficient human resources, inadequate supporting facilities, suboptimal communication with fishers, and operational management challenges. These constraints have prevented the full optimization of PPI functions, particularly regarding fish auction services, infrastructure utilization, and service delivery. Strengthening institutional coordination, increasing infrastructure investment, enhancing human resource capacity, improving stakeholder communication, and expanding operational budgets are therefore essential to maximize the role of Lonrae Fish Landing Base as a sustainable fisheries infrastructure that contributes to fisheries governance and the welfare of coastal communities.
10.6066/jtip.2026.37.3.271: Tuna processing industries generate a significant amount of by-products, including dark muscle and skin, which are potential sources of functional proteins such as fish protein hydrolysate (FPH) and gelatin. This study aimed to characterize FPH from tuna dark muscle and gelatin from tuna skin, while evaluating the effects of freeze-drying (FD) and oven-drying (OV) on their physicochemical and antioxidant properties. The results indicated that the yield and proximate composition of FPH-FD and FPH-OV did not differ significantly (p>0.05). In contrast, antioxidant activity showed a significant effect (p<0.05), with FPH-OV exhibiting a stronger radical-scavenging capacity than FPH-FD, as indicated by its lower IC50 value, namely 152.75 µg/mL and 647.68 µg/mL, respectively. Unlike FPH, the drying methods for gelatin significantly influenced moisture content, ash content, gel strength, and antioxidant activity (p<0.05). The freeze-dried gelatin had higher gel strength (399.7 g) than oven-dried gelatin (372.7 g), although both values exceeded the typical high-Bloom range of 200-300 g. Under the tested laboratory conditions, oven-drying at 60 °C produced FPH with yield and proximate composition comparable to those of freeze-drying and with higher antioxidant activity, whereas it increased moisture and ash contents of gelatin and reduced its gel strength.
10.1007/s44187-026-01368-z: Abstract Fish and fishery products are increasingly recognized as important components of healthy and sustainable diets, yet consumption remains low and seasonal in several inland European markets. This study examines motivational heterogeneity in fish and fishery product consumption in Hungary and explores its potential implications for freshwater aquaculture commercialization. The total sample comprised 576 respondents, of whom 463 reported consuming fish or fishery products. Exploratory factor analysis and Gaussian Mixture Modelling were conducted on the subsample of 314 fish-consuming respondents who provided complete valid responses to all motivational items. Exploratory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations identified two latent motivational dimensions: convenience and accessibility, and health and product characteristics. Gaussian Mixture Modelling distinguished three consumer segments: health-oriented, moderately practical consumers; low-motivation consumers; and convenience-dominated consumers. Taste and perceived health benefits emerged as the strongest general motivations, while convenience, accessibility and ready-to-cook formats contributed more strongly to differentiating between consumer profiles. The findings indicate that motivational heterogeneity may be relevant when considering the commercialization of freshwater aquaculture products in a low-consumption inland market. However, the survey measured motivations toward fish and fishery products in general rather than attitudes toward farmed fish specifically. Therefore, the aquaculture-related conclusions should be interpreted as sectoral implications rather than as direct empirical evidence of attitudes toward aquaculture. Interpreted in the light of previous literature, the identified consumer profiles suggest that transparent product information, trust-building and convenient product formats may support the development of more differentiated commercialization approaches for freshwater aquaculture value chains.
10.1111/cobi.70425: Abstract Coastal fisheries are typically managed within bounds set by political jurisdictions of nations and their provinces. This approach often results in multiple states/provinces managing a single genetically distinct fish population autonomously and typically without coordination. In multispecies, decentralized, and data-poor fisheries, this can lead to inadequate assessments and fisheries overharvests. We developed an integrative risk indicator for interjurisdictional stocks (IRIIS) to assess the overexploitation risk to interjurisdictional populations. IRIIS incorporates species-specific vulnerability, distribution of genetically distinct populations with respect to jurisdictional boundaries, and differences in management practices across jurisdictions. As a case study, we used genetic tools and policy analysis to evaluate nine common target species spanning multiple jurisdictions along India's western coast. We showed that distinct populations of a species differed greatly in how they are managed by respective fisheries, and management disparities across jurisdictions can strongly influence the overexploitation risk for a population. IRIIS clearly identified these differences and helped determine specific fisheries policies that need reconciling across jurisdictions to reduce the risk of overexploitation. As a comprehensive management instrument, IRIIS is dynamic and sensitive to periodic revisions in fishery policy and could guide managers across jurisdictions in lowering the overexploitation risks to multispecies coastal fisheries.
10.3390/fishes11110679: Underwater fish disease detection is a vital visual perception task for health monitoring, disease early warning and precision breeding management in aquaculture. In complicated underwater environments, fish lesions suffer from faint boundaries and tiny sizes, while cross-scale fused features of detection models are contaminated by mixed degradation interference. To tackle the above issues, this paper proposes a YOLOv12-based detection method for fish lesions under complex underwater conditions. Firstly, an underwater spatial context receptive field module named CRB is designed. It expands the receptive range of shallow features through two-stage depthwise separable dilated convolution, establishes spatial correlations between local lesion responses and surrounding neighborhood structures and enhances the local structural representation of lesions with faint boundaries and small scales. Secondly, an underwater degradation-aware channel enhancement module DCE is presented. Degradation priors are constructed from image intensity, gradient and local contrast. Combined with mixed pooling to generate channel weights, the module recalibrates lesion-related responses and degradation interference responses after cross-scale feature fusion, so as to suppress the propagation of degradation noise within fused features. Lastly, the experiments are conducted on a self-built underwater largemouth bass lesion detection dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves Precision of 87.4%, Recall of 81.3%, F1-score of 84.2% and mAP@50 of 85.8%, which outperforms the baseline model by 3.3, 3.7, 3.5 and 3.6 percentage points, respectively. The proposed method serve as an effective visual perception solution for fish lesion detection in complex underwater environments.
10.1111/jfb.70740: Abstract Aquatic invasive species are among the top threats to freshwater fishes globally, causing declines in freshwater biodiversity and altering ecosystem functioning. Within Nova Scotia, Canada, invasive chain pickerel ( Esox niger ) and smallmouth bass ( Micropterus dolomieu ) have been found to reduce the abundance and diversity of native fishes. The invasive range of both species threatens and overlaps with the critical habitat of one of Canada's most endangered fishes, the Atlantic whitefish ( Coregonus huntsmani ). Here, we examine the seasonal space and depth use of adult chain pickerel and smallmouth bass using acoustic telemetry in Milipsigate Lake, Nova Scotia. High-resolution positions were calculated and analyzed using resource selection functions (RSFs) and generalized additive models (GAMs) to determine the relative space use and predicted depth of both species within the lake. Areas with the highest relative probability of use (>0.7) differed between species, and seasonal changes in space use were only significant for smallmouth bass ( p < 0.001). Chain pickerel had the highest relative probability of space use in shallow areas of Milipsigate Lake (<4 m), whereas areas with the highest relative probability of space use for smallmouth bass were concentrated around four distinct overwintering sites. Chain pickerel were predicted to occupy a narrow range (~2 m) of relatively shallow depths year-round. Smallmouth bass were predicted to occupy depths that were on average three times deeper than chain pickerel, including a broad range of depths from spring to fall (0-15 m) that contracted during the winter months (2-6 m). Here, we showed that the combined occupancy of the lake by both species is extensive, with limited overlap in space or depth use year-round. Ultimately, the methodologies and results presented in this study could help inform the development of management strategies for invasive freshwater fish species.
10.1007/s12520-026-02600-8: Abstract Euryhaline fish pose a challenge when interpreting the fishing habitats utilised in areas where both fresh and saline waters would have been accessible. One such example is the island of Gotland, central Baltic Sea, where archaeological fishbone assemblages often contain euryhaline fish species that could have originated from different habitats. To understand which waterbodies were used for fishing in the past, 87 Sr/ 86 Sr ratios of 41 fish teeth from the Mesolithic, Neolithic and Viking Age - Middle Ages were analysed using laser ablation-multi collector-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry and correlated with a bioavailable baseline of water sources. We identify several shifts in the origin of euryhaline fish and discuss them in relation to environmental and cultural shifts. Using modern ecological knowledge, we discuss the likely habitat structures in the now drained lakes of Gotland. The results enhance our understanding of prehistoric and historic fishing practices and shed light on the broader socio-economic and environmental dynamics on the island of Gotland.
10.51317/wrehv191: The purpose of this study was to analyse the influence of effective communication on the sustainability of women’s small-scale fisheries in Homa Bay County, Kenya. The sustainability of women-led small-scale fisheries enterprises is often constrained by inadequate communication and information-sharing mechanisms, which limit women's ability to access timely market information, share enterprise-related challenges, participate in collective decision-making, and identify solutions to emerging operational constraints. These communication barriers stand to undermine enterprise resilience, compromise the quality and nutritional value of fish products, and ultimately threaten the livelihood security of fishers' households. The study is anchored on the Magic Bullet Theory (Hypodermic Needle Model). Applying the mixed-methods approach, the study analysed quantitative and qualitative data collected from a sample of 330 small-scale women fishers with a ninety-six per cent response rate. The results from both data sources were triangulated and became the basis of the study findings and conclusions. Fisher’s effective communication had a moderate and significant relationship with the sustainability of small-scale fisheries. The findings revealed that r=0.342, R2= 0.117, F (1,341) =45.597, at P=0.000<0.05, confirming that fishers' effective communication had a statistically significant contribution to the sustainability of small-scale fisheries. The coefficient of determination, R2= 0.117, indicates that fishers' effective communication activities explain 11.7 per cent of the variation in the sustainability of fisheries by women. The paper contributes to the literature on the role of effective communication in the sustainability of small-scale enterprises, poverty reduction among small-scale fishers, and nutritional value among families of women fishers. Furthermore, it adds to the importance of fishers engaging in a dialogue with the market and community.
10.1139/as-2026-0032: In this paper, we describe how Inuit traditional knowledge and western science have been mobilized over three decades to support the co-management of Arctic char (iqalukpik) (Salvelinus alpinus) fisheries in the waters near Ulukhaktok in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region (ISR), Canada. Fisheries within the ISR are co-managed under the provisions of the Inuvialuit Final Agreement, with support from the Inuvialuit-Canada Fisheries Joint Management Committee (FJMC) as the designated co-management board. In response to community concerns of declines in one of its most important subsistence fisheries, the FJMC worked with Inuit from Ulukhaktok to establish a community-based Working Group focused on Arctic char in the area in 1993. Through the efforts and leadership of the Ulukhaktok Char Working Group (UCWG), co-management partners have mobilized traditional knowledge and western science continually over the past three decades through opportunities for information-sharing both within the UCWG and the broader community, harvest data collection, fisheries monitoring, and additional community-driven research programs. These activities have informed the UCWG in the development, implementation, and ongoing annual reviews of its community Fishing Plan, which describes the current knowledge of the fishery and management measures that support conservation, sustainable use, and stewardship.
10.3897/aiep.56.213543: Elasmobranchs are ecologically and commercially important, but biological information remains limited for many species. This study investigated length-weight relationships (LWRs) of elasmobranchs caught as bycatch in a set-net fishery at Nishiki, Mie Prefecture, Japan, during 2018-2025. A total of 739 individuals representing 21 species were collected during 284 fishing operations, and 15 species with at least five individuals remaining after exclusion of damaged specimens and Cook’s distance outliers were analyzed. LWR parameters were estimated, for groups with at least ten specimens, in 13 species: Cephaloscyllium umbratile Jordan et Fowler, 1903; Sphyrna zygaena (Linnaeus, 1758); Hemitriakis japanica (Müller et Henle, 1839); Mustelus manazo Bleeker, 1854; Triakis scyllium Müller et Henle, 1839; Heterodontus japonicus Maclay et Macleay, 1884; Bathytoshia brevicaudata (Hutton, 1875); Hemitrygon akajei (Müller et Henle, 1841); Hemitrygon izuensis (Nishida et Nakaya, 1988); Gymnura japonica (Temminck et Schlegel, 1850); Myliobatis tobijei Bleeker, 1854; Urolophus aurantiacus Müller et Henle, 1841; and Okamejei schmidti (Ishiyama, 1958). Of the 15 species analyzed, 11 are classified as threatened on the IUCN Red List and two Near Threatened. For batoids, both disc width (DW) and total length (TL) were evaluated, and DW gave higher coefficients of determination than TL in all six ray species with sufficient data. Sex-combined LWR exponents ( b ) ranged from 1.659 to 4.168. BIC-based model selection indicated sex-specific intercepts with a common slope for four species-measurement combinations. These LWRs provide baseline biometric information for biomass estimation, bycatch assessment, and fisheries management.
10.56201/ijccp.v10.no1.2024.pg116.132: Monitoring of contamination level in Lake Geriyo was coordinated by evaluating the concentrations of metals (Zn, Cu, Pb, & Cd) in sediment and fish samples of the lake in two seasons. The order of the concentrations of the metals in the sediment were Zn > Cu > Pb > Cd. The results showed that the metals exhibited lower values than sediment quality guideline (SQG). Thus, Lake Geriyo sediment can be categorized as unpolluted. Metal levels were within the set limit of TEL, PEL, ERL, and ERM which indicated that the sediment did not pose any danger to local fauna and flora. Zn and Cd were below the background values (Hakanson, 1980) nevertheless Pb and Cu exceeded. Metal Bioaccumulation were determined in the liver, gills and flesh from benthic and pelagic fish species obtained from the lake. The levels of the heavy metals differ remarkably amid fish species and organs. Flesh have the lowest concentration of all the metals. Liver was the choose organ for Zn, Cu and Pb accumulations. Cd nevertheless exhibited higher concentration in the gills. The metals bio concentration in fish flesh were acceptable by the international legislation limits for Cu, Zn, and Cd but however Pb go beyond in Clarias and Tilapia for wet season and Heterotis both seasons , consequently risky for human consumption and a danger to public health. These levels might be likely due to anthropogenic inputs as there is no industrial activity around the lake.
10.3390/jmse14222209: Marine aquaculture wastes move among water, particles, sediments, and biomass. Evaluating system-wide benefits requires accounting for elemental stocks, discharge loads, and the fate of harvested biomass. This narrative review examines species-specific evidence for sea purslane (Sesuvium portulacastrum) and the polychaete Perinereis aibuhitensis, alongside evidence from other halophytes, macroalgae, and polychaetes. Sea purslane assimilates dissolved nitrogen and produces harvestable biomass. The polychaete consumes deposited particles and ventilates burrows. These activities can affect assimilation, organic matter mineralization, and particle movement. In one experiment, sediment nitrogen and phosphorus fractions changed. Final nutrient concentrations in the overlying water exceeded control values, and polychaete biomass fell. One field study documented natural co-occurrence. It manipulated only the plant and used one pond per condition. We found no independently replicated experiment that manipulated both species and could estimate their interaction. Combined performance may depend on whether plant uptake keeps pace with sediment release. Near-bottom oxygen levels and the fate of resuspended particles may also matter. We propose three testable predictions, compare in-pond and separate configurations, and illustrate how to evaluate interaction and approximate additivity. Further validation should account for carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus within a common boundary and assess discharge peaks, harvest safety, seasonal stability, and operating costs.
