10.1186/s12711-026-01094-1: Abstract Background Pooled DNA genotyping has gained increasing attention in recent decades due to its potential to substantially reduce genotyping costs and its applications in identifying trait-associated DNA markers and estimating parental contributions to pooled offspring samples. However, accurately estimating parental contributions from pooled offspring genotype data remains a major challenge in selective breeding. This study presents a novel approach based on a differential evolution (DE) algorithm to estimate individual parental contributions to pooled offspring samples and assesses its accuracy across a wide range of simulated scenarios. Results Parental contributions were estimated with up to 100% accuracy by genotyping both in-silico pooled offspring and individual parents across various conditions, including different parental combinations (20 males × 20 females, 8 males × 8 females, and 5 males × 5 females), SNP densities (10-3981 markers), and pool sizes (2-1000 individuals), with or without knowledge of parental sex. In a simulated progeny testing scenario involving five males and five females that produced six full-sib families with 200 offspring each, 1200 offspring were ranked by body weight and grouped into 10 in-silico pools based on fixed weight intervals. Parental contributions to each pool were accurately estimated, enabling reliable calculation of genetic merit, defined as the mean body weight of all offspring from each parent. Genetic merit estimates obtained from pooled genotyping showed a perfect correlation with those derived from individual genotyping, with a root mean squared error of 1.4 g relative to a mean offspring weight of 674 g. Only 10 in-silico pools were genotyped instead of 1200 individuals, substantially reducing genotyping effort. The method was implemented as an open-source R package, DNApooling , and validation using empirical genotyping data demonstrated reliable estimation of parental contributions and genetic merit under real-world conditions. Conclusions The method provides a robust, scalable, and cost-effective approach for estimating parental genetic merit through progeny testing, analysing mating patterns in mass-spawning species, and assessing genetic diversity within pooled samples. Its practical utility is particularly relevant to genetic evaluation in aquaculture breeding programs.
10.1007/s11160-026-10109-5: Abstract Fish ecologists and managers have an interest in estimating the efficacy of freshwater habitat restoration, comparing among restoration options and basins. This often boils down to the question: How many fish can this habitat support? The number of fish a habitat can support, termed capacity, has increasingly become the currency for comparing habitats, restoration options, management policies, and is the backbone of many life cycle models. Underlying this focus is the assumption that capacity is determined from a factor or factors that limit abundance, and that improving these factors will promote an increase in population abundance. Researchers have a number of methods to estimate capacity, each with different benefits and drawbacks that vary by situation. Broadly, these methods fall into five categories: habitat expansion -applying high percentile observed fish densities to estimates of habitat area or volume; stock-recruit -fitting statistical relationships to time series of paired adult and progeny abundance; quantile regression -fitting high percentile regressions to local estimates of fish abundance and habitat features; microhabitat-scale models -scaling up statistical microhabitat suitability or individual bioenergetic requirements to reach and population levels; and food web models -estimating the energy flow from the primary and secondary production in a stream environment up through food webs to fish. The appropriate method in each situation will be determined by the available data, what management questions are being evaluated, the urgency and cost of producing estimates, and the temporal and spatial scales of estimates required.
10.1111/fme.70133: ABSTRACT Estimates of outmigration timing of Atlantic salmon smolt ( Salmo salar ) have become crucial inputs for predictive models that quantify effects of anthropogenic impacts. Recent reviews indicate that choice of method may impact estimates of migration timing, demanding an evaluation of the various monitoring tools in tandem. Here, we compared the migration behavior of smolts tagged with PIT tags or acoustic telemetry tags with smolts monitored with river transects of underwater video systems in two rivers in western Norway for three consecutive migration seasons (2019-2021). Despite discrepancies in the quantiles of migration, the methods often observed many of the same local peaks in migration distributions. Choice of tagging location had the largest observed effect on the migration timing of tagged individuals, with smolts from upstream of lakes arriving to the fjord 13.4 days later on average. Smolt length and morphological smolt index had negligible effects on migration timing.
10.1111/jfb.70741: Abstract Two new species of the ‘ Mesonoemacheilus guentheri ’ group are described from the Western Ghats Hotspot, based on morphological and multi-locus molecular data (mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunit 1, cytochrome b and nuclear Recombination-Activating Gene 1 sequences). Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum , new species, from a headwater stream of the Periyar River, is distinguished by a unique colour pattern of three series of whitish blotches on a brown background, and 8-9 branched pectoral-fin rays. Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis , new species, from a headwater stream of the Pamba River, is distinguished by a unique colour pattern comprising midlateral series of regularly or irregularly set and shaped whitish blotches with a wide brown margin, and pointed, elongated nasal flap-bars. Mesonoemacheilus now comprises 11 species, all of which are endemic to the rivers draining the Western Ghats Biodiversity Hotspot.
10.3390/fishes11110680: This study compared biofloc technology (BFT) and recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) for juvenile Piaractus brachypomus and tested whether responses depended on commercial feed. Fish (174.71 ± 2.80 g) received feeds labeled 24% or 32% crude protein (CP) for 90 days in a 2 × 2 factorial (three tanks per treatment). Water quality, growth, and physiological responses were analyzed by tank. Final weight (444.96 ± 37.37 vs. 444.19 ± 50.07 g, p = 0.9758) and survival (95.55% vs. 91.11%, p = 0.4082) did not differ between BFT and RAS. During days 45-90, fish fed 24% CP feed had greater weight gain (126.06 vs. 91.96 g, p = 0.0385) and specific growth rate (0.69 vs. 0.54% day-1, p = 0.0496). Higher apparent feed intake with 24% CP feed (3.86 vs. 2.14 g fish-1 day-1) may have contributed to this gain. Hepatic thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS, nmol g-1 tissue) were higher in BFT than RAS (5.80 ± 1.27 vs. 3.39 ± 0.82, p = 0.0010) and with 32% CP feed (5.23 ± 1.84 vs. 3.96 ± 1.18, p = 0.0295). Both systems supported juvenile grow-out. Among the feeds tested, the 24% CP product combined greater growth with lower hepatic TBARS.
10.3390/fishes11110681: The present study optimized and evaluated a lower-cost SYBR Green qPCR assay for White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV) detection and applied it to wild Penaeus monodon and Penaeus indicus from coastal Mozambique. Primer sets targeting VP19, VP24, VP26, and VP28 were compared with VP24_I showing favourable analytical performance (efficiency, 95.0%; R2 = 0.9988), good inter-run precision, no detectable cross-amplification with Infectious Hypodermal and Hematopoietic Necrosis Virus (IHHNV) or Decapod Iridescent Virus 1 (DIV1), and sequence confirmation of WSSV amplicons. Its dilution endpoint was comparable to that of the commercial MAXDETECT qPCR kit under the conditions tested, while reagent costs were reduced by 85% (USD 1.88 versus USD 12.55 per reaction). The assay was applied to 330 shrimp, and these individual-level results were combined with previously generated one-step PCR results from 300 shrimp from the same survey. After adjustment for geographic region, detection method, and site-level clustering, P. indicus had higher odds of WSSV detection than P. monodon, although this difference was not statistically significant (OR = 1.60; 95% CI: 0.86-2.98; p = 0.139). A similar trend was observed when the qPCR and one-step PCR datasets were analyzed separately. VP24_I represents a promising lower-cost candidate assay for WSSV surveillance, while the observed species association should be interpreted cautiously.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2020587: Nearly four billion people depend on coastal ecosystems, where the growing influence of wildfire remains an understudied threat to ecosystem health. Wildfires alter watershed hydrology, mobilizing sediments, nutrients, and contaminants that degrade coastal water quality and disrupt marine habitats long after fires are extinguished. Prior work documents wildfire effects on watershed hydrology and inland water quality, but few studies address what satellites can and cannot observe with respect to the wildfire-to-coast pathway. We identify these observational gaps, drawing on evidence from California, and present a first-order global screening of where they matter most. We argue satellite Earth observation, particularly a future constellation of complementary hyperspectral, multispectral, thermal, and radar sensors, offers a scalable way to bridge marine monitoring and capture wildfire’s cascading coastal effects. To show where this capacity is most needed, we present a simplified global vulnerability index highlighting regions where high fire danger overlaps with dense populations and critical marine resources. As wildfire risk grows, closing these monitoring gaps through transdisciplinary collaboration, integrating remote sensing, and in situ data will be essential to safeguarding coastal ecosystems.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2006926: With the rapid expansion of coastal nuclear and coal-fired power plants, the environmental impacts of thermal discharge on adjacent marine ecosystems have become a major concern in environmental science. Unlike previous reviews focusing on a single biological group or isolated water-quality parameter, this review integrates physicochemical and biological responses, microbial functional ecology and the microbial loop, identifies candidate indicator taxa and functional traits, compares nuclear and coal-fired effluents, and synthesizes effects on seawater physicochemical properties, plankton community structure, and microbial diversity and function. We distinguish two impact pathways, which are direct entrainment/impingement within once-through cooling systems and in situ warming experienced by organisms in the discharged plume. Chlorination by-products, nutrient enrichment and discharge-modified hydrodynamics are considered because they confound field-derived signals; thus many field patterns are mixed-stressor responses and cannot be attributed to warming alone. Nuclear and coal-fired plants differ in effluent composition, in that nuclear once-through discharges during normal operation are dominated by heated seawater and biocide residues. Many field-observed patterns represent mixed-stressor responses and cannot be attributed to warming alone. Thermal discharge reduces dissolved oxygen and pH, accelerates nutrient cycling, increases pollutant bioavailability, and alters phytoplankton, zooplankton, and microbial communities, thereby affecting food-web stability and biogeochemical processes. The review also discusses current controversies and knowledge gaps. The main contribution of this review is to integrate seawater chemistry, plankton dynamics and microbial functional ecology within a single attribution framework, to identify candidate indicator taxa and functional traits. This synthesis provides a scientific basis for environmental monitoring, ecological risk assessment and adaptive management of thermal discharge in coastal marine ecosystems.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1925773: Benthic imagery constitutes a primary data source for studying seafloor habitats, providing rich visual information essential for ecological assessment and marine ecosystem monitoring. Recent advances in underwater robotic platforms have substantially increased the capacity for large-scale benthic image acquisition, shifting the primary bottleneck from data collection to image annotation and analysis. However, manual annotation of benthic imagery remains labor-intensive, time-consuming, and dependent on domain expertise, limiting the scalability of marine habitat analysis. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted annotation tools have shown promise, their application to benthic imagery remains challenging due to the substantial domain gap between underwater imagery and conventional terrestrial computer vision datasets. In addition, annotated benthic datasets are often limited in size, geographically sparse, and highly imbalanced. Few-shot learning (FSL) offers a promising solution by enabling rapid adaptation to new datasets using only a small number of labeled examples. In this work, we propose a foundation-model-based few-shot classification (FSC) framework for benthic imagery annotation. The proposed framework uses pretrained visual representations and systematically investigates the influence of backbone family, model scale, support-set construction strategy, and adaptation algorithm under limited labeled-data conditions. Furthermore, we investigate a prioritized support-set construction strategy based on embedding-space clustering to improve annotation efficiency in low-shot regimes. Experimental results across three benthic imagery datasets demonstrate that DINOv3 ViT-S/16 provides the strongest overall classification performance among the evaluated backbone families, while increasing backbone size does not consistently improve accuracy. LinearSVC also demonstrates strong and consistent adaptation performance across the datasets. In addition, the proposed prioritized labeling strategy improves classification accuracy compared with class-balanced random sampling on Datasets B and C, with average gains of 7.62 and 5.02 percentage points, respectively, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals excluding zero, while the improvement on Dataset A is inconclusive. However, these accuracy gains do not consistently translate into higher macro-averaged F1 scores, highlighting the dataset-dependent effects of representative sample selection. Beyond classification performance, this work introduces an annotation-time modeling framework to analyze the practical deployment trade-offs of few-shot benthic annotation workflows. Under the evaluated annotation-time assumptions, FSC is estimated to reduce overall annotation time by 6.7% and 21.7% on Datasets A and B, respectively, compared with traditional fine-tuning approaches. On Dataset C, traditional fine-tuning shows only a small and uncertain estimated advantage of 1.3%. Overall, the results suggest that DINOv3-based few-shot classification provides an effective low-label annotation-support approach, with potential annotation-time advantages that depend on dataset size, classification accuracy, and annotation costs.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1907711: Calcifying macroalgae play critical roles in coral reef ecosystem functioning and carbonate dynamics. However, the metabolic responses underpinning several of their ecological functions remain poorly characterized, particularly in the Red Sea. To evaluate how macroalgal metabolism varies over time under naturally fluctuating conditions, we conducted in situ metabolic assays in the spring and fall over three years (2022-2024) using two ecologically important calcifying reef taxa: the green macroalga Halimeda opuntia and the crustose coralline alga Lithophyllum sp. We quantified rates of light and dark calcification, net photosynthesis, and respiration under natural light and temperature regimes in shallow nearshore habitats of the central Red Sea. Halimeda opuntia metabolism varied significantly across time points in both lagoonal and reef habitats, whereas Lithophyllum sp. showed more stable light calcification rates, though its dark calcification, respiration, and net photosynthesis varied. This variation did not follow a consistent seasonal pattern. Notably, light calcification rates in H. opuntia were more than twice those of Lithophyllum sp., consistent with their roles as fast-growing sediment producers versus slower-growing reef framework stabilizers, respectively. These results provide essential species-resolved in situ metabolic baselines for dominant calcifying macroalgae in the central Red Sea and highlight how divergent macroalgal functional groups contribute to carbonate production and reef stability in a region that regularly experiences environmental extremes.
10.1002/jat.70513: ABSTRACT Incomplete combustion of plastic waste is an emerging pathway for forming thermally transformed microplastics (MPs), whose physicochemical identity and ecotoxicological potential in aquatic vertebrates remain poorly understood, as available evidence has focused primarily on the toxicity of their leachates and extracts. Accordingly, we conducted an exploratory investigation of biochemical and behavioral profiles in juvenile Astyanax sp. exposed to MPs derived from the burning of expanded polystyrene (B-EPSMPs) and polyethylene terephthalate (B-PETMPs), integrating physicochemical characterization, behavioral responses, and biochemical biomarkers. Fish were allocated to Control, B-EPSMP, and B-PETMP groups, with 20 individuals maintained in one exposure aquarium per group for 10 days at a nominal B-MP concentration of 4 mg/L. Although the materials exhibited high morphometric similarity, Raman and UV-Vis analyses revealed distinct structural and spectroscopic profiles in the combustion-derived materials. No mortality was observed, but the exposed groups exhibited distinct sublethal response profiles. In the gastrointestinal tract, fish from both B-MP groups showed higher ROS and MDA levels and higher CAT and MPO-like activities relative to the Control group. Encephalic biochemical differences were more pronounced in the B-EPSMP group, including higher nitrite and dopamine levels, enhanced AChE activity, and lower BChE activity. Basal locomotor behavior remained largely preserved, whereas behavioral paradigms involving novelty and social interaction revealed differences among the observed groups. Fish from the B-EPSMP group exhibited greater locomotor reactivity to novelty and reduced interspecific social responsiveness toward Hyphessobrycon eques , whereas fish from the B-PETMP group mainly showed differences in novel-object exploration. Multiblock integration identified distinct biochemical-behavioral patterns among the sampled groups, with greater separation associated with the B-EPSMP group. Because each treatment was represented by a single exposure aquarium, these findings describe exploratory, tank-confounded associations rather than independently replicated treatment effects. Overall, the study provides preliminary evidence of distinct biological response patterns in fish exposed to fire-derived MPs and establishes a basis for future investigations using independently replicated exposure units.
10.1111/jfb.70742: Abstract Seasonal variation in fish parasite burden reflects the interplay between parasite transmission, environmental conditions and host characteristics, yet the relative contributions of these factors remain incompletely understood in many wild freshwater fishes. We investigated gill ectoparasitism in the Maghrebian Bleak ( Tropidophoxinellus callensis ), a freshwater fish endemic to Algeria and Tunisia, examining variation in parasite burden in relation to season, host age, physiological condition and dietary breadth. Three ectoparasite taxa were identified, Gyrodactylus barbi , Trichodina sp. and Dactylogyrus fraternus , providing the first characterisation of the gill ectoparasite assemblage of this species. Parasite burden peaked in summer, and season remained significantly associated with ectoparasitism after accounting for host characteristics, although much of the explained variation was shared among predictors. Parasite abundance increased with host age in unadjusted analyses, but the relationship reversed after accounting for hepatic condition and other predictors. Furthermore, parasite burden exhibited a nonlinear relationship with hepatic condition, reaching its highest values at intermediate hepatosomatic indices. These findings demonstrate that seasonal variation in ectoparasitism is closely intertwined with host ontogeny and physiological condition, highlighting the importance of considering intrinsic and extrinsic factors jointly when investigating host-parasite relationships.
10.18475/cjos.v56i2.a16: Queen conch (Aliger gigas) are gastropod mollusks whose fishery is economically, culturally, and ecologically significant to the Caribbean region. Their populations have been in decline since the 1960s due to many stressors acting at numerous spatial and temporal scales. In Belize, this decline persists despite national and international conservation measures, including habitat conservation and fishery regulations. This study examines how the Belizean queen conch fishery has affected conch population health and conservation in two marine reserves between 2018 and 2022. Conch population surveys were conducted in the Conservation and General Use Zones of the Sapodilla Cayes Marine Reserve (SCMR) and the South Water Caye Marine Reserve (SWCMR) in 2018, 2019, and 2022. Demographic metrics related to the fishery and reproductive maturity were measured, including siphonal length, shell lip thickness, legal harvest status, and illegal poaching. Results show strong evidence of conch poaching. 1,098 conch were surveyed in 2018, 2019, and 2022. Of the total conch surveyed, 604 (55.01%) were alive at the time of survey, 149 (13.57%) had been legally harvested in compliance with Belize's fishery regulations, and 324 (29.51%) had been poached. However, poaching levels differed between marine reserves. In the SWCMR, 287 (51.99%) of the surveyed conch had been poached, and 37 (6.78%) of the conch surveyed in the SCMR had been poached. Sustained poaching activity at these levels, especially in the SWCMR, will have negative long-term effects on conch survival and population recruitment. These trends should urge managers, researchers, and community leaders to explore local causes, effects, and attitudes around the conch fishery and conch conservation.
10.3390/aquacj6040059: Reliable fish feeding assessment is essential for intelligent aquaculture, yet classification accuracy alone does not establish operational reliability. This structured critical review examines multimodal deep learning approaches, including selected unimodal deployment comparators, through five appraisal dimensions: label validity, data independence and adaptation, robustness to degraded or unavailable sensing, predictive reliability and calibration, and deployment and feeding-management evidence. A key concern is feature-label coupling, where motion-derived labels and model inputs share optical-flow representations, potentially limiting the biological interpretation of classification performance. Reviewed studies demonstrate advances in multimodal fusion, corruption testing, missing-modality handling, knowledge distillation, domain adaptation, and computational efficiency. However, inconsistent dataset provenance, evaluation protocols, and measurement boundaries constrain cross-study comparisons and generalization claims. Uncertainty-informed training does not establish calibrated inference-time confidence, while embedded inference benchmarks may exclude preprocessing and other operational costs. Research priorities include acquisition-independent evaluation, robustness testing under sensing failures and distribution shifts, confidence calibration, selective prediction, and end-to-end deployment assessment. Prospective feeding trials with predefined control policies and independently measured production outcomes are needed to establish operational benefits. By distinguishing demonstrated capabilities from insufficiently verified claims, this review provides an evidence-oriented foundation for developing dependable fish feeding-assessment systems.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2037603: Coastal and marine engineering plays a critical role in the blue economy. However, such projects can exert cumulative and long-term pressures on marine ecosystems that cannot be adequately addressed through pollution control regulations. This study examines how China’s Ecological and Environmental Code, which entered into force on 15 August 2026, establishes a systematic legal framework for the ecological governance of coastal and marine engineering. Through a comparative analysis of successive legislative provisions and an examination of regulatory requirements throughout the project life cycle, this study identifies three major developments: (1) a shift from pollution control towards ecological priority and ecosystem protection; (2) a shift from project approval towards life-cycle governance; and (3) a shift from fragmented liability rules towards a more coherent framework for liability allocation and ecological restoration. The analysis demonstrates that the Code’s principal contributions lie in the systematic integration of existing legal institutions and the development of a more coherent framework for legal interpretation. Its practical effectiveness, however, depends on the lawful exercise of regulatory powers by competent authorities, the implementation of supporting regulations, and effective coordination with other sector-specific legislation.
10.1007/s42452-026-09653-3: Abstract Marine macroalgae are increasingly investigated as sources of food ingredients, hydrocolloids, biomaterials, bioactive compounds, animal-feed additives, biostimulants, and other applied products. Although global bibliometric studies have provided overviews of macroalgal research, an integrated bibliometric and text-mining synthesis comparing applied research across genera selected for their relevance to aquaculture planning in Costa Rica remains lacking. We analyzed 2,996 Scopus-indexed articles published from 2000 to April 2024 on 16 genera relevant to Costa Rican aquaculture. The analysis combined manual screening, supervised AI-assisted classification, and bibliometric mapping of publication trends, industrial sectors, countries, journals, institutions, authors, and keywords. Publication output increased after 2010 and accelerated from 2018 to 2023, especially in the health, agri-livestock, food, manufacturing, and biotechnology sectors. Sargassum , Ulva , and Gracilaria had the largest publication volumes, while India, China, and South Korea accounted for approximately 30% of the records. Keyword networks centered on antioxidant and antimicrobial activity, polysaccharides, extraction, nanoparticles, methane mitigation, and biomaterials, indicating that much of the literature remains focused on exploratory biochemical characterization and in vitro bioactivity studies. These patterns provide evidence-based insights for preliminary research prioritization. Sargassum , Ulva , Gracilaria , and Asparagopsis appear to be promising candidates for further evaluation, followed by Padina , Codium , Cladophora , Gracilariopsis , and Hypnea . However, bibliometric evidence alone cannot determine their suitability for aquaculture development and specific applications. Their potential use in Costa Rica should be evaluated through local cultivation trials, strain selection, seasonal biochemical profiling, contaminant screening, supply-chain assessment, regulatory evaluation, and techno-economic feasibility.
10.3390/fishes11110675: Aquaculture supplied 53% of global aquatic animal production in 2024, while 37.6% of assessed marine stocks remained outside biologically sustainable levels. The growth of aquaculture has not been matched by an equivalent development of the criteria that should guide it. This narrative review with framework synthesis examines that gap for European aquaculture, with capture fisheries considered only as context. Policy documents, technical standards, and the peer-reviewed literature were analysed around four axes: the science anticipation approach of the Geneva Science and Diplomacy Anticipator (GESDA), with its 5-, 10- and 25-year horizons; the EU Taxonomy for Sustainable Activities; circular side-stream valorisation and workforce training; and operational welfare indicators supported by precision aquaculture. The review finds that no technical screening criteria for aquaculture have yet been adopted under the Taxonomy, although the sector remains subject to EU environmental, animal health and welfare legislation; that circularity and welfare are rarely measured in ways that demonstrate environmental outcomes; and that the move offshore raises structural design questions for which aquaculture-specific evidence is still limited. A conceptual and illustrative horizon matrix is proposed, built with explicit allocation criteria and decision rules, that links technology clusters to Taxonomy objectives, candidate indicators and governance challenges. The matrix reflects the authors’ interpretation of the literature and has not been empirically validated; an implementation and validation pathway, including structured expert consultation, is outlined to test it.
10.1007/s44307-026-00145-4: Abstract The growing recognition of base editing as a precise genome-engineering strategy for single-nucleotide conversions without double-strand breaks has increased interest in its application to animal agriculture, where many economically important traits are influenced by single nucleotide variants. Although recent engineering efforts have broadened the targeting scope, improved editing precision, and reduced off-target activity, major challenges remain in translating these tools to livestock and aquaculture species, particularly with respect to delivery, mosaicism, germline transmission, and breeding-scale deployment. In this review, we outline the development of cytosine, adenine, dual, and mitochondrial base editors, and discuss their advances in livestock and fish, including trait-oriented editing in pigs and cattle, rapid functional validation in model fish, and early proof-of-concept studies in aquaculture species. We further discuss the emerging potential of mitochondrial DNA base editing for animal breeding and evaluate the extent to which current advances support the broader goal of precision breeding and sustainable animal production.
10.3390/aichem1040020: This narrative review examines where artificial intelligence (AI) improves aquaculture environmental monitoring relative to conventional methods, how validation designs shape the interpretation of reported gains, and what evidence is needed for routine farm use. A thematic synthesis, supplemented by a targeted OpenAlex literature update, compares baselines, validation designs, and measured outcomes across water-quality monitoring, harmful algal bloom surveillance, contaminant sensing, and environmental management. In a flow-through farm, a neural time-series model improved imputation of influent dissolved oxygen (DO), while linear interpolation performed best for tank DO. In a separate six-pond evaluation within one farm, physics-guided transfer learning reduced the mean absolute error of nighttime DO forecasts by 35.5% relative to a standard long short-term memory model. In a 45-day pilot in one koi pond, integrated predictive control used 26.86% less energy than manual operation. These findings support task-specific use of AI for monitoring and decision support. Broader deployment of automated control requires independent farm validation and prospective assessment of water quality and resource use.
10.3390/fishes11110678: Accurate extraction of coastal aquaculture facilities from remote sensing imagery remains challenging because these facilities exhibit irregular spatial distributions, substantial scale variations, and weak contrast against complex marine backgrounds, often with indistinct boundaries. To address these challenges, this study proposes FCS-UNet, an enhanced U-Net framework incorporating three components: Dual Hybrid Attention (DHA), Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention Module (MSCAM), and Progressive Stacked Feature Refinement (PSFR). The contribution of this study is the integration of adapted attention and multi-scale modules with a bottleneck block of stacked depthwise-separable convolutions, evaluated by facility type on a new dataset. Experimental results show that FCS-UNet achieves an Accuracy of 93.64 ± 0.42%, a Dice coefficient of 95.25 ± 0.24%, and an IoU of 91.01 ± 0.47%, improving the U-Net baseline by 3.68, 2.75, and 5.02 percentage points, respectively. Dongwuyang experiments and ablation studies further evaluate the model’s performance. Furthermore, facility-type-stratified evaluations demonstrate that FCS-UNet achieves the highest Dice and IoU for both raft and cage facilities in both study areas. Under a random image-level split within a single coastal region, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of FCS-UNet for coastal aquaculture facility extraction.
10.1093/najfmt/vqag096: Abstract Objective Chum Salmon Oncorhynchus keta migrate annually to spawn in the Yukon River drainage at sites within both the United States and Canada, providing a rich subsistence and commercial fishing culture for communities along the river. Yukon River Chum Salmon runs have been roughly cyclical, though overall they have declined over the past 47 years. Beginning in 2020, abrupt declines in their populations resulted in complete fisheries closures and hardship for the remote villages that rely on them. We present a review of the known extent of Chum Salmon spawning habitat in the Yukon River drainage to facilitate research and management discussions as we rebuild the fisheries and the runs that sustain them. Methods Following extensive review of peer-reviewed journals, reports, and gray literature spanning roughly 160 years, spawning sites were differentiated as either summer or fall stocks and were classified as major or minor spawning systems based on maximum escapement estimates or, if unavailable, maximum relative abundance estimates. To place these data in context, we explored trends in reconstructed runs, escapement, and relative abundance and included descriptions of known threats to the long-term viability of production in relevant tributaries within the overall Yukon River drainage. Threats to spawning systems were collated. Results A total of 192 systems in the study area were identified to have Chum Salmon spawning via review of available peer-reviewed manuscripts, reports, and unpublished study findings, of which eight were major spawning areas for summer stock and seven were major areas for fall stock. Abundance estimates were located for the 1950s through 2024, and early discourse related to Chum Salmon, principally from non-Native expeditions or later discussion with Native elders, was located back to 1866. A dendrogram for Chum Salmon populations was updated through 2024 based on the 48 systems with genetic samples, and gaps in our understanding of Yukon River Chum Salmon genetic composition were described. Although all populations of Chum Salmon in the Yukon River are depressed, the Canadian component, especially from the White River drainage, has diminished considerably more compared with the others. Conclusions Habitat degradation issues in freshwater are generally regional and do not appear substantial enough to cause the recent, widespread, and temporally acute decline of Chum Salmon throughout the drainage. However, the combination of regional issues alongside broader factors such as climate change may lead to a prolonged recovery, and an understanding of regional freshwater stressors is important.
10.3389/fmicb.2026.1939609: Background Host-associated microbiota play a central role in maintaining physiological homeostasis and regulating host immune responses. In aquatic organisms, this relationship is particularly dynamic due to continuous exposure to the surrounding environment. While acute viral infections are known to induce dysbiosis, the effects of recurrent sublethal exposures, which better reflect conditions in aquaculture and natural environments, remain poorly understood. Methods Here, we investigated how recurrent exposure to viral particles shifts the whole-body microbiota of the freshwater zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) and the intestinal microbiota of the marine turbot ( Scophthalmus maximus ). Fish were subjected to recurrent exposure to sublethal doses of four RNA viruses belonging to three different viral families of aquaculture relevance: the rhabdoviruses spring viremia of carp virus (SVCV) or viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) in zebrafish and turbot, respectively, the birnavirus infectious pancreatic necrosis virus (IPNV), and the nodavirus red-spotted grouper nervous necrosis virus (RGNNV) in both species. Microbial communities were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and diversity, co-occurrence networks, and predicted functional profiles were analyzed. Results Our results demonstrate that recurrent sublethal viral exposure in fish induces microbiota alterations that combine both conserved and virus-specific alterations. In zebrafish, Ralstonia was consistently enriched across viral exposures, whereas in turbot, changes in bacterial taxa varied among virus-exposed groups. Nevertheless, some genera showed a shared pattern of enrichment, including Polaribacter 4 and Aestuariicella in both VHSV- and IPNV-exposed groups. In contrast, RGNNV-exposed groups exhibited the most pronounced dysbiosis, including the virus-specific near disappearance of Plesiomonas , the most abundant taxa in the zebrafish control group. Discussion This underscores the importance of host-virus interplay in shaping microbiota dynamics, accompanied by changes in predicted metabolic functions. Together, these results emphasize the need to consider microbiota dynamics in disease progression and support the potential of microbial indicators as tools for monitoring fish health.
10.1093/fshmag/vuag069: Abstract The American Fisheries Society’s (AFS’s) second edition of Standard Methods for Sampling North American Freshwater Fishes, which was published fall 2024, contains summaries of standard sampling comparison data that fisheries professionals can use to help diagnose problems in their fish populations. These summaries are based on a database containing records from almost 15,000 surveys of 52 fish species in 54 states and Canadian provinces sampled with the AFS standard gear types. Here, we demonstrate a webtool that allows users to upload data from an individual fish population collected using the standard methods reported in the book, and compare their data with existing North American, ecoregion, and within-state summaries of common fish assessment metrics from standard data collected in similar water body types. User input is simply fish species, water body type, standard gear type, and a data spreadsheet containing fish lengths, weights, and sampling effort from your survey. Output includes visualizations of CPUE, length frequency, and relative weight, and data tables that allow for rapid fishery diagnoses, similar to how short summaries of standard laboratory results from an individual compared to a larger population are important for physicians diagnosing health problems in human patients.
10.1371/journal.pone.0355126: The bocachico Prochilodus magdalenae, Colombia’s most ecologically and economically important native freshwater fish, has declined sharply under compounding anthropogenic pressures, yet whether climate anomalies compromise its gamete quality remains unexplored. This species shows two annual reproductive peaks (May-July and October-December), offering a natural model for comparing reproductive performance under contrasting climatic conditions. We assessed semen quality in captive males across both peaks, one coinciding with the influence of a strong El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) event (>90% probability) and the other with neutral conditions. Seminal pH, osmolality, volume, CASA-derived sperm kinematics, and total antioxidant capacity (TAC) of seminal plasma were analyzed alongside water temperature, precipitation, and ENSO status using Boruta selection, Random Forest/SHAP, and redundancy analysis. Semen quality differed significantly between peaks: the ENSO-neutral second peak showed higher TAC (312.4 ± 162.4 vs. 200.7 ± 25.0 µmol TE/100 g), total motility (97.8 ± 3.4% vs. 96.2 ± 4.4%), and sperm concentration (28,956.4 ± 2,238.1 × 10⁶ vs. 17,430.7 ± 1,849.6 × 10⁶ spz/mL) than the El Niño-affected first peak (p < 0.05). ENSO occurrence and water temperature emerged as the strongest predictors of TAC across Boruta and Random Forest/SHAP analyses, ranking above pH and sperm kinematics, and a composite Integrated Composite Conservation Score built from the five most discriminant seminal traits was likewise significantly lower under El Niño (0.440 vs. 0.495, p < 0.001). Seminal TAC declined significantly with increasing water temperature (β = -33.5, p < 0.001), falling below values recorded at the El Niño-associated critical threshold (30.4°C), projecting this relationship onto IPCC AR6 regional warming scenarios for Colombia forecasts a 32-41% decline in TAC by 2050. These findings show that ENSO-driven anomalies substantially compromise seminal quality in P. magdalenae , expose its antioxidant system as a key vulnerability under future warming, and underscore the need for environmental monitoring in conservation and breeding programs for this and other Neotropical Characiformes.
10.1007/s11160-026-10093-w: Abstract Studies of animal color patterns have provided important insights into evolution, particularly the genetic and developmental bases of adaptation, natural selection’s role in molding both nuptial and nonbreeding traits, and sexual/social selection’s role in ornament evolution. Here we review these topics for the threespine stickleback, a leading evolutionary model. Concerning genetics, we find that melanic characters are the best elucidated, with one to multiple genes indicated. Red coloration appears polygenic and candidate genes include ttc39b, but manipulations using CRISPR-Cas9 are needed. When red is present in females as well as males, shared QTL are involved, but red-correlated gene expression can also be sex-specific. Plasticity is important for both conspicuous and cryptic color patches, with light environment critical. Regarding selection, lateral barring appears adaptive against predation, but opportunities for experimental evolution studies need to be pursued-also for nuptial color. For males, red intensity is often correlated with condition, aggression and dominance, as well as successful offspring rearing, but contrary results have also been obtained. Further, there is no direct evidence that benefits resulting from choice of mate drive preference evolution. Sensory drive, however, is increasingly supported. Genetic correlations, for example between the expression and perception of color, may be important yet their underpinnings are largely unknown. Comparative data from related species bolster observations of threespine stickleback social behavior which suggest, first, that spine color merits additional research attention; and second, that a comparative approach based in current sensory ecology methods and considering multiple color patches is likely to provide valuable insights.
10.3391/ai.2026.21.4.218006: Invasions by nonnative species pose a major threat to freshwater ecosystem function and integrity. Freshwater springs, particularly those in Florida, are threatened by loss of water quantity, degradation of water quality, and invasions of nonnative species, the last of which exacerbate the other problems. Most studies quantify the abundance of nonnative species by numbers of individuals, but the average size of species also is important as large species may have greater impacts on systems than small species. Therefore, we evaluated the biomass of native and nonnative fish and snails in a first magnitude spring in Florida. We used seine, snorkel, and video surveys to sample fish and random substrate quadrat samples to sample snails. We measured individuals of all species and calculated biomasses from weights estimated from length measurements. For both fish and snails, the native species outnumbered the nonnative species. Small poeciliids and killifish were the most numerous fish, whereas tiny hydrobiid snails were the most numerous snails. In contrast, most of the nonnative fish and snails were as large or larger than the largest native fish and snails, producing aggregate biomasses of nonnative species that were roughly equivalent to those for fish and snails. Given the greater impact of large-bodied organisms on ecosystem processes, these nonnative species likely have a much greater impact on this spring than their numbers would suggest.
10.3390/fishes11110677: Zona pellucida (ZP) proteins form the egg envelope, but the ZP gene repertoire of viviparous teleosts remains incompletely characterized. Here, we investigated ZP genes in black rockfish (Sebastes schlegelii), a species characterized by internal fertilization and prolonged ovarian sperm storage. We identified 22 ZP genes on 11 chromosomes, comprising three ZPAX1, seven ZP3, seven ZP4, and five ZP3-like genes. Phylogenetic analysis of 107 vertebrate proteins recovered the major ZP1/4, ZP2, ZP3, and ZPAX-related groups. ZP4.1-ZP4.7 fell within the broad ZP1/4 clade, ZPAX1.1 and ZPAX1.2 grouped with teleost ZPAX proteins, and ZPAX1.3 was placed near the ZPAX/ZPY clade. The ZP3 and ZP3-like proteins were distributed across the ZP3-related clade. The candidates shared ZP-domain sequences but differed in exon organization and accessory domains. Expression analysis of eight selected genes revealed stage-dependent differences in ovarian transcript abundance. Across the ovarian developmental stages FM-1 to FM-5, ZP4.5 expression increased from FM-1 to FM-3, decreased at FM-4, and remained relatively high at FM-5. In situ hybridization signals were strongest in FY and FM-3. Predicted protein associations represent candidate functional links that require experimental validation. These findings characterize the ZP gene repertoire of black rockfish and identify candidates for further functional analysis.
10.3390/fishes11110676: This study evaluated how daily feeding regimens and photothermal induction duration modify reproductive performance in pikeperch (Sander lucioperca) during out-of-season reproduction. Broodstock were evaluated over two consecutive cycles differing in chilling duration: 2021-SHORT (1-week chilling, nine pairs of breeders per group) and 2022-LONG (5-week chilling, 15 breeders per group), making duration collinear with experimental year and breeder age under either ad libitum (0.5% biomass/day) or Restrictus (0.4% biomass/day) feeding. The feeding regimen affected female latency time, oil globule fragmentation, embryo survival, and larval malformations-which more than doubled under ad libitum conditions-but did not affect sperm quality. Induction duration affected gametes in a contrasting manner: longer chilling impaired egg quality but enhanced sperm quality. While non-significant interaction testing (p = 0.075) warrants cautious interpretation of embryo survival slopes under ad libitum feeding, observed variations highlight the need for future studies investigating whether individual differences in feed intake or coping styles influence reproductive sensitivity. Our preliminary observations suggest that inducing females with oocyte diameters exceeding 1000 µm may be associated with reduced egg quality, though formal threshold validation is required; meanwhile, avoiding ad libitum feeding during the cooling period can be recommended. The divergent responses of male and female gamete quality to chilling duration highlight the need for studies investigating gamete quality in out-of-season reproduction without a chilling phase.
10.3390/fishes11110674: Climate-driven ocean warming is altering the distribution of many marine species, but records at higher latitudes do not necessarily demonstrate a directional shift in the population core. This study evaluates the spatial dynamics of the carangid fish Seriola rivoliana in the Mediterranean Sea and European Atlantic. Morphometric, meristic, and molecular characteristics of new specimens captured in the Strait of Sicily are also described. Using an occurrence dataset from 1984 to 2025, GIS-based spatial statistics (Mean Center, Standard Distance, and Standard Deviational Ellipse) were calculated across four temporal intervals to assess range expansion and latitudinal shifts. Results reveal an increase in the geographical spread of documented occurrences in the Mediterranean. In the European Atlantic, records were documented at progressively higher latitudes over the study period, while the geographical centroid of reported occurrences did not show a consistent northward displacement. Potential impacts of the species in the Mediterranean are discussed. Overall, the observed patterns are more consistent with geographical range expansion than with a consistent directional displacement of the occurrence-record centroid. The integrated GIS approach proves to be a valuable tool for describing and comparing changes in the spatial distribution of reported occurrences over time.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1914036: Understanding marine species distribution and habitat use contributes to the development of effective population conservation and management. Biologging, particularly accelerometry, provides valuable insights on individual movement and behaviour. Technical constraints such as the need for tag recovery limit long-term studies of free-ranging fish over large spatial scales, hindering detailed examination of movements over seasonal or annual migrations. Pop-up Satellite Archival Tags (PSATs) equipped with triaxial accelerometers offer a promising avenue for large flatfishes such as Atlantic halibut ( Hippoglossus hippoglossus ) by providing a recoverable platform to aid the collection of year-long accelerometry data. Accurate interpretation of acceleration data from these externally-attached free-floating tags requires accounting for possible confounding effects between swimming speed and factors related to the nature of the attachment. This study aims to evaluate whether PSAT-derived accelerometer tilt values can be used to estimate horizontal swimming speed in free-ranging Atlantic halibut while accounting for the influence of water currents, vertical movements, and tag attachment. Flume tank experiments showed that an asymptotic model accurately described the relationship between tilt and flow rate, with minor effects of attachment design except under low-flow conditions. Analysis of 39 tagged halibut and two stationary moored PSATs in the Gulf of St. Lawrence (Canada) revealed that ambient water currents induce tilt, with current-induced tag movement confounding swimming speeds below a threshold of about 0.25 (0.15-0.39) m s -1 . Because of the non-linear relationship between tilt and speed and unknown current orientation, fine-scale correction was not possible. Vertical movements also influenced tilt values but were infrequent and can generally be accounted for. First-order mean horizontal swimming speed during active behaviour was estimated at 0.66 (0.62-0.79) m s -1 . However, swimming speed estimates are constrained by hydrodynamic effects inherent to external, single tether attachment designs. Further developments on water current effects are needed to refine tilt-based swimming speed estimates. This study establishes a framework for the interpretation of PSAT accelerometry data in Atlantic halibut and offers prospects for improving the mechanistic understanding of spatial distribution and behaviour in an underrepresented fish in accelerometry studies.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1952449: Shoreline management in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) is largely informed by small-scale studies with coarse temporal resolution, potentially obscuring fine spatial patterns and interannual dynamics. This study examines spatiotemporal shoreline change along 400 km of the Kenyan coastline from 2000 to 2024 and tests its association with regional sea-level trend and variability, accounting for spatial dependence. Twenty-five annual Landsat-derived shoreline positions were analyzed using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) along 12,455 transects using Weighted Linear Regression (WLR) weighted by a tide- and registration-based positional uncertainty of approximately 40 to 68 m per epoch. Results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity. The Kilifi and Kwale-Mombasa zones show net accretion (mean WLR 0.57 and 0.51 m yr -1 , respectively), whereas the Tana-Manda zone shows net erosion (mean WLR = -0.92 m yr -1 ), with 36.23% of its transects significantly eroding. Shoreline change is strongly spatially autocorrelated (Moran’s I = 0.866, p = 0.001) and 12.01% of transects form statistically significant local clusters (6.23% as High-High accretion and 5.57% Low-Low erosion clusters). Neither sea-level trend nor sea-level variability showed a detectable association with shoreline change at the native support of the predictors (OLS R 2 ≤ 0.028, p ≥ 0.26; SLM not significant; GWR adjusted R 2 < 0). 10.3389/fmars.2026.1976573: Offshore habitats of the world’s oceans are increasingly being altered by human activities, particularly where energy extraction and production require infrastructure. These structures provide artificial habitats that marine life grows on and attracts mobile fauna. We surveyed chondrichthyan fauna on oil and gas infrastructure and in natural habitats of the Gippsland Basin, south-east Australia over four years for a pre-decommissioning campaign. We used a combination of remote underwater video (ROV), baited remote underwater video (BRUV), and environmental DNA metabarcoding (eDNA). These methods combined yielded 39 taxa from 19 families, ~30% that were endemic to Australia, including six species with conservation listings. Despite a greater number of taxa being observed on pipelines using ROV, mean richness was highest at a nearby reef, and there was no difference in mean richness estimates from BRUVs between pipeline and natural reference sites. Benthic species, such as the Port Jackson shark ( Heterodontus portusjacksoni ) and the draughtboard shark ( Cephaloscyllium laticeps ) were abundant at the base of platforms and along pipelines (including their egg casings) on ROV surveys, whereas stingarees from the Urolophus genus were common in soft sediment natural habitats and the benthic surrounds. Observations of conservation listed species from ROV included the white shark ( Carcharodon carcharias ; IUCN status Vulnerable) in the benthic surrounds of platforms, the Australian longnose skate ( Dentiraja confusa IUCN status Critically Endangered) in natural habitats and on platforms, and the Greenback stingray ( Urolophus viridis IUCN status Vulnerable) in benthic surrounds. Several juvenile and newborn sharks were also observed on BRUVs, providing support for a potential nearshore nursery. A comparison of methods indicated that ROV and eDNA metabarcoding may be less suitable for highly mobile and rare species, whereas BRUVs appear more appropriate. These findings demonstrate the value of a multi-method approach for assessing chondrichthyan communities associated with offshore infrastructure and may help inform decommissioning and offshore renewable energy developments.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1966604: Introduction Daily grid-scale forecasts of catch occurrence are increasingly used for operational planning and to track species redistribution under climate change, yet what sets their predictability limit is rarely quantified. Methods We assembled 6 years (2020-2025) of daily Japanese flying squid ( Todarodes pacificus ) catch, vessel-activity, and ocean-reanalysis records for Korean waters: 20.35 million grid-days on a 0.05° grid, over 99% zero-catch. Results The 2025 holdout is a genuine distribution shift rather than a modeling artifact: 32 of 33 covariates stayed below the 0.25 major-shift threshold of the population stability index while catch per vessel fell 11.9-fold inside the fixed optimal-temperature habitat. On that holdout, daily occurrence forecasting is bounded by persistence, the trivial forecast that repeats the previous day's map (one-day-ahead 8-Neighbor F1 0.506) and so encodes only the inertia of yesterday's fishing. Three improvements (a Focal-Tversky loss, a ConvLSTM-Transformer hybrid, and a validation-weighted ensemble) reached 0.347 (five-seed mean), and two designs embedding persistence scored 0.486 (five-seed mean) and 0.502 (one seed); none exceeded persistence detectably, so the bound is not an artifact of insufficient tuning. The constraint is inherited from the record rather than from model capacity: national fishery statistics measure effort as the presence of all operating vessels rather than squid-directed ones, so only 1.81% of effort-positive grid-days carry a squid catch. The vessel-presence field persists almost deterministically where the catch field does not (8-Neighbor F1 0.923 versus 0.506), and a catch in the neighboring cells on the previous day raises the probability of a catch 14.4-fold while the environmental windows used in the feature design raise it not at all. Intensity, unlike occurrence, proved only weakly determined by the environment (best R² about 0.05, Tweedie and log-normal, on the densest cells), so the two components are modeled separately. Discussion Because that inertia reflects how the statistics are collected rather than how the models are built, the bound is expected to hold for fine-scale forecasts based on records of this kind. To our knowledge, this is the first quantification of such a ceiling for daily, grid-scale catch forecasting, and it identifies squid-directed effort records as the decisive next input.
10.1111/fog.70093: ABSTRACT Marine capture fisheries production (MCFP) is vulnerable to climate change, but the nonlinear relationship between climate and MCFP is not yet well understood across different national fisheries systems. Using annual data from China and Norway from 1961 to 2023, random forest (RF) models and partial-dependence plots are applied. Detrended production anomalies assess impact, recovery, and temporal variability. CO2 and surface air temperature (SAT) were the two leading predictors in both countries; in China, their ranks swapped across random seeds, while in Norway SAT consistently ranked first. At species level, CO2 and SAT were the leading predictors across the selected Chinese species and SAT across the selected Norwegian species, although relationship directions differed. China's upper-lower contrasts for CO2 and SAT are statistically supported in the primary analysis but approach zero following production-regime adjustment. Norway's upper-lower contrast confidence intervals include zero, and the estimated change points are imprecise in both countries. China has a positive mean event-year production shortfall, but its difference from other years is statistically uncertain. Recovery estimates depend on event definitions and regime adjustment. Norway's event estimates are generally uncertain, and its temporal-variability point estimate is higher in the main analysis, but the cross-country difference is statistically uncertain. Several findings are sensitive to detrending, fishing effort, and regime treatment. The results describe predictive associations rather than causal climate effects and support monitoring environmental conditions together with fishing pressure, catch composition, and long-term MCFP changes.
10.1111/raq.70230: ABSTRACT Iron is an essential cofactor for oxygen transport, electron transfer, DNA synthesis, and Fe-S cluster enzymes, with its redox cycling between Fe 2+ and Fe 3+ , underpinning both its biochemical utility and cytotoxic potential via ROS generation, requiring tight homeostatic regulation across all organisms. In contrast to terrestrial vertebrates, aquatic organisms acquire iron not only from dietary sources but also directly from the surrounding water through the gills. This dual acquisition pathway has driven unique regulatory adaptations of iron homeostasis, maintained through tightly coordinated mechanisms of absorption, transport, and storage. Disruption of these mechanisms, either by deficiency or overload, can impair growth, cause anemia, promote oxidative stress, and aggravate metabolic disorders. This review synthesizes current knowledge of iron uptake routes, systemic regulation, storage, and recycling in major aquaculture species. In addition, it provides an overview of dietary iron requirements, iron deficiency and overload, and the effects of feed composition, mineral sources, functional additives and environmental factors on iron bioavailability. Finally, the review discusses ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death associated with lipid peroxidation, and highlights critical knowledge gaps and research priorities for improving iron nutrition and metabolic health in aquaculture species.
10.1177/1973798x261507651: Background Deep-freezing (≤-18°C) is widely used to preserve fish and seafood and extend shelf-life limiting losses in nutritional quality. However, freezing conditions may influence ice crystal formation and cellular damage, affecting nutrient retention. Objectives To assess the impact of deep-freezing on the nutrient profile of the most commonly consumed fish and seafood in the Italian population, including Cod, Hake, Gilthead Seabream, Plaice, Salmon, Seabass, Octopus and Shrimp. Methods Studies evaluating changes in proteins, amino acids, lipids, fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals during deep-frozen storage, as well as differences in fresh vs deep-frozen fish were evaluated. Results Thirteen studies were included. Total protein content was largely preserved, although reductions in protein solubility and myofibrillar functionality were reported at higher temperatures or after prolonged storage. Total lipid content was generally stable, while fatty acid composition showed variable changes, with occasional decreases in polyunsaturated fatty acids over time. Vitamin retention was more heterogeneous, with water-soluble vitamins appearing more susceptible to degradation, than fat-soluble ones. No changes in mineral content were assessed. Conclusions Despite methodological heterogeneity, the evidence suggests that rapid deep-freezing and lower storage temperatures better preserve nutritional quality. Further standardized studies are needed to improve comparability across species and storage conditions.
10.18543/baidc.3525: This article analyses the roles of the social economy and taxation as drivers of a just ecological transition in the maritime and fisheries sector in the Basque Country. The paper examines the current state of the sector and its regulatory framework, from international guidelines to the powers granted by special legal provisions (norma/decreto foral) under the Basque Economic Agreement, paying particular attention to the social dimension. Finally, it identifies challenges and opportunities for fully integrating the social economy into the economic, social and environmental development of the territory, thus contributing to a sustainable ecological transition. 10.3389/fmars.2026.2018983: When trying to balance ecological protection with basic community livelihoods, coastal small-scale capture fisheries are facing serious governance challenges related to fairness, food security, and community resilience. Existing studies have focused on protecting rights, community participation, and the use of adaptive learning. However, further clarification is needed of how prioritizing basic needs, allocating responsibilities in light of participants’ differing circumstances, and reflecting on action can be ethically justified within a coherent framework. It is also necessary to show how these reasons can help participants understand and carry out their responsibilities. To address this ocean governance issue, this paper combines classical textual interpretation, conceptual analysis, and normative reasoning. It provides a modern explanation of “forming one body with all things,” “frugality,” and “self-cultivation through practice (shishang molian).” Through this, it builds a normative framework of relations, virtue, and practice to supplement the existing ethical arguments on co-management. The framework starts from concern for other people and marine ecosystems. It explains the ethical basis for limiting resource use, sharing conservation responsibilities, and reflecting on one’s own judgment. On this basis, it calls for respecting people’s right to participate, giving priority to basic needs within ecological limits, sharing responsibilities according to capacities, benefits, and the impacts of participants’ actions, and reviewing arrangements through joint learning. Based on this, the paper proposes four conditional propositions. These propositions concern the relationships between meaningful influence on decisions and perceived procedural fairness and governance trust; needs-based allocation and household food access; endorsement of restraint norms and compliance with fishing restrictions; and learning and feedback mechanisms and community resilience. Finally, the paper also suggests ways to test these propositions in future research. This paper links the ethical evaluation of co-management arrangements with how actors understand and carry out their responsibilities, providing an interconnected ethical basis for coastal fisheries governance. At the same time, the propositions still need empirical testing, and the choice of specific institutional arrangements and their application in different cultural contexts require further justification.
10.3389/fvets.2026.1929997: Introduction Fish enteritis is a major health challenge in aquaculture as low-fishmeal feeding strategies become more common. Soybean meal-induced enteritis (SBMIE) is a representative model of diet-induced intestinal inflammation, but evidence remains dispersed across species, feed ingredients, pathological endpoints, and mechanistic approaches. Methods We mapped fish enteritis research using 554 Web of Science Core Collection publications from 2010 to 2024 and analyzed publication trends, contributors, keyword evolution, and co-citation patterns with CiteSpace and VOSviewer. Scopus and PubMed were used for cross-database validation, yielding 475 eligible publications after screening and deduplication. Mechanistic evidence from the 2010-2024 corpus was narratively synthesized and updated with eligible SBMIE studies published through 30 June 2026. Results Research output increased markedly after 2018, with China, Norway, and the United States as major contributors and Aquaculture and Fish & Shellfish Immunology as leading journals. Keyword and co-citation analyses identified soybean meal, Atlantic salmon, distal intestine, gut microbiota, immune response, and lipid metabolism as central or emerging themes. Annual publication counts showed a strong positive correlation between the WOSCC and Scopus/PubMed datasets (Pearson’s r = 0.922, p < 0.001). Mechanistically, SBMIE can be organized into a layered framework involving soybean-derived triggers and epithelial barrier disruption, microbiota dysbiosis with innate immune amplification, and intestinal metabolic remodeling with possible gut-liver involvement. Barrier dysfunction and TLR/MAPK/NF-κB-related inflammatory activation are relatively well supported, whereas the causal roles of microbiota shifts, microbial metabolites, bile acids, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-AhR signaling, and AMPK/FOXO-related responses require further validation. Conclusion This review maps the fish-enteritis research landscape and synthesizes mechanistic evidence on SBMIE. The narrative synthesis provides a microbiota-immune-metabolic perspective on SBMIE, although causal links among these processes require further validation. Future work should use component-specific SBMIE models, time-course designs, causal microbiota-metabolite validation, and production-relevant feeding trials to support mechanism-guided soybean inclusion strategies in aquafeeds.
10.3390/jmse14222189: The specific habitat conditions in different parts of a species’ range may give rise to intraspecific polymorphism at various levels (morphological, biological, genetic, etc.), but this phenomenon has not been sufficiently studied. Here, the results of research on the morphological, biological, genetic, karyological, and parasitological characteristics of the gray rockfish Sebastes glaucus (Sebastidae, Scorpaeniformes) in two water bodies differing in habitat conditions are presented, i.e., a desalinated lagoon and adjacent sea areas off Zavyalov Island (the northern Sea of Okhotsk). Individuals in the two water bodies were found to differ significantly in terms of some morphological characteristics (the number of lateral line pores and the total number of vertebrae), size (the fish in the lagoon are smaller in length and body weight), maximum age and growth rates (individuals in the sea reach a greater age and grow faster), chromosome morphology and the number of chromosome arms, and the degree of infection with metacercariae of trematodes (100% in the lagoon and their complete absence in the sea). Furthermore, samples from the lagoon and the sea are reliably differentiated from each other based on genetic analysis using mtDNA markers. The identified differences may be due to a combination of factors, including both abiotic (higher temperature and lower salinity in the lagoon and its isolation from the sea) and biotic (limited forage resources and high parasite load in the isolated lagoon) factors.
10.1088/1402-4896/aec3dd: Abstract Macroscopic descriptions of collective motion require observables that retain information about future dynamics. We tested the predictive value of recent rotation beyond instantaneous group structure using three whirligig-beetle recordings for model development and 12 for evaluation, with nine golden-shiner recordings assessing transfer of fixed categorical settings. In beetles, adding rotation five frames earlier to current rotation, polarization, group radius and shape reduced mean-squared error by 13.73% and 13.20% at three- and ten-frame horizons. Estimating current rotation and its trend from six observations over the same interval further improved prediction in every recording at horizons of 3, 10 and 30 frames. In stochastic simulations, history reduced direction switching from 17.124 to 5.671 switches per minute, closer to the observed rate of 2.808, and improved waiting-time curves. Residual switching and correlation errors remained in smaller groups, and stationary distributions showed no consistent improvement. Time spent in the current rotational category accounted for 59.20% of the four-observation prediction-score gain, while longer contexts retained additional information. In fish, categorical history improved prediction under both body-heading and movement-based definitions of rotation; continuous gains depended on the definition. Short observation windows therefore provide effective coordinates for reduced prediction, with clearer benefits for switching dynamics than for stationary statistics.
10.3390/diagnostics16223848: Background/Objectives: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) has variable clinical expression and marked allelic heterogeneity. This study assessed the diagnostic yield of molecular testing in a regional Romanian cohort with an initial clinical diagnosis of NF1 and described the clinical features of patients with NF1 molecular findings. Methods: This retrospective study included 77 patients evaluated between 1990 and 2025. We reviewed the use and results of next-generation sequencing (NGS), multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). Results: Of the 77 patients, 42 (54.5%) underwent molecular testing. NGS was performed in 36 patients, MLPA in 15, and FISH in 7. NGS identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic NF1 sequence variants in 30 of 36 sequenced patients (83.3%), representing 30 of 42 tested patients (71.4%). In one additional patient with a negative NGS result, MLPA detected a suspected intragenic NF1 deletion that was not independently confirmed. Including this finding, the observed yield was 31/36 (86.1%) among sequenced patients and 31/42 (73.8%) among all tested patients. FISH detected no 17q11.2 microdeletions. One patient had an NF1 variant of uncertain significance. Each of the three recurrent NF1 variants was observed within a single family. A homozygous pathogenic MSH6 variant led to the reclassification of one patient as having constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (CMMRD). Conclusions: NGS identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic NF1 variant in 30 of the 36 sequenced patients. Because access to testing and the methods used varied across the cohort, this proportion applies to the sequenced subgroup. In one child initially diagnosed with NF1, molecular testing established a diagnosis of CMMRD.
10.65339/ijsis.v1.i4.303: This study assessed sanitation and hygiene practices, supply management, and operational challenges among fish vendors at Bongao Public Market, Tawi-Tawi, Philippines. Using a descriptive cross-sectional case study design, 50 vendors were selected through quota sampling. Data were gathered through structured questionnaires, supplemented by interviews and direct observations, and analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and weighted means. All respondents were male and Tausug, while the largest age group was 31-40 years (36%). Heavy rainfall was the leading operational challenge (74%), followed by hot weather (24%). Vendors reported frequent avoidance of spoiled fish (weighted mean = 4.78), washing fish before display (4.70), and cleaning stalls and tools (4.62). However, proper waste disposal (2.44), covering displayed fish (2.18), and wearing protective gear (2.07) received low ratings. Respondents generally reported sufficient fish supplies for daily sales (4.66). Overall, established hygiene routines and perceived supply adequacy coexisted with weaknesses in contamination prevention and weather-related operational challenges. The study recommends regular food safety training, improved waste collection and drainage, accessible protective equipment, fish covers, and appropriate ice or refrigeration facilities. Findings are limited by nonprobability sampling at one market, reliance primarily on vendor reports, and the absence of microbiological testing. By identifying specific priorities for vendors and market administrators, this study provides practical evidence for locally responsive sanitation improvements. Coordinated action among local government units, public health authorities, and vendors is particularly important. Its implications support Sustainable Development Goal 3, Good Health and Well-Being, while encouraging safer seafood handling and more sustainable fish vending livelihoods in Bongao.
10.1139/cjz-2026-0062: There is growing concern that exotic rainbow smelt (Osmerus mordax [Mitchill, 1814]), are impacting lake trout (Salvelinus namaycush [Walbaum in Artedi, 1792]) fisheries in lakes where they have invaded beyond direct competition and predation. Smelt contain the thiamine-degrading enzyme thiaminase whose consumption can cause thiamine deficiency, which decreases growth and condition. Recent studies further suggest smelt may also impact trout indirectly by altering trophic interactions and reducing the flow of thiamine through the food web. Here, we used a multi-lake study in the Sudbury Basin (Ontario, Canada) to test whether presence of exotic smelt was associated with changes in trout trophic ecology, body condition, growth, and tissue thiamine status. Muscle thiamine concentrations in trout did not differ between lakes with and without smelt, although one fish from Wanapitei Lake (smelt lake) exhibited muscle thiamine at concentrations that can be associated with thiamine deficiency. Body condition was significantly lower in trout from lakes with smelt, and asymptotic length of trout populations declined with increasing proportion of smelt in the diet. Muscle δ15N values were significantly higher in trout from smelt-invaded lakes, and muscle thiamine concentrations declined with increasing δ15N. We discuss possible impacts of consumption of smelt on lake trout conservation.
10.56557/upjoz/2026/v47i215954: Petroleum-derived residues in edible aquatic organisms provide an indication of contaminant occurrence in coastal fisheries, although aggregate fluorescence measurements cannot identify individual toxic constituents. Finfish and shellfish collected from the Parangipettai and Pazhaiyar fish landing centres at the Vellar and Coleroon estuarine mouths, Tamil Nadu, in December 2024, were examined for solvent-extractable, chrysene-calibrated petroleum hydrocarbon (PHC) fluorescence and crude fat. The collection comprised ten finfish and ten shellfish taxa, with 38 specimens recorded in each group across the two landing centres. The reported finfish PHC ranges were 0.25-1.30 µg/g wet weight at Parangipettai and 0.10-1.20 µg/g at Pazhaiyar; the corresponding shellfish ranges were 1.67-4.75 and 1.40-4.82 µg/g. The site-level summary means were 0.784 and 0.662 µg/g for finfish and 2.801 and 2.876 µg/g for shellfish, respectively. Extractable fat values spanned 0.9-9.71% in finfish and 0.5-10.9% in shellfish. Shellfish showed higher PHC concentrations in the reported group summaries, but sampling during a single month does not establish temporal trends, sources or bioaccumulation rates. Because the assay was not compound-specific, regulatory compliance and risks to seafood consumers cannot be determined from these measurements alone.
10.3390/fishes11110673: The transition to precision aquaculture systems requires the introduction of automated methods for continuous monitoring of the physiological state and behavior of aquatic organisms. The practical implementation of video analytics systems in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) is constrained by the non-representativeness of existing image datasets, the shortage of annotated video sequences for individual fish instance tracking tasks, and the lack of systematized engineering recommendations for organizing video recording in an artificial aquatic environment with high concentrations of suspended solids, variable lighting, and hydrodynamic interference. This study proposes methodologies for video recording and creating an annotated video dataset required for training a video analytics system for RAS.
