An analytical review of modern approaches to recognizing feeding behavior, fish detection and tracking, and morphometric analysis of fish was conducted. The identified limitations of existing open datasets relate to the predominance of static RGB images, the insufficient number of annotated video sequences, and limited species representation. Requirements are formulated for video recording equipment and its installation, as well as for lighting systems, auxiliary sensors, and recording schedules, with the aim of reducing the impact of common image artifacts such as low contrast, blur, glare, uneven illumination, and color distortion. To address the tasks of detecting and tracking a group of objects, a methodology for frame-by-frame annotation of video sequences using a modified TrackMe tool was developed, allowing the consistent formation of trajectories of individual fish while preserving their identity under conditions of occlusion and high stocking density in RAS. The developed FishMonitorAI Dataset corpus includes 8017 frames obtained from 12 video recordings of Lena sturgeon (Acipenser baerii) and grouped into four subsets corresponding to behavioral states (rest, feeding) and external stimuli (light stimulus, strike on the tank wall). In the current version, 900 frames of the calm-state subset (three 30-s segments) have been manually annotated with bounding boxes and individual track identifiers (16,543 boxes) following an explicitly defined visibility criterion. Baseline experiments with leave-one-sequence-out cross-validation showed that four detectors (YOLOv8n, YOLO11n, YOLO11s, RT-DETR-l) reach mAP@0.5 of 91.6-92.2% but only 44.6-47.3% mAP@0.5:0.95, while the best tracking configuration achieves HOTA = 42.6% and IDF1 = 47.0%; even with ground-truth boxes, IDF1 does not exceed 73.4%, indicating that preserving the identity of visually similar sturgeon is the main challenge of the dataset. The engineering recommendations, annotation methodology, and annotated corpus with baselines are intended to facilitate the development of fish detection and tracking models for recirculating aquaculture systems.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1962143: Sardina pilchardus (European sardine) is a small pelagic fish that primarily inhabits the northeastern Atlantic and plays a key ecological and economic role in Portuguese and Spanish fisheries. Its distribution is closely linked to temperature and ocean productivity, making it potentially vulnerable to climate change. Despite extensive research on climate-driven shifts in marine species distributions, applications of Species Distribution Models (SDMs) to Sardina pilchardus in the Iberian Peninsula remain limited. SDMs provide a spatially explicit framework for relating species occurrences to environmental conditions and projecting changes in habitat suitability under future climate scenarios. This study tests the hypothesis that future climate change will alter the spatial distribution of potential suitable habitat for Sardina pilchardus along the Atlantic Iberian coast, and evaluates whether changes in sea surface temperature, wind-driven upwelling, and other oceanographic conditions contribute to these projected changes. Boosted Regression Trees (BRT), a machine-learning SDM, were used to project shifts in habitat suitability under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 climate scenarios, with sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a concentration, salinity, bathymetry, upwelling index, and mixed layer depth as predictors of sardine distribution. The projections indicate an overall expansion of potential suitable habitat, particularly along the Galician coast and in the Gulf of Cádiz, with localized losses between Lisbon and the Algarve. These projected habitat gains are primarily associated with summer mixed layer depth and summer upwelling. Under SSP2-4.5, potential suitable habitat, which reflects environmental suitability rather than realized distribution or abundance, is projected to increase by 66% for 2040-2069 and by 69% for 2070-2099 relative to 2003-2022; under SSP5-8.5, the projected increases are 63% and 77%, respectively. These results suggest that future changes in potential sardine habitat along the Atlantic Iberian coast may be driven more strongly by changes in water-column structure and upwelling than by temperature.
10.1111/faf.70123: ABSTRACT Spatial structure and movement are common features of marine fish populations, yet many fisheries management systems continue to rely on single-region stock assessments. When stock-level catch advice is generated at a broader spatial scale than management implementation, empirical catch allocation strategies provide a way to distribute harvest among regions and fleets. However, the performance of spatial catch allocation approaches remains poorly understood in terms of their ability to achieve robust management outcomes, especially when confronted with uncertainty in underlying population structure, movement and recruitment dynamics. Using a closed-loop management strategy evaluation (MSE) conditioned on a demersal fish population (western Atlantic black sea bass, Centropristis striata ), we compared uniform, catch-based, survey-based, and catch-survey hybrid catch allocation strategies across operating model scenarios that varied in population structure, movement directionality and magnitude, and recruitment dynamics. Across scenarios, catch allocation strategy generally affected regional outcomes more strongly than system-level outcomes, redistributing catch, biomass, interannual variability in catch and depletion risk among regions. Differences among strategies were modest under bidirectional movement and recruitment varying around regional means, but stronger regional tradeoffs emerged when movement was unidirectional or recruitment declined in one population component. Uniform and catch-based strategies generally produced steadier catches, whereas survey-based strategies were more responsive to changes in regional biomass distribution but increased interannual variability in catch. No single strategy consistently outperformed others across metrics or spatial scales. Empirical catch allocation can provide a useful bridge between spatially aggregated assessment advice and spatial management, but its performance is conditional on underlying spatial processes.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1854986: Mass coral bleaching events increasingly interact with chronic and acute stressors to reshape tropical reef ecosystems. Caribbean reefs are particularly vulnerable to these cumulative effects, as recurrent thermal stress acts on ecosystems already transformed by disease, coral mortality, and local and regional stressors. Here, we evaluated spatial and seasonal variation in benthic communities and their associations with herbivore assemblages across eight back- and fore-reef sites in Parque Nacional Arrecife de Puerto Morelos (PNAPM), Mexican Caribbean, during the dry, rainy, and cold-front seasons of 2024. Benthic communities differed substantially among sites, with turf algae-sediment matrix and fleshy macroalgae dominating much of the reef system and hard-coral cover remaining generally low. Benthic composition varied significantly among seasons, with a reef zone × season interaction indicating contrasting seasonal trajectories between back- and fore-reef environments, despite the absence of an overall difference between reef zones. Herbivore assemblages also differed markedly among sites but showed no consistent spatial or seasonal pattern at the community level. Associations between herbivores and benthic composition were restricted to particular functional groups and benthic components, revealing selective and context-dependent herbivore-benthos relationships. Overall, decades of cumulative disturbance have not resulted in a uniform contemporary benthic state in Puerto Morelos. Instead, contrasting benthic configurations persist and reorganize seasonally, while their relationships with herbivore assemblages remain context dependent. These findings show that understanding the trajectories of chronically disturbed Caribbean reefs requires recognizing the spatial and seasonal complexity of benthic communities and the context-dependent nature of their relationships with herbivores
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0179: Intraspecific life-history diversity can help salmonid populations cope with environmental variability, yet the mechanisms generating this diversity are poorly understood. Using genetic sibship reconstruction, we measured spatial separation among siblings as a proxy for early-life dispersal, and size differences among siblings of steelhead/rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) sampled 4-7 months after emergence across a watershed. Sibling separation was widespread, with ~90% of families exhibiting spatial separation among sampled siblings. Mean within-family dispersal distance was 8.1 river kilometers (rkm), increasing to ~10 rkm when accounting for an increasing to asymptotic relationship with family size, and maximum dispersal reached 40 rkm. Greater sibling separation was associated with increased variation in sibling body size. Body size declined from the lower mainstem upstream and stabilized beyond ~14 rkm. Sex and Omy05 haplotype were not associated with sibling separation or within-family variation in body size. These results suggest that early-life dispersal into a heterogenous river network could be a mechanism for within-family phenotypic diversity consistent with diversified bet hedging.
10.1111/jfb.70720: Abstract Alewife ( Alosa pseudoharengus ) is a small, pelagic fish that is an important prey source for piscivores in the Laurentian Great Lakes, yet its spatial ecology is poorly known, which limits the ability to monitor populations. Acoustic telemetry is a tool to understand spatial ecology; however, there may be tagging effects on a smaller body-sized population of Alewife where tag burden is higher than in larger-bodied marine populations. We assessed survival, swimming abilities and healing of Alewife from Lake Ontario after acoustic transmitter implantation. In a laboratory setting, tagged Alewife were compared across tag sizes (Innovasea models V6 and V7-4x), controls and shams (surgery conducted with no tag implantation) in fall 2024 ( n = 76). Tagging survival was also assessed in spring 2025 (variety of V7 tags) when Alewife had developed gonads and across sex ( n = 126). Capture, transport and laboratory introduction resulted in moderate mortality in fall 2024 (40%), which was reduced in spring 2025 (4%), an improvement we attribute to the refined protocols reported here. Post-treatment (transmitter, sham, control) survival was high (100% in fall; 91% in spring) with tag burdens from 2 to 8%. We attribute lower spring survival to gonad development, but it was also influenced significantly by a holding tank effect. Two weeks post-tagging, Alewife achieved critical swimming speeds of 37.9 ± 7.6 cm s -1 , with no significant differences among treatments. Incisions were all scored as moderately to highly healed 2 weeks post-surgery. Our findings establish the feasibility of tagging smaller, freshwater Alewife with acoustic tags, following best practices reported here, for telemetry applications in the Great Lakes to better understand the spatial ecology of this lower trophic species of major management and ecosystem importance.
10.18697/ajfand.156.27670: This study was conducted to assess the fish biomass, biodiversity patterns and sustainable harvesting potential of demersal large-scale fisheries in Lake Malawi. This study aimed to determine appropriate fisheries output management target points (total allowable catch (TAC) and maximum sustainable yield (MSY)). The assessment was conducted in 2024 and was based on fish biomass survey data from 2020, which was conducted on Lake Malawi by the Department of Fisheries. A stern trawler (RV Ndunduma) was fitted with a bottom trawl net with a code-end mesh size of 38 mm. Biomass was estimated using the swept-area method and MSY was estimated using the Beddington and Cooke model. Shannon, Simpson and Pielou’s evenness indices were employed to assess biodiversity, while non-parametric statistical tests such as PERMANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis were used to determine differences in fish community composition and fish size distributions across the regions of the lake. The study estimated the total fish biomass and MSY of demersal fisheries in Lake Malawi at 261,297.8 tons and 130,648.9 tons per year, respectively. The southern region of the lake contributed the highest proportion of biomass and MSY, accounting for 55.6% of the total biomass. The study recorded high fish species richness (152), predominantly demersal fish species and very low densities of midwater fish species. The southern part of the lake recorded the highest fish species richness and abundance; however, it also showed a significant regional difference in community composition and fish size distribution. The findings further showed that the following commercially important fish species, Diplotaxodon, Lethrinops, and Rhamphochromis, in the southern part of the lake had smaller mean body sizes than in other regions, suggesting possible excessive fishing effort and growth overexploitation. The study also revealed limitations in the current fish biomass assessment approach, which is biased toward demersal species and may underestimate midwater fish stocks targeted by large-scale fishers. This study demonstrates that sustainable fishery management in Lake Malawi requires region-specific allocation of fishers, improved fish biomass assessment, stricter enforcement of fishery regulations and enhanced conservation measures. This will ensure that fish biodiversity is protected and that there is long-term fishery productivity. The findings provide scientific information for guiding fisheries policy, TAC allocation and ecosystem-based fisheries management in Malawi. Key words: Trawl fishery, fish biomass assessment, demersal fisheries and fisheries management
10.1111/1758-2229.70465: ABSTRACT Environmental monitoring of salmon aquaculture increasingly uses eDNA-based bacterial community profiling, yet the practical value of Oxford Nanopore duplex sequencing remains uncertain due to low yield. We compared full-length 16S rRNA simplex and duplex Nanopore reads for predicting benthic environmental quality (EQ) at 15 Scottish salmon farms. After stringent Q30-filtering, samples contained far more high-quality simplex than duplex reads. Random Forest models trained on simplex data perfectly classified samples as above or below the good-moderate EQ boundary (accuracy 100%, κ = 1), while duplex models reached 97.6% (κ = 0.95). For four-class EQ predictions (good, moderate, poor, bad), simplex reads again performed better (80.5% accuracy, κ = 0.67) than duplex reads (73.2%, κ = 0.53). Taxonomic profiles of high-impact samples were highly concordant across read types, sharing indicator taxa such as Sulfurovum , Lutimonas and Psychrobacter . In contrast, low-impact samples showed reduced concordance due to higher diversity and insufficient duplex coverage. Nanopore sequencing also detected strong bacterial bioindicators absent from Illumina-based studies, highlighting its potential for uncovering previously undetected diversity. Overall, duplex sequencing provided no advantage for EQ assessment. Nanopore simplex sequencing is therefore a viable option for eDNA-based benthic monitoring, though further optimization is needed to improve throughput and scalability.
10.3390/en19225521: Co-locating hydrogen production and aquaculture on floating offshore wind platforms requires dispatch policies that jointly optimize energy trading, electrolyzer longevity, and cage water quality-objectives that scalarized reinforcement learning struggles to reconcile. We develop a conservation-closed reduced-order model of a 20 MW-class floating wind system, driven by ERA5 North Sea reanalysis and cross-checked against OpenFAST, and cast dispatch as a Markov decision process. Scalarized twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) agents achieved nominally higher revenue than rule-based control (+0.033 M€; Hedges’ g = 0.94) but converged to a degenerate, hydrogen-abandoning equilibrium in 7% of independent runs (2/27). A hierarchical TD3 agent (H-TD3) with an annealed logarithmic Nash-bargaining reward showed no collapse across 20 seeds (Fisher’s exact test, p = 0.32), reached 95% of its final physical-objective level at the earliest observable episode in every seed, and exhibited an order-of-magnitude smaller plateau dispersion than scalarized baselines, with revenue statistically indistinguishable from rule-based control (1.216 ± 0.040 M€). Over 1000 h, H-TD3 increased cage biomass by 22.6% and yielded an electrolyzer-subsystem hydrogen cost of €3.05/kg (excluding electricity, wind-farm, and aquaculture costs), or €6.45/kg at €60/MWh wind electricity. These results frame multi-objective offshore dispatch as a risk-control problem: Nash-bargaining rewards produced fewer collapses than linear scalarization, though the difference was not significant.
10.53730/ijhs.v10n3.16037: Complex karyotype (CK) is an emerging high-risk feature in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). We evaluated its diagnostic and prognostic relevance by integrating conventional cytogenetic analysis (CCA) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) in 30 patients. CCA identified CK in 23% of cases, including high-complexity profiles (≥5 abnormalities). FISH detected recurrent genomic lesions with established prognostic value: del(13q), trisomy 12, del(11q), del(17p). Integrated analysis improved detection of genomic complexity and refined risk stratification beyond single-lesion assessment. A representative case highlighted the ability of combined approaches to identify high-risk CK with TP53 disruption. These findings support routine integration of CCA and FISH for comprehensive cytogenetic profiling in CLL.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1977454: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guidance for broader socio-economic monitoring exists, but no single set of indicators fits every fishery; it has to be worked out in context, with the people whose wellbeing is being measured. Less is known about how this is done in practice. We describe, step by step, how general monitoring guidance was adapted with stakeholders into a wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for The Bahamas’ domestic fisheries, using the critically endangered Nassau grouper ( Epinephelus striatus ) as a case study. Twenty-eight participants from government, non-governmental organizations, research, and the value chain took part through meetings, surveys, a hybrid workshop, and interviews. Together they defined the scope, confirmed six wellbeing domains and prioritized 6 research themes. The resulting framework (Framework V01) contains 59 indicators across 20 attributes, including indicators of readiness for a prospective national seafood labeling program. We report the criteria used to select attributes and indicators and the minimum standards set for inclusive participation. T Participation was uneven, which shaped the framework and is discussed as a limitation. Framework V01 has not yet been tested in the field. Its content is specific to The Bahamas, but the documented process, including its compromises, offers a practical reference for others adapting wellbeing monitoring to their own fisheries.
10.3389/fpos.2026.1929622: This study examines the relational and interpretive dimensions of policy-network implementation in the Fisheries Cultivation Village Program in XIII Koto Kampar District, Riau Province, Indonesia. The study employed a qualitative approach based on 15 semi-structured interviews conducted between April and May 2026, with interview data analysed thematically using NVivo 12 Plus. The findings show that program implementation involved differentiated actor roles, information flow, liaison and brokerage functions, trust relationships, and resource interdependence across organizational boundaries. Actors also demonstrated varying degrees of similarity in their definitions of implementation problems, particularly regarding feed/raw materials, market access, and capital, while identifying related solution areas including technical guidance, institutional strengthening, market access and downstreaming, and infrastructure improvement. These findings indicate that policy-network implementation involves both relational patterns and actors’ interpretations of problems and possible responses. The study contributes a relational-interpretive perspective that combines analysis of how actors interact with how they understand implementation challenges and formulate solution options. Rather than treating network positions, trust, interdependence, or shared problem definitions as indicators of implementation effectiveness, the study conceptualizes them as analytical features of how the policy network is organized, experienced, and interpreted.
10.22495/cbsrv7i4art3: The adoption of sustainable aquaculture standards is promoted as a pathway toward food safety, environmental protection, and market upgrading, yet smallholder uptake often remains limited because compliance costs are immediate while market rewards are uncertain. This study examines that tension using a 2016-2017 survey of 240 aquaculture households in coastal Nam Dinh Province, Vietnam, comprising all 120 Vietnamese Good Agricultural Practices (VietGAP) households identified as actively implementing or preparing for VietGAP in the survey frame and 120 conventional households randomly selected from the same localities. Farm-level economic accounting is combined with a binary logistic model. VietGAP farms generated higher output values but also incurred substantially higher costs, producing lower mixed-income-to-intermediate-cost ratios than conventional farms. The original model estimates show strong associations between VietGAP participation, public technical training, and intensive or semi-intensive farming systems. Because the analytical sample was deliberately balanced by adoption status, these model outputs are interpreted as within-sample associations rather than population adoption probabilities. The study also draws on direct questionnaires with 45 market actors and 30 local officials to contextualize market coordination and policy conditions. The findings are presented as historical, mechanism-focused evidence from the early implementation phase of VietGAP rather than as a description of current prevalence. They suggest that sustainable aquaculture standards are more likely to scale when technical capability, market coordination, and compliance finance develop together.
10.3389/fmicb.2026.1992240: The extent to which recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) biofilters contain pathogenic microorganisms is poorly understood. Previous studies have been limited to single facilities, offering little insight into pathogen prevalence across different systems. This study quantified the occurrence of three bacterial and four viral pathogens in 50 freshwater biofilters from 36 commercial RAS across 11 facilities in Norway and the Faroe Islands for Atlantic salmon using quantitative PCR (qPCR). We also characterized the bacterial community structure using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Overall, pathogens were present at low abundance. Flavobacterium psychrophilum was detected in 35 of 50 biofilters (70%). Its highest abundance was estimated at 18.6 copies per ng template DNA or 0.015% relative to 16S rRNA gene copies. Yersinia ruckeri and Candidatus Branchiomonas cysticola were rare, detected in 4 (8%) and 1 (2%) biofilters, respectively. Infectious pancreatic necrosis virus (IPNV) was detected in 16 biofilters (32%). Avirulent infectious salmon anemia virus (ISAV-HPR0), Orthoreovirus piscis -1 (PRV-1), and salmon gill poxvirus (SGPV) were detected in 11 (22%), 6 (12%), and 3 (6%) biofilters, respectively. Microbial community analysis showed that heterotrophic bacterial genera, e.g., Flavobacterium , Aeromonas , Pseudomonas , and Mycobacterium , were commonly found in RAS biofilters.
10.1186/s43067-026-00416-z: Abstract The growing demand for animal protein highlights aquaculture’s importance for food security, yet conventional practices face challenges in water-quality monitoring, operational efficiency, and energy sustainability. This study develops a solar-powered Internet of Things (IoT)-based Smart Aquaculture system integrating real-time water-quality monitoring, automated pumps, aerators, and feeders, and renewable energy supplied by a 300 Wp photovoltaic module and a 100 Ah battery. The system was evaluated through technical performance assessments and a 60-day cultivation experiment comparing conventional and IoT + solar ponds. Sensor measurements exhibited deviations of ≤ 5% from laboratory references, while data transmission achieved an average latency of 180 ms and a packet loss rate of 0.8%. Daily energy consumption averaged approximately 850 Wh/day, compared with photovoltaic generation of 1,200 Wh/day, resulting in a 70.8% load-to-generation ratio and an average energy surplus of 350 Wh/day under observed solar conditions. The IoT + solar pond demonstrated a 29.2% increase in average daily fish growth, a 10-percentage-point improvement in survival rate (82% to 92%), and a 17.1% reduction in feed conversion ratio (1.75 to 1.45). One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed a substantial difference in sampled final fish weights between groups (F(1,58) = 2417.16, p < 0.001). However, the absence of independent pond-level replication limits causal inference and broader generalizability. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating IoT-based automation with photovoltaic energy for aquaculture operations, while indicating potential improvements in productivity and energy management. The proposed system provides a practical foundation for developing adaptive, energy-efficient, and sustainable aquaculture technologies, warranting further validation through independently replicated field trials.
10.3389/fsufs.2026.1901590: Ethnic supermarkets serving specific cultural communities have long provided alternatives to mainstream food retail systems; however, their role in seafood diversity and supply chain structure is poorly understood. To characterize product diversity and pricing, we surveyed non-frozen seafood products at supermarkets serving Asian, Black/Latin American/Caribbean, Eastern European, and “mainstream” communities in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA, and conducted interviews with store staff to elucidate seafood procurement systems at different stores. The four types of stores offered significantly different product compositions from each other (i.e., different mixes of live organisms, whole finfish, fillets, and processed and packaged products). Asian supermarkets offered significantly greater diversity in seafood species (including higher proportions of wild-caught and domestic species) at significantly lower prices than other stores. Interviews suggested that seafood supply chains at the large chain businesses were typically highly centralized, while smaller and ethnic businesses tended to work with multiple and culturally specific providers, and in many cases put considerable effort into building a complex network of suppliers in order to obtain their desired seafood products. These results indicate that ethnic supermarkets provide critical access to culturally specific seafood products for a wide range of communities, in stark contrast to an increasingly homogenized mainstream seafood retail system. These ethnic markets further function as an established but in some ways underrecognized market for domestic seafood. They also provide an example of a non-corporate, alternative food system resilient to perturbations. Small-scale seafood harvesters and local seafood advocates could benefit from recognizing and building on these successful existing networks.
10.3390/ijms272210324: Repetitive DNAs are key drivers of genome evolution, but their dynamics accompanying the divergence of Aegilops genomes remain incompletely understood. Tandem repeats often serve as FISH markers in phylogenetic studies, however, few families have been used for evaluating relationships among Aegilops species. In this study, we employed three recently discovered satellite repeats, pTa-713, pTa-k566 and oligo-45, to analyze diploid Aegilops taxa to gain a deeper insight into the chromosomal mechanisms of genome evolution. We analyzed 121 accessions representing 11 diploid Aegilops species using these three probes and showed that they are effective for chromosome and genome identification in Aegilops. For each species, we established a generalized karyotype and assessed intra- and interspecific polymorphisms. Diploid genomes varied in repeat content and distribution; Ae. speltoides had the highest pTa-713 content, whereas D-, M- and N-genomes were highly abundant in oligo-45. The specific labelling patterns allowed us to subdivide Aegilops into six groups, mostly consistent with the taxonomic classification of the genus. FISH results showed that Ae. tauschii is karyotypically distinct from species of the Sitopsis group, which contradicts the affinity established via the analysis of low-copy DNA sequences. This controversy could be due to different evolutionary pathways between coding- and non-coding DNA fractions, introgressive hybridization and incomplete lineage sorting.
10.1002/nzm2.70092: Traditional sero fisheries support coastal livelihoods in Indonesia, yet their retained bycatch remains poorly documented. This case study quantified retained-bycatch composition, catch per unit effort (CPUE) and assemblage structure in four sero units, a small-scale stationary trap operating in seaweed-farming, coral-associated, mangrove and river-mouth settings in Bone Bay. Over 120 hauls (February-May 2024), retained non-target catch was classified as commercial bycatch (CB) or low-value retained bycatch (LVB). Retained bycatch comprised 20,877 individuals and 476.0 kg from 85 taxa, and fishes contributed 97.4% of individuals. LVB made up 70.4% of individuals but 35.3% of biomass and was concentrated at the river-mouth unit (90.8% of LVB individuals), where Ambassis vachellii dominated and salinity and water transparency were lowest. Generalised linear models showed significant station effects on CPUE for both fractions (all p < 0.001). CB abundance was highest at the mangrove unit (45.6 individuals 100 m -1 haul -1 ), whereas CB biomass was highest at the coral-associated unit (2.86 kg 100 m -1 haul -1 ), reflecting mean individual weights of 18.5 and 126.0 g, respectively. PERMANOVA showed that assemblage structure differed among all stations ( R 2 = 0.36-0.48), although for LVB and total retained bycatch, dispersion also differed. These findings should be interpreted as a case study of four gear units rather than as generalisable habitat effects: each station was represented by a single sero unit, sampling covered only 4 months, habitat was confounded with mesh size and the fishing intensity of other gears around the stations was not quantified. Recording CB and LVB separately, in both abundance and biomass, is recommended for monitoring small-scale fisheries, and replicated, longer-term studies are needed before the patterns can be generalised.
10.1111/jfb.70744: Abstract Rising water temperatures can disrupt host-associated microbial communities important to fish metabolism, immunity and pathogen defence; however, the effects of prolonged thermal exposure and subsequent recovery remain poorly understood. We examined skin and gut bacterial assemblages of juvenile zebrafish under four temperature regimes: T1 (28°C for 60 days), T2 (28°C for 30 days followed by 34°C for 30 days), T3 (34°C for 30 days followed by 28°C for 30 days) and T4 (34°C for 60 days). Bacterial assemblages were profiled on days 1, 30 and 60 using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing and analysis of resulting bacterial amplicon sequence variants. Gut community composition was comparatively stable across thermal treatments and showed limited overlap with water assemblages. In contrast, skin communities showed marked thermal sensitivity, with shifts in beta diversity, species richness and the relative abundance of commensal and potentially opportunistic taxa. Chronic heat exposure enriched Lysobacter , Rubrivivax , Gemmobacter and Pseudomonas and reduced Rhodobacter . Following cooling, T3 skin communities shifted towards control profiles, with increased overlap in core taxa, but did not fully return to the control state. These findings demonstrate tissue-specific responses to prolonged warming and identify the skin bacterial community as a potential non-invasive indicator of thermal perturbation and recovery.
10.1111/jfb.70745: Abstract Metabolic rate is often assumed to be a trait that remains relatively consistent within individuals, with most variation attributed to environmental factors. However, few studies have quantified metabolic repeatability in fishes. We examined the short-term repeatability of standard metabolic rate (SMR), absolute aerobic scope (AAS) and maximum metabolic rate (MMR) in yellow perch ( Perca flavescens; n = 15). Repeatability was moderate for SMR ( R = 0.318), mild for AAS ( R = 0.243) and poor for MMR ( R = 0.080), indicating modest within-individual variability in metabolic measurements over a 32-day experiment. More data on metabolic repeatability across varying contexts are needed to help understand within- and among-individual variation.
10.1111/jfb.70704: Abstract As a key forage fish in the Arctic, Arctic cod ( Boreogadus saida ) plays a critical role in transferring energy in Arctic marine ecosystems. While understanding Arctic cod population dynamics within the context of a rapidly warming Arctic could provide essential information for regional conservation efforts, it remains elusive. Here, we postulate that the isotopic ratio of oxygen ( 18 O: 16 O, expressed as δ 18 O) in otoliths can be used to reconstruct both the thermal and spatial history of Arctic cod across the Canadian Arctic and provide insights into future population dynamics. Otoliths grow throughout the life of a fish and incorporate oxygen stable isotopes proportionate to ambient concentrations following a temperature-dependent fractionation, thereby reflecting the thermal habitats utilized by Arctic cod through their lifetime. Here, we measured δ 18 O in otoliths from 370 Arctic cod caught across the Canadian Arctic. We derived in-situ fractionation equations inclusive of an age component, compared these with available laboratory-derived equations, and estimated ambient temperature at larval stages of fish development. We further modelled the effects of ambient temperature experienced during otolith core formation on standard length-at-age using a generalized linear model to better understand the effects of warming temperatures on Arctic cod. The results of our study confirm ontogenetic vertical migration of Arctic cod from the epipelagic layer (0-100 m) to the deeper Atlantic water mass (>100 m) within the first year of life. However, the lack of regional small-scale variation in δ 18 O values within deeper Atlantic waters that fish used impeded the detection of regional horizontal movements at depth based solely on this tracer. Analyses of δ 18 O also showed that Arctic cod experiencing warmer temperatures during early life stages are smaller around age of maturity, suggesting applicability of the temperature-size rule. Thus, the effects of increasing surface water temperatures in the Canadian Arctic could propagate through the marine food web. While oxygen isotopes in otoliths are a promising way to monitor the effects of temperature on Arctic cod growth in the Canadian Arctic, work remains to realize the full potential of this tool to identify shifts in habitat use.
10.1002/aff2.70373: ABSTRACT Lake Tana, Ethiopia, harbours the world's only remaining cyprinid species flock, making it globally significant for conservation. Yet, these resources face mounting anthropogenic pressures from overfishing and land use changes. We assessed fish assemblage structure and seasonal dynamics in the Gulf of Lake Tana from September 2024 to August 2025 and land use land cover (LULC) changes from 2000 to 2025 using Landsat and Sentinel imagery. Fish specimens were sampled monthly from fishers at landing sites employing gillnets of varying mesh sizes. The specimens were identified to species level and analysed using Shannon diversity ( H ′), evenness ( J ), dominance ( C ) and Index of Relative Importance (%IRI). Exploratory multivariate analyses (non-metric multidimensional scaling [NMDS] and principal component analysis [PCA] of four seasonal aggregates) were used to describe seasonal assemblage patterns. A total of 2764 specimens representing 18 species were recorded, dominated by endemic Labeobarbus spp. (81.8%), followed by Oreochromis niloticus (11.9%) and Clarias gariepinus (6.3%). Diversity was moderate ( H ′ = 2.60) and differed significantly among four hydrological seasons (individual-based permutation test, 9999 permutations: p = 0.0024), being highest in the dry season ( H ′ = 2.596). After Bonferroni correction, dry-season H ′ differed significantly from pre-rainy (Hutcheson t -test, t = 3.84, adjusted p = 0.0006) and post-rainy H ′ ( p = 0.036), but not from rainy-season H ′ (adjusted p = 0.066). Evenness was high in all seasons ( J = 0.87-0.95). Sex ratios were female-biased in the catches of 12 of 18 species ( χ 2 , p < 0.001). Between 2000 and 2025, cropland and settlements expanded to nearly 60% of the mapped area, whereas wetlands declined by 92.7%. Because, fish data cover a single year and no environmental covariates were measured, these LULC trends are presented only as landscape context that is associated with the current assemblage composition. The findings provide baseline data for further studies, testing these associations directly, and support the need for watershed rehabilitation, buffer zone protection and sustained fisheries monitoring to protect the lake's globally unique cyprinid flock.
10.26437/whzcjr24: Purpose: This study therefore examines the impact of selected MP instruments on FISTR flow in Nigeria over the period 1970-2024. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopts an ex-post facto research design and relies on annual time-series secondary data covering the period 1970-2024 in Nigeria. The dataset comprises 55 annual observations for the study variables, sourced from official publications of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin and World Development Indicators (WDI) of the World Bank. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model is employed to estimate the short-run and long-run relationships among the variables. To assess the robustness of the ARDL estimates, Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS), Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS), and Canonical Cointegrating Regression (CCR) estimators are also employed. Research Limitation: The study focuses exclusively on five monetary policy variables, excluding other potentially relevant factors such as trade openness, fuel prices, fisheries infrastructure, government expenditure, climate variability and institutional quality. Findings: The ARDL bounds test confirms the existence of a long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables. The long-run estimates reveal that EXR and interest rate (INTR) significantly promote FISTR, whereas inflation (INF) and foreign reserves (LFREV) exert significant adverse effects, while money supply (MS) has a positive but insignificant influence. In the short run, EXR and INF initially depress FISTR, whereas INTR and MS stimulate trade after short lags. The error correction term indicates that approximately 74.2% of short-run disequilibrium is corrected annually. The FMOLS, DOLS and CCR estimators largely validate the ARDL results, confirming the robustness of the findings. Practical Implication: Directing monetary expansion towards productive fisheries financing and strategically utilising foreign reserves for infrastructure development can strengthen cold-chain facilities, storage, processing capacity, transportation, and export infrastructure. Social Implication: It will improve the well-being of fishing and processing communities and the affordability of fish as a source of animal protein. Originality/Value: Beyond methodological novelty, it demonstrates that fisheries trade performance is shaped not only by sector-specific factors but also by broader macroeconomic conditions. These findings provide new insights for designing monetary policies that support fisheries financing, trade competitiveness, and sustainable industry development.
10.3390/ijms272210257: Heavy-metal residues in fish maw are closely associated with its collagen fraction, yet the binding behavior and molecular mechanism of grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) fish maw collagen toward common metal ions remain poorly characterized. To address this, hot-water-soluble collagen (HSC) and acetic acid soluble collagen (ASC) were extracted and characterized via SDS-PAGE, UV spectroscopy, zeta-potential measurement and amino acid analysis. Adsorption isotherms, fluorescence, CD and SEM-EDX were used to probe binding with Cu(II), Hg(II), Cd(II), and Cr(III). Dried fish maw contained 56.907 ± 0.319 g/100 g of protein and 25.01% collagen. In the four-ion mixed competitive system containing Cu(II), Hg(II), Cd(II) and Cr(III), the Langmuir and Freundlich models were applied only as empirical fitting tools, and the fitted parameters are apparent values under competition. Cd(II) showed the highest apparent adsorption capacity, while Cu(II), Cr(III) and Hg(II) exhibited stronger apparent affinity; Cu(II), Hg(II) and Cd(II) were better described by the Langmuir model, whereas Cr(III) was better described by the Freundlich model. Cu(II), Cr(III), and Hg(II) triggered static fluorescence quenching. The binding of Cr(III) and Hg(II) may involve hydrophobic interactions, while the binding of Cu(II) may involve hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces, and it may also result from the non-specific intermolecular aggregation of collagen induced by Cu(II). Low-concentration Cr(III) disrupted collagen ellipticity bands and induced disordered conformations. This work deepens the mechanistic understanding of heavy-metal binding to fish maw collagen and offers fundamental insights for future relevant research.
10.1111/fme.70130: ABSTRACT The Saline Rift Valley Lakes (SRVLs) of Tanzania support important inland fisheries, but increasing fishing pressure threatens their sustainability. This study assessed the status of fish stocks in two Tanzanian SRVLs: Lakes Kitangiri and Singida. Data on catches, species composition, catch per unit effort, maturity stages, and length-based indicators were collected from May to September 2023. Results indicate strong evidence of overfishing, reflected in declining catches and high exploitation rates. The endemic Oreochromis amphimelas (Manyara tilapia) was the most affected species, with exploitation rates (> 0.9) and fishing mortality 13-18 times above sustainable reference points. Length-frequency data showed that most individuals were captured before reaching optimal size. All sampled O. amphimelas exhibited small body depths relative to the legal 7.62 cm gill-net mesh size, and a high proportion of individuals were immature or early maturing. Interviews revealed widespread use of small-mesh nets, contributing to the capture of undersized fish. However, some individuals matured at relatively small sizes, suggesting possible shifts in population structure linked to environmental stressors. These findings reveal a mismatch between current mesh size regulations and the biological characteristics of target species. Revising gear regulations and adopting species-specific management measures are recommended to improve fisheries sustainability in SRVL.
10.1111/jfb.70721: Abstract A new species of Pimelodella occurring in the upper Bermejo basin is described using morphological and genetic data. The new species is distinguished from most congeners by having fewer total vertebrae (37-39), short adipose-fin base (20.3%-25.2% of L S ), maxillary barbel almost reaching or reaching the origin of the adipose fin, subequal lobes of caudal fin or upper lobe slightly longer, supraoccipital process articulating with the anterior nuchal plate and epiphyseal branch of supraorbital canal on the head ending in a single sensory pore (s6 + s6). The type locality of the new species is situated in the transition zone between the Yunga and Dry Chaco terrestrial ecoregions near the area of influence of Parque Nacional El Rey. Considering the high anthropogenic impact resulting from agricultural activities in the region and the high level of endemism present in the upper Bermejo basin, the new species could be categorized as Endangered (EN) in a future formal assessment, following the IUCN criteria.
10.1111/jfb.70727: Abstract Accurately estimating fish growth is critical for fisheries management, but growth parameter estimates are often affected by multiple sources of error. While the independent effects of ageing error and fishing selectivity are well documented, their combined effects remain unknown. This study used a simulation approach to determine how ageing imprecision and selectivity (logistic and dome-shaped) compound when estimating growth parameters across four rockfish ( Sebastes spp.) life histories. Results demonstrated that ageing imprecision and selectivity exacerbate biases in growth parameter estimates that exceed the error caused by selectivity alone, while selectivity was the primary driver in estimating size-at-age. The magnitude of this compounded bias was heavily dependent on the species' life history and the shape of the selectivity curve. Because growth parameters are frequently used as proxies for critical stock benchmarks like natural mortality and stock depletion, these compounded errors could distort population models. Current growth models fail to account for both sources of error simultaneously, highlighting the critical need to develop integrated frameworks that account for both ageing imprecision and selectivity.
10.56557/upjoz/2026/v47i215953: Background: Looc Lake in Castillejos, Zambales, Philippines, supports local fisheries, but baseline information on its fish assemblages, water quality and anthropogenic pressures remains limited. Aims: The study provided a preliminary assessment of freshwater fish assemblages, evaluated water quality parameters, and identified potential anthropogenic threats in Looc Lake, Castillejos, Zambales, Philippines. Study Design: Spatial rapid bioassessment and environmental monitoring across five designated sampling stations covering the eastern, western, northern, southern and central regions of a shallow tropical floodplain lake. Place and Duration of Study: Looc Lake, Castillejos, Zambales, Luzon Island, Philippines. Sampling was conducted during daytime hours (06:00-10:00 h). Methodology: Fish specimens were collected using gill nets (mesh size 7-10 cm), cast nets, and fish traps deployed for four hours per station. Species were identified, counted, and analysed for relative abundance, diversity, dominance, evenness, catch per unit effort, and Bray-Curtis similarity. In-situ water quality parameters (pH, dissolved oxygen, water temperature, and Secchi disk visibility depth) were recorded alongside colourimetric tests for ammonia and nitrates. Anthropogenic activities were documented through observational assessments. Results: Water quality parameters indicated slightly alkaline, well-oxygenated, and temperatures within the reported range. A total of 1,611 individuals belonging to six families and eight non-native fish species were recorded, of which the fish assemblages were heavily dominated by the invasive black-chin tilapia (Sarotherodon melanotheron). All fish species were classified as non-native. Diversity indices revealed low species richness and high dominance. Based on the Bray-Curtis similarity analysis, fish assemblages exhibited high spatial homogeneity and minimal turnover across the lake stations, with similarity indices ranging from 0.60 to 0.89. However, the studied floodplain lake faces ecological pressures from solid waste dumping, macrophyte overgrowth, quarrying-induced siltation, and seasonal desiccation. Conclusion: Looc Lake exhibits low fish biodiversity dominated by invasive exotic cichlids, alongside environmental pressures from solid waste and nearby quarrying. Sustainable management policies and continuous monitoring are essential to conserve the lake's ecological integrity and local fishing livelihoods.
10.9734/ajfar/2026/v28i111189: This study assessed fish species composition, relative abundance and diversity in Nworie River, Imo State, Nigeria, using fish-catch records obtained between January and August 2026. The assessment aimed to establish a baseline for subsequent biodiversity monitoring and fisheries management. Records were drawn from three sampling stations representing the upstream (A), midstream (B) and downstream (C) sections of the river. Specimens were collected fortnightly using a gill net and a dugout canoe, and records were pooled across stations. Species abundance and relative abundance were summarised descriptively, while Simpson’s dominance, diversity and reciprocal indices were calculated to characterise the recorded assemblage. The dataset comprised 1,652 fish specimens assigned to 12 species across four families. Cichlidae accounted for 80.93% of the total catch. Haemichromis fasciatus was the most frequently recorded species (255 specimens; 15.44%), followed by Pelmatolapia marae (239; 14.47%), Oreochromis aureus (209; 12.65%), Sarotherodon galilaeus (187; 11.32%) and Oreochromis niloticus (179; 10.84%). Together, these five-species represented 64.71% of all recorded individuals. Haemichromis elongartus was the least abundant recorded species (13; 0.79%). Simpson’s dominance, diversity and reciprocal indices were 0.1075, 0.8925 and 9.30, respectively. The findings indicate unequal numerical representation among the recorded species and provide an initial fish assemblage inventory for Nworie River. Because the analysis concerns pooled catch records, the estimates should not be interpreted as absolute population abundances. Continued taxonomic verification and effort-standardised monitoring are recommended.
10.3390/nitrogen7040137: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RASs) continuously accumulate organic carbon and nitrogen, relying on microbial nutrient-reduction efficiency to support fish production performance. Previous UV-C studies in aquaculture have focused on disinfection and pathogen control, with limited research on carbon-nitrogen dynamics. This study evaluated continuous UV-C irradiation in a RAS for 30 days using Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), comparing conventional and UV-C-treated systems with three replicates each (n = 3). Water quality, carbon and nitrogen dynamics, bacterial abundance, plankton density, and fish production were monitored throughout the experimental period. UV-C was associated with 59.1% and 59.2% reductions in estimated organic carbon and the carbon accumulation rate, respectively. Bacterial abundance and plankton density decreased by 69.1% and 26.7%, coinciding with reduced capacity of microbial and planktonic nutrient sinks within the system. UV-C irradiation was able to reduce NH4+, and NO3- up to 22.0% and 10.6%, respectively. Higher NO2- in UV-C was increased to 1.08 mg/L due to shifts in carbon availability and microbial community structure. Residual nitrogen increased by 17.7% because nitrogen fluxes shifted toward assimilative pathways. Consequently, nitrogen utilization efficiency improved, as reflected by higher nitrogen efficiency factor, nitrification ratio, and nitrogen-carbon transformation ratio. UV-C treatment increased final biomass by 14.1%, achieved 100% survival, and reduced FCR by 24.3% compared with Ct, suggesting its potential to modify carbon-nitrogen dynamics and improve resource-use efficiency in RAS.
10.3390/polym18222875: Valorization of gelatin capsule waste as a functional packaging material could simultaneously reduce industrial by-products and dependence on petroleum-based plastics. In this study, gelatin capsule waste was converted into active films containing hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL; 0-3.0%, w/v), and the effects of HEWL incorporation on physicochemical, mechanical, barrier, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties were investigated. The films remained visually transparent and exhibited strong ultraviolet-shielding properties, with negligible transmittance in the 200-300 nm range. HEWL incorporation improved the films’ thermal and physicochemical properties, as evidenced by reductions in moisture content (21.79 to 20.68%), water solubility (50.17 to 43.50%), swelling (777 to 406%), and water vapor permeability (5.34 to 4.20 × 10-4 g·mm·m-2·h-1·Pa-1). Tensile strength increased from 29.65 MPa in the control film to a maximum of 35.55 MPa at 1.5% HEWL, whereas elongation at break remained unchanged (p ≥ 0.05). The glass transition temperature (Tg) progressively increased from 29.78 to 41.03 °C with increasing HEWL concentration. At 3.0% HEWL, the ABTS radical-scavenging capacity and ferric-reducing antioxidant power increased by 1.10-fold and 1.48-fold, respectively. Furthermore, HEWL-containing films exhibited antibacterial activity against the tested foodborne bacteria, with Gram-positive bacteria showing greater susceptibility than Gram-negative bacteria. The film formulation containing 2.0% HEWL was subsequently evaluated for preserving semi-dried striped snakehead fish during room-temperature storage. Compared with the HEWL-free gelatin film, the HEWL-containing film retarded microbial proliferation and lipid oxidation while maintaining product moisture over 3 days of storage. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of valorizing gelatin capsule waste into a bioactive packaging matrix and support the development of HEWL-loaded films for the short-term preservation of semi-dried aquatic products.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1983862: The transition of marine ranching from scale-oriented expansion toward high-quality development requires the simultaneous improvement of production efficiency, ecological sustainability, and farmed-animal welfare. However, increasing stocking intensity and technological investment may generate trade-offs among economic output, ecological carrying capacity, animal health, and long-term production sustainability. Existing studies have mainly examined ecological efficiency, resource and environmental carrying capacity, technological innovation, and industrial performance, while farmed aquatic animal welfare and its systemic interactions with ecological and socioeconomic outcomes remain insufficiently addressed. To fill this gap, this study introduces the One Welfare framework and constructs a One Welfare High-Quality Development Index (OWHI) integrating animal welfare, ecological environment, and economic and social development. Based on marine-ranching policy texts and development practices in the Beibu Gulf urban agglomeration, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) is employed to identify configurations associated with high-quality development, while System Dynamics (SD) is used to examine feedback mechanisms and the long-term effects of alternative policy combinations. The results reveal substantial conjunctural causation and equifinality, with no single condition constituting a necessary condition for high OWHI. Three major pathways are identified: technology-policy driven, ecology-market synergistic, and welfare-environment synergistic configurations. Smart technological empowerment and animal welfare management play important cross-path roles. Scenario simulations further show that isolated welfare, technological, or ecological interventions generate limited long-term improvements, whereas the coordinated integration of welfare standards, AI-enabled monitoring, IMTA, and cross-regional governance produces stronger and more persistent synergistic effects. These findings extend conventional ecological-economic-social assessments of marine ranching by explicitly incorporating animal welfare and provide a configurational and dynamic basis for improving marine ranching sustainability.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1923310: Long-term fisheries statistics often underestimate total removals by overlooking small-scale, subsistence, recreational catches, and discards, thereby biasing assessments of fisheries trends and undermining management effectiveness and governance performance. Here, we reconstruct Uruguay’s marine fisheries catches over seven decades (1950-2022), integrating official statistics with expert-based estimates to quantify industrial, small-scale (SSF), subsistence, recreational, and discard components. Reconstructed total catches ranged from 5.0 to 5.14 million tonnes. Industrial fisheries dominated national landings until the mid-2000s, followed by a prolonged decline driven by overexploitation of key species, fleet contraction, and market constraints. In contrast, SSF have gained relative importance since 2007 and now contribute nearly one fifth of total marine landings, reflecting both structural shifts and improved statistical coverage. Subsistence and recreational fisheries remain low in volume but socially and culturally significant, yet largely absent from official datasets. These long-term trends reveal marked changes in species composition, fishing gears, and sectoral contributions, alongside critical data gaps, particularly in industrial discards and early SSF records. By correcting presentist bias and recovering unreported catches, this reconstruction provides a more complete perspective on the historical trajectory and current status of Uruguay’s marine fisheries. The findings highlight the need for more transparent and inclusive monitoring systems embedded within participatory governance frameworks. More broadly, they demonstrate how long-term reconstructions can expose structural transformations and persistent data blind spots in national fisheries, offering a transferable basis for comparative analyses and for strengthening evidence-based governance under chronic data limitation.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0059: Across its range, the survival and maturation dynamics of Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) are dependent on growth, energy reserves, and predation pressure. This study examined growth of one-sea-winter (1SW) and two-sea-winter (2SW) salmon using archived scales collected from the Miramichi River, Canada, spanning 59 smolt migration years (1958-2016). Fork length and nearly all scale-derived growth metrics exhibited significant long-term linear trends, however, no evidence was found for critical periods of reduced growth. Hence, growth during the post-smolt year showed no declines corresponding to periods of reduced marine survival, suggesting that variation in marine recruitment of North American Atlantic Salmon are not dependent on post-smolt growth. Growth patterns recorded on scales, including intercirculi spacing, were broadly similar between sea-age groups until the end of the first winter at sea, suggesting shared migration routes and overlapping marine distribution during this period. By identifying temporal shifts in growth and critical phases of growth similarity and divergence, this study improves understanding of salmon responses to environmental variability and refines inferences about the marine distribution of salmon from individual populations.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1937827: Tiger sharks ( Galeocerdo cuvier ) are apex predators with well-established ecological roles in tropical and subtropical marine ecosystems, yet their spatial ecology in the eastern Atlantic remains almost entirely unresolved. Here we provide the first systematic, comprehensive characterisation of tiger shark habitat use around Boa Vista Island, which hosts one of the Atlantic’s largest loggerhead turtle nesting aggregations, within the Cabo Verde archipelago, a priority area for elasmobranch conservation. To characterise tiger shark habitat use around the island, 526 stereo-baited remote underwater video (stereo-BRUV) deployments across four survey periods in 2025 were combined with 40 local ecological knowledge (LEK) interviews. Tiger sharks occurred on 5.5% of deployments (29 detections), with 86% of detections east of 22.80° W. Detection frequency peaked at 11.6% in June, coinciding with the onset of the loggerhead nesting season, compared with 1.9-2.8% in the remaining survey periods. Detection probability was negatively associated with sea surface temperature and positively associated with salinity, but both covariates varied almost entirely between sampling months, preventing these associations from being distinguished from temporal variation. Measured individuals ranged from 1,487 to 4,502 mm fork length, and 12 of 26 (46%) were juvenile-sized, indicating that multiple size classes use the shelf and that early-life habitat use in the region is a priority for future research. LEK identified a broader perceived occurrence footprint, including Baía de Sal Rei within the coastal survey domain and the offshore João Valente Bank beyond it-both IUCN-designated Important Shark and Ray Areas-as priority areas for targeted future surveys. Together, these findings shift the evidence base for tiger sharks in the eastern Atlantic from simple presence confirmation to the first systematic description of recurrent, seasonally structured habitat use, providing an initial empirical foundation for conservation planning of this apex predator in a data-poor yet ecologically significant region.
10.1111/faf.70119: ABSTRACT Since its emergence, conservation biology has been framed as a discipline focused on preserving biodiversity. Less often acknowledged is that conservation is shaped by cultural assumptions about how, why, when, where and by and for whom it is designed and applied. Failing to recognize these assumptions risks reinforcing unjust systems of power rooted in historical forces that continue to shape present-day realities. This is especially evident for Pacific salmon in Canada, where colonial management systems have disenfranchised Indigenous fishers for over a century. In this narrative review, we describe critical moments in this history, focusing on case studies from British Columbia and drawing parallels to the United States and Sápmi to illustrate the pervasiveness of colonialism in salmon fisheries management. We examine periods from pre-colonial times to the present, focusing on Indigenous fisheries governance, treaty processes, the criminalization and vilification of Indigenous fishers, Indigenous resistance and significant legal and legislative developments. Our analysis shows that states have frequently leveraged conservation needs to justify policies benefiting settler societies while disenfranchising Indigenous communities, legacies that continue to shape power dynamics within contemporary fisheries conservation. We write primarily to settler decision makers, fisheries scientists and managers and the legal community, who play critical roles in reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples. We highlight the need for Indigenous authority over conservation, state institutions directly accountable to Indigenous Peoples, sustained funding for Indigenous-led salmon restoration and management and the upholding of Indigenous laws as essential steps towards a more just fisheries conservation and governance.
10.15835/buasvmcn-asb:2026.0003: Fish consumption in restaurants in Romania is a complex phenomenon, influenced by a number of economic, political, cultural and ecological factors. In the context of a growing demand for fish dishes, this report explores the characteristics of the fish processing and consumption market in Romanian restaurants, with a special focus on the Bucharest-Ilfov area. The purpose of this study is to identify and analyse the factors that influence the consumption of fish in restaurants and to provide recommendations for improving menus and increasing sustainability in this sector. The current research was conducted as a survey case analysis within restaurants order to gather quantitative and qualitative data on fish consumption patterns. The results indicate that diversifying menus by introducing more fish dishes can bring significant benefits to restaurants, both economically and operationally. Fish also proves to be a versatile and sustainable raw material, which, if used correctly, can attract new segments of consumers concerned about health and sustainability.
10.1038/s44183-026-00254-6: Abstract High-resolution datasets can transform understanding and management of human activities in the ocean, yet their real-world uptake and impact remains poorly quantified. Here, we assess the influence of Global Fishing Watch (GFW), an open access platform that monitors fishing activity globally, by combining a user questionnaire ( n = 467) with a structured review of peer-reviewed and grey literature ( n = 293). Questionnaire responses reveal frequent engagement across academia, NGOs and government, with the interactive map and download portal as main access points. Publications, however, are dominated by those from high-income countries, highlighting inequities in data use and publishing barriers. GFW datasets are applied across diverse thematic areas, with ecology, conservation, and monitoring of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing emerging as dominant foci. Discrepancies between self-reported use and published outputs suggest that publication metrics underestimate the platform’s real-world impact in geographic scope, and areas such as applied policy, teaching and outreach. Despite its open-access nature, persistent barriers limit engagement, particularly in lower-income regions, leading to uneven global uptake. Overall, GFW enhances transparency and supports evidence-based management, targeted capacity-building, broader use of ancillary datasets and systematic tracking of societal outputs are needed to fully realise its potential for equitable ocean governance.
10.1111/faf.70122: ABSTRACT Monitoring diverse, dispersed small-scale invertebrate fisheries remains challenging because taxonomic diversity, informal trade and dispersed harvesting limit sustained programs that can capture standardised data used for catch identification and measurement. Computer vision is increasingly being used to overcome these challenges, but most affordable and accessible single-camera systems face a trade-off: close-range imagery required for high fidelity species identification while increasing parallax error for three-dimensional specimens. We tested a hardware-agnostic calibration method to improve an automated fisheries-monitoring platform. Nationally standardised coins placed on specimens provided a local, distance-independent scale reference. Manual, coin-corrected and uncorrected computer-vision measurements of carapace length in spiny lobsters ( Panulirus penicillatus ) were compared using linear mixed-effects models. Coin correction removed systematic bias, reducing mean percentage error from 10.77% to 1.20% and mean absolute error from 8.6 to 2.3 mm. By contrast, linear-regression correction for Panulirus penicillatus under-corrected small lobsters and over-corrected large individuals, biasing Length-Based Spawning Potential Ratio estimates. Where remote observers could verify species-level labels, computer-vision classification exceeded 90% accuracy, with other performance metrics scoring above 80%. Performance on unfiltered operational data depended on image acquisition: close-range board imagery substantially outperformed greater-distance mat imagery for taxa requiring fine diagnostic detail, particularly bivalves and gastropods. Coplanar calibration is therefore necessary for 2D computer-vision systems to provide reliable species identification and morphometric data simultaneously, supporting scalable, field-appropriate monitoring of multi-species invertebrate fisheries in data-limited small-island developing states.
10.1111/raq.70225: ABSTRACT Tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) is an important commercial fish species in Latin America and Asia, where its production primarily relies on pond farming and net cage culture. The need for more controlled and sustainable production systems has increased interest in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). This narrative review, based on a structured literature search, synthesizes current evidence on tambaqui production in RAS throughout its production cycle. Available studies demonstrate successful production from larviculture and juvenile rearing through fattening and broodstock development, including induced reproduction. The review also examines management practices involving stocking density, temperature, feeding and nutrition, behavioral management, feed restriction, and anesthetics during handling. Evidence is strongest for larviculture and juvenile rearing under controlled experimental conditions, whereas fattening and broodstock production are promising but require further commercial-scale validation. Despite these advances, further research is needed to validate the available findings across larger and commercial-scale systems, improve the reporting of engineering and operational parameters, and expand knowledge on carrying capacity, techno-economic performance, energy demand, long-term fish welfare, and genetic management. Overall, RAS represents a technically viable and promising strategy for tambaqui production. However, commercial expansion requires system-specific validation integrating biological performance, fish welfare, engineering efficiency, energy use, and economic viability.
10.1111/faf.70120: ABSTRACT One of the most pressing challenges confronting the scientific community today is understanding the consequences of global change on ecological communities and mitigating their impacts. Cleaning mutualisms are essential to the health and stability of coral reef ecosystems, influencing individual fitness, parasite dynamics, and community composition. However, these interactions are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures. This review describes the behavioural diversity and ecology of dedicated cleaners, ranging from cognitively sophisticated wrasses and efficient, low-conflict gobies to visually signalling shrimps. We then review how the intricate interactions between cleaners and clients respond to environmental change, including chronic stressors (e.g., acidification), extreme events (e.g., marine heatwaves), and direct anthropogenic disturbances (e.g., underwater noise). Mounting evidence demonstrates that such stressors can disrupt cleaner and client dynamics, diminishing interaction motivation and quality, and altering underlying neurobiological mechanisms. Despite recent advances, significant gaps remain in our understanding of the long-term resilience and recovery of cleaning mutualisms across ecological, behavioural, cognitive and physiological pathways. As ocean climate-related drivers of change intensify and increasingly co-occur, it becomes urgent to investigate whether cleaners can continue to fulfil their ecological roles, or if reefs will face a future with compromised mutualistic services.
10.1111/fog.70092: ABSTRACT In continental shelf ecosystems, physical-biological coupling between hydrographic structures and bottom-up pathways can generate spatial gradients in prey availability and quality that may influence the lipid quality of small pelagic fish. The income-breeding Engraulis anchoita on the Northern Argentinean Continental Shelf (NACS) fuels reproduction through active feeding and makes tissue lipid quality closely linked to local oceanographic and dietary conditions. This study integrated stomach content and tissue-specific fatty acid (FA) analyses sampled in three zones of the NACS spawning ground under contrasting oceanographic conditions: Río de la Plata salinity front (RP), Mar del Plata shelf waters (MDP), and El Rincón thermohaline front (ER) during austral spring. Diet composition differed markedly among sampling zones, shifting from small euryhaline copepods in RP to almost exclusive consumption of the lipid-rich Calanoides carinatus in ER. These variations were accompanied by differences in tissue FA profiles: ER individuals showed the highest total lipid content, saturated FA, and polyunsaturated FA concentrations, while MDP muscle was dominated by monounsaturated FA, matching Calanidae copepod markers. The omega-3/omega-6 was highest in ER ovaries, indicating selective omega-3 enrichment. The DHA/EPA ratio decreased from RP to ER, reflecting a progressive shift toward diatom-based food webs at lower temperatures, while the EPA/ARA ratio increased from RP to ER in both tissues, suggesting that individuals inhabiting the productive ER frontal system were in a more advanced reproductive condition. Together, these results reveal spatial patterns in tissue lipid quality closely coupled to the physical heterogeneity of the NACS shelf, suggesting a potential bottom-up trophic pathway that may have implications upon anchovy egg viability, larval survival and fish conditions.
10.65770/unbx5666: Fish scales are a well-established source of type I collagen and represent a potential route for recovering higher-value materials from fish-processing by-products. However, fish-scale collagen is often treated as a single material even though processing can generate products with markedly different structures, functions, and levels of supporting evidence. This narrative review examines fish-scale-derived collagen across the source-processing-material form-property-application-evidence continuum, with emphasis on cosmetic, nutricosmetic, and biomedical uses. Four material categories are distinguished: purified collagen, collagen peptides or hydrolysates, collagen-containing composites, and retained whole-scale collagenous matrices. Available studies show that fish species, scale composition, demineralization, extraction, hydrolysis, and material modification influence collagen recovery, structural integrity, thermal behavior, fibril formation, and downstream performance. For skin-related applications, several controlled human studies support defined orally administered fish-scale collagen peptide preparations for selected hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle-related outcomes, whereas controlled human evidence for topical application remains limited. Biomedical evidence is most developed for wound-healing materials, while bone, oral, periodontal, and corneal applications have progressed through cell-based and animal studies. Many favorable outcomes, however, involve composite materials or retained scale matrices and cannot be attributed to collagen alone. Translation remains constrained by raw-material heterogeneity, inconsistent extraction and yield reporting, incomplete product-specific safety assessment, sterilization and manufacturing requirements, limited human biomedical evidence, and insufficient environmental and economic evaluation of scale-up. Fish-scale collagen should therefore be considered a family of application-dependent materials rather than a uniform alternative collagen source.
10.66618/equalitylawandsocial.v2i2.1589: Fish shooting machine gambling remains a social and legal problem in Purba Tua Village, Batang Onang Subdistrict, despite its prohibition under Indonesian positive law and Islamic criminal law. This study examines the mechanisms, contributing factors, criminal liability, and applicable sanctions for the practice from both legal perspectives. Employing empirical legal research with a sociological-juridical approach, the study uses descriptive qualitative analysis based on interviews, observations, and documentation. Data were obtained from nine informants representing residents, community leaders, religious leaders, police officers, and players. The findings reveal that players deposit money to obtain game credits, while accumulated points can be exchanged for cash, demonstrating the elements of wagering and financial gain. The practice involves machine owners, operators, venue providers, attendants, and players. Its persistence is associated with expectations of quick profits, peer influence, economic circumstances, and limited compliance with legal and religious prohibitions. Under Law Number 1 of 2023, organizers may be subject to Article 426, while players may be subject to Article 427, depending on their respective roles and the evidence established. From the perspective of Islamic criminal law, the practice constitutes maisir and may be classified as jarimah ta'zir. It also contradicts maqashid al-syari'ah, particularly the protection of wealth, intellect, religion, and family. Effective prevention requires proportionate law enforcement, legal education, religious guidance, and community involvement.
10.1111/jfb.70726: Abstract The Marbled Stargazer, Uranoscopus marmoratus, is redescribed based on five individuals collected from the southeastern Arabian Sea, India. This species is a poorly known fish which is distributed predominantly in the eastern Indian Ocean and belongs to the Uranoscopus japonicus species group. U. marmoratus is defined as having one pair of basipterygial processes; a simple posterior nostril and tubular anterior nostril; one internal supracleithral spine and one sharp humeral spine; 4-5 preopercular and 1 subopercular spines; no scales on the predorsal region; no supraocular cirri; 52-62 transverse rows of scales on the sides of the body; well-developed occipital lobes; occipital commissure with four posterior branches; head length 2.6-3.6 times in standard length; head large; head width 3.0-3.3 times in standard length; body depth 4.2-4.7 times in standard length; head depth 1.1-1.4 times its width; dorsal surface marbled, with pale spots on a brown background. Otolith morphological description of the fish was also provided for the first time. COI sequence generated herein represents the first genetic record of the species in GenBank, and Maximum-Likelihood (K2P) analysis recovered this species as a distinct lineage, offering additional support for its taxonomic distinctiveness.
10.1108/jadee-03-2025-0120: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceived system sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Using the Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) Guidelines, 94 respondents each rated 21 themes across 4 systems, yielding 84 ordinal ratings per respondent. Questionnaires were administered in person to 56 respondents and completed online by 38. Theme-specific Friedman tests accounted for repeated observations, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 21 omnibus tests and, separately, 126 paired Wilcoxon comparisons.
