Cumulative-link mixed models provided an ordinal sensitivity analysis. Ridge-penalised multinomial regression examined the separate ranking outcome. Findings Differences across systems were supported for 18 of the 21 themes after adjustment for multiple testing. Corporate ethics, rule of law and biodiversity showed no supported omnibus differences. Super-intensive farming generally received the highest ratings for the importance of addressing sustainability issues. These ratings concern perceived priorities rather than measured performance. First-rank counts were 27, 7, 5 and 55 for super-intensive, intensive, semi-intensive and extensive/improved extensive/integrated systems, respectively. Age and self-reported knowledge were positively associated with selected ranking contrasts. These associations provide secondary evidence because two outcome categories were small. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample comprised 52 consumers, 36 business stakeholders and 6 experts. Its size and composition limit generalisation. Survey mode, fixed question order, unmeasured familiarity with production systems, concentrated high ratings and seven uniform response profiles may have influenced the findings. Sparse ranking categories limit prediction and practical interpretation of the multinomial model. Social implications Promoting sustainable shrimp farming systems also aligns with MARD’s approved “Sustainable aquaculture development plan in the Mekong Delta to 2030” (Decision No. 3550/QÐ-BNN-TCTS, August 2021), which aims to develop regional aquaculture sustainably. Originality/value The study applies the SAFA themes to comparisons of shrimp farming systems rated by the same stakeholders. By distinguishing the importance assigned to individual issues from an overall sustainability ranking, it explains how these two forms of judgement contribute different evidence to sustainability assessment.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2012048: Improving the carbon emission efficiency of marine capture fisheries is important for the sustainable development of fisheries under climate change. Using 66 major marine fishing countries over 1995-2017 as the sample, we divided the countries into three groups by fishing structure: high-input predatory fish-dominated, mixed, and small pelagic and other finfish-dominated. We measured carbon emission efficiency with a slacks-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs and a metafrontier approach, and decomposed the potential emission reduction into managerial inefficiency and the technology gap. The results show the following. (1) Carbon emission efficiency was generally low, with a mean metafrontier efficiency of 0.331, and the differences between groups were closely related to catch value. (2) The technology gap was concentrated in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group and the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, and its causes differed across countries: in Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia it was associated with fuel-intensive fishing operations, whereas in Peru and Chile it stemmed from the low value of the catch. (3) The mean annual potential carbon emission reduction of the sample countries was 85.4 Mt CO 2 -eq, about 53% of their total emissions, and was concentrated in countries such as Indonesia, India and Vietnam. (4) Managerial inefficiency was the main source of the reduction potential, accounting for 69%. In the mixed group, almost all of the potential came from managerial inefficiency; in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group, the technology gap dominated; and in the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, both sources contributed. Countries should therefore choose different pathways according to the source of their reduction potential. For most countries, catching up with the best practice of similar countries could release most of the potential with existing technology, especially in countries where the potential is concentrated, such as Indonesia and India. Countries whose technology gap is accompanied by high fuel intensity should focus on promoting energy-saving fishing gear and propulsion technology, while countries that mainly land low-value catch should increase the value of their catch.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0190: There has been considerable recent interest in applying portfolio theory to manage multispecies fisheries, analogous to the management of financial portfolios. It is demonstrated here that this analogy breaks down for several reasons. First, fisheries portfolio theory focuses on mitigating the uncertainty in short-term landings and revenue, which, unlike financial stocks, can usually be predicted to good precision. Meanwhile, it neglects the much more important risks of overfishing and stock depletion. Additionally, while portfolio theory reduces the volatility of the combined portfolio, it may call for highly varying landings of individual fisheries, which can cause considerable hardship. Finally, the control parameters (portfolio weightings) and random variables fundamental to portfolio theory have not been properly defined in the fisheries context, nor do such appropriate definitions seem to exist. Fisheries portfolio theory fails because it focuses on the wrong risk and it calculates this risk incorrectly. Additionally, it is based on an incorrect assumption that the actions of managers do not affect future fishery productivity.
10.3390/hydrobiology5040045: The increasing global demand for fish and fishery products has established fisheries and aquaculture as essential sectors for food security and economic development. However, the intensification of these activities may also increase exposure to biological hazards inherent to aquatic environments and production systems, raising concerns for food safety, occupational and public health. Among these hazards, pathogenic bacteria, associated with water, sediments, and aquatic organisms, are of particular concern. Environmental changes, including climate change and the expansion of aquaculture practices, may further promote the emergence and dissemination of these microorganisms. Within this context, Legionella spp. is recognized as a relevant waterborne pathogen due to its widespread occurrence in natural and artificial aquatic environments and its capacity to cause human disease, primarily through the inhalation of contaminated aerosols. Consequently, workers involved in aquaculture, fisheries, and fish-processing industries may represent a population potentially exposed to this microorganism. Although legionellosis is not considered a zoonosis associated with fish consumption, and no occupational cases linked to these sectors have been reported to date, the persistence of Legionella in aquatic environments highlights a plausible but insufficiently investigated exposure pathway. This narrative review synthesizes information from SciELO, Scopus, Google Scholar, and other relevant bibliographic sources on the biological and clinical characteristics of Legionella, available detection methods and prevention strategies. The aim is to examine the potential for occupational exposure within fish production systems and discuss its possible implications for worker health. By identifying hypothetical exposure scenarios and current knowledge gaps, this review seeks to support future research and contribute to the prevention and assessment of biological risks in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, without assuming the existence of a demonstrated occupational hazard or an emerging public health problem.
10.3390/ani16223589: Mountain river networks are composed of a mainstem and multiple tributaries, where complex hydrological processes and habitat heterogeneity provide diverse niches for fishes. Previous studies have documented the fish fauna and diversity in the Dadu River basin, providing baseline information for regional fish conservation. However, differences in fish assemblage composition among river units and their relationships with water environmental conditions require further examination through continuous multi-year surveys. From 2023 to 2025, a three-year continuous survey of fish assemblages was conducted across 28 sampling sites in the mainstem and nine major tributaries of the Shimian reach in the middle Dadu River (upper Yangtze River basin), along with concurrent monitoring of water physicochemical parameters. A total of 54 fish species belonging to three orders and seven families were recorded, with Cyprinidae and Cobitidae being the dominant groups. Fish assemblages were mainly composed of rheophilic, benthic, and demersal-spawning species, reflecting the typical ecological characteristics of fishes in high-gradient river habitats. Fish assemblage composition remained generally stable over the three survey years but showed marked spatial differences among river units. NMDS ordination and PERMANOVA indicated that functional habitat types (mainstem, upstream and confluences) explained a significant proportion of variation in assemblage structure, whereas the effect of survey year was not significant, indicating that spatial differences across habitat types were more pronounced than interannual variation. Distinct fish assemblages were formed among the mainstem, confluences, and individual tributaries, with several natural tributaries supporting higher proportions of endemic and cold-water fishes. Water environmental analyses revealed evident hydrochemical gradients among river units, and redundancy analysis (RDA) showed that water temperature, dissolved oxygen, and nutrient concentrations were closely associated with the spatial distribution of fish assemblages. Building on previous surveys of fish fauna in the Dadu River basin, this study adds three years of fish assemblage data at the mainstem-tributary river network scale and further describes spatial differences in assemblage composition among river units and their relationships with water environmental conditions. These results provide baseline information for understanding the spatial distribution of fish assemblages in alpine canyon rivers and for fish biodiversity conservation and tributary habitat management in the Dadu River basin.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1941096: Introduction Post-harvest fish loss is an important concern in Somalia's fisheries sector, with potential implications for fish quality, livelihoods, food security, and market development. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional mixed-methods survey was conducted with 94 fisheries stakeholders across four Somali fish markets: Mogadishu, Kismayo, Bosaso, and Berbera. Data were collected through questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and field observations and analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Results Respondents identified inadequate fish handling, limited preservation and cold-storage facilities, unreliable electricity, transportation difficulties, and weaknesses in quality control and enforcement as major challenges. They reported perceived effects on fish availability, market prices, consumer access, food security, income, business activities, and fish quality. Recommended mitigation measures included improved fish handling, timely icing, better cold-chain facilities, improved preservation technologies, training, stronger quality-control systems, and collaboration among stakeholders. Discussion The findings provide insights into stakeholder-perceived post-harvest challenges and potential mitigation strategies in Somali fisheries. However, the study did not directly measure physical fish losses, discarded quantities, or their economic value. The findings therefore represent stakeholder perceptions and reported experiences rather than measured losses or established causal effects.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0083: Greenland halibut (Reinhardtius hippoglossoides) and witch flounder (Glyptocephalus cynoglossus) are fished in deep water (>500m) along the continental slope of eastern Canada, which is an area of oil and gas exploration. Virtually no information is available regarding the effects of noise on these species at this depth, however, some commercial fish harvesters believe that noise from seismic surveying displaces fish and causes reductions in catch. We used acoustic telemetry and a control-impact study design to test this hypothesis by measuring fish movement in response to weeks of industrial seismic survey noise. There were no large-scale displacements of tracked fish from the impacted area for either species. Greenland halibut movement, while in the study arrays, did not change with proximity to seismic activity. Witch flounder remained in the impact array longer than the control array and were more likely to remain stationary with increased seismic noise. Noise impact in this study revealed different behavioral effects, even within these two flatfish species, and suggests that effects on commercial catch rates will vary according to species.
10.3390/molecules31224099: The overuse of antibiotics in aquaculture has accelerated the emergence of drug-resistant bacteria and biofilm-associated infections, creating an urgent need for alternative antimicrobial agents. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) are promising candidates owing to their low toxicity and cost, but their intrinsic antibacterial activity is often inadequate. Herein, we report a series of copper-doped ZnO nanoparticles (Cu@ZnO NPs, 1-5 mol% Cu) synthesized via a facile solvothermal method. The 2% Cu@ZnO NPs, comprising well-dispersed spherical particles of approximately 200 nm with a highly positive surface charge (+20 mV), exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, outperforming pristine and commercial ZnO, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.2 mg/mL and a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 1.0 mg/mL against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Mechanistic studies suggested that bactericidal activity may arise from the synergy of electrostatic adsorption, membrane disruption accompanied by protein leakage, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and sustained metal-ion release. The nanoparticles were shown to reduce biofilm formation by 80.96% and maintained 88.4% viability of L929 fibroblasts at 20 μg/mL, indicating good biocompatibility. In a zebrafish larvae infection model, 5.0 μg/mL of 2% Cu@ZnO increased the 72 h survival rate from 6.25% (Vibrio-challenged) to 65.0%. Cu@ZnO-loaded filter materials further demonstrated practical applicability for aquaculture water pretreatment. This work elucidates the structure-activity relationship of Cu-doped ZnO nanomaterials and offers a low-toxicity, filter-integrable alternative to antibiotics for sustainable aquaculture.
10.9734/ajfar/2026/v28i111188: Coastal water quality is affected by multiple pollution sources, and their contributions to receiving waters depend on pollutant generation, transport pathways, and delivery processes. This study developed a source-based assessment of pollutant loads in the Xuan Dai Bay area, Vietnam, using 2025 activity data for aquaculture, domestic wastewater, crop cultivation, livestock farming, and stormwater runoff. Annual loads of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) were estimated using source-specific emission factors and delivery coefficients. Total generated loads were estimated at 3,945.54 tonnes per year (t yr⁻¹) of BOD, 10,711.35 t yr⁻¹ of COD, 1,447.66 t yr⁻¹ of TN, and 318.95 t yr⁻¹ of TP. After the proposed delivery factors were applied, the estimated loads reaching the bay were 1,577.79, 3,955.95, 716.31 and 193.73 t yr⁻¹, respectively. Aquaculture was the dominant source of estimated delivered TN and TP, contributing 70.44% and 82.12%, respectively, while livestock farming was an important source of organic loads. The results demonstrate that source rankings can change when pollutant transport is considered alongside generation. Although the estimates provide an initial basis for prioritizing pollution-control measures, uncertainty in emission factors and delivery coefficients limits their precision. Local validation and hydrodynamic assessment are needed to refine source attribution and support future assessments of environmental carrying capacity.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1982214: The Taiwan Strait is a hotspot for frequent and intense marine heatwaves (MHWs) in summer, with severe impacts on local marine ecosystems, yet their underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Recent studies have documented the drivers of MHWs from interannual timescales to long-term changes, while the role of intraseasonal variability is still underexplored. The Boreal Summer Intraseasonal Oscillation (BSISO) is a prominent component of the atmospheric intraseasonal oscillation (ISO) over the tropical Indo-Pacific Ocean. Here, we examine the modulation of BSISO on MHW features over the Taiwan Strait in June-August during 1993-2024, and explore the BSISO-associated local physical processes responsible for each regional MHW. Sea surface temperature and probability of MHW occurrence in the Taiwan Strait fluctuate as the BSISO convection propagates, with the most pronounced increase during phases 4 + 5. Statistical analysis reveals that 52% of regional MHWs coincide with these specific phases, with longer duration and greater cumulative intensity than other events. These regional MHWs are primarily induced by enhanced solar radiation under clear-sky conditions during BSISO phases 4 + 5. Composite heat budget results indicate that intraseasonal shortwave radiation changes contribute approximately 58% of the mixed layer warming tendency and facilitate the genesis and intensification of MHWs. The findings on the physical processes linking the BSISO to MHWs may provide insights into the mechanisms of MHWs from an intraseasonal perspective.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1950637: Coral lead (Pb) isotope records provide multi-decadal perspectives on marine Pb histories, but how individual records represent regional isotope histories remains an important interpretive question. We present a 1951-1998 Pb isotope record from a Porites coral at Lutao, southeast of Taiwan, and compare it with published records from Dongsha and Ogasawara in the Northwest Pacific. The three coral records exhibited substantial inter-site isotopic differences during 1953-1963, smaller differences in interval-mean 208 Pb/ 207 Pb during 1964-1984, and persistent site-specific characteristics. In 1985-1998, Lutao had a statistically distinguishable lower 208 Pb/ 207 Pb composition than Dongsha, whereas the middle-to-late change within Lutao itself was not statistically resolved. This contrast shows that inter-site isotopic differences need not imply an equivalent temporal shift at an individual site. Published Pb isotope reference fields are compatible with multiple possible source combinations but do not uniquely identify historical sources or marine transport mechanisms. Together, these results reveal spatial heterogeneity in coral Pb isotope histories, with smaller inter-site differences during 1964-1984, and highlight the need to evaluate the spatial representativeness of individual coral Pb isotope records before extrapolating site-specific signatures to regional historical interpretations.
10.15517/29j0jp96: Introduction: Costa Rica hosts remarkable marine biodiversity, vital for conserving its marine and coastal ecosystems. However, marine macroalgae remains understudied, especially in the Área de Conservación Guanacaste (ACG). To address this, the BioMar-ACG Project began in 2015 as a collaboration between the government, academic institutions, and NGOs, aiming to document marine biodiversity using morphological and molecular tools, with local community involvement. The project has since expanded macroalgal collections, identified new species, corrected misidentifications, and revealed high regional endemism. Objective: To update the marine macroalgae inventory of the ACG using 2009-2024 collections from the BioMar-ACG Project and CIMAR-UCR previous projects, through morphological and molecular identification. Methods: Surveys were conducted at 35 coastal and island sites, from intertidal zones to 20 m depth, using snorkeling and SCUBA techniques. Sampling occurred during both upwelling and non-upwelling seasons to capture environmental variability. Macroalgae were manually collected, documented in situ, and preserved for morphological and molecular analyses. DNA was extracted using commercial kits, targeting six molecular markers (COX, ITS, psbA, rbcL, tufA, and UPA) for genetic identification. Final taxonomic identifications integrated molecular and morphological data. Results: A total of 562 specimens were analyzed, representing 101 species distributed among Rhodophyta (59 spp.), Heterokontophyta (22 spp.), and Chlorophyta (20 spp.). Thirty-one species were newly recorded for Costa Rica, 22 for the Pacific of Central America, and nine genera were documented for the first time in the region. Molecular analyses revealed nine potential new species to science. Conclusions: The BioMar-ACG Project substantially increased knowledge of the marine flora of Costa Rica’s northern Pacific, doubling the number of species previously reported for the ACG. The discovery of new genera and species, together with high genetic divergence within groups such as Ceramiales and Dictyotales, highlights the underestimated and cryptic nature of macroalgal diversity in the Eastern Tropical Pacific. These findings emphasize the need for continuous exploration, molecular re-evaluation of historical records, and inclusion of diverse habitats and depth gradients in future studies. The integration of morphological and molecular data, combined with community-based research, has proven an effective model for strengthening biodiversity documentation and marine conservation in Costa Rica.
10.1093/bbb/zbag168: Abstract Fish are dietary sources of bioactive lipids, including long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids; however, phosphatidylcholine (PC) molecular profiles across fish species and muscle types remain poorly characterized. We analyzed PC molecular species in skeletal muscle from eight fish species by LC-MS-based lipidomics and examined associations with swimming lifestyle and muscle type. PC fatty acyl composition and molecular profiles varied substantially among species, and principal component analysis separated three farmed species from five wild-caught marine species. An exploratory comparison among wild-caught species suggested that the two migratory Scomber species generally showed higher relative abundances of 18:0-, 20:4-, and 22:6-containing PC molecular species than the two demersal species. PC profiles also differed between white and red muscle, particularly for 16:0-, 18:0-, and 18:1-containing molecular species. These findings provide foundational data for future studies of factors shaping fish muscle PC composition.
10.1111/raq.70228: ABSTRACT Infectious disease in aquaculture is shaped by interactions among pathogens, hosts and the surrounding environment. Temperature, salinity and other physicochemical conditions are established modifiers of several aquatic diseases, whereas environmental contaminants have been studied predominantly for their direct toxic effects. Whether contaminant exposure also alters subsequent infection has received much less integrated attention. We critically evaluate evidence linking environmental contaminants with viral, bacterial and parasitic infections in aquatic animals, while using established physicochemical stressors as a reference framework. Direct challenge studies show that pesticides, persistent organic contaminants, microplastics, mycotoxins and other pollutants can alter pathogen replication, infection severity or infection-associated mortality in specific host-pathogen systems. Several studies report altered infection outcomes after sublethal exposure despite limited or absent mortality, growth impairment or overt cytotoxicity before pathogen challenge. Pathogen challenge can therefore reveal functional effects of contaminant exposure that may be missed by conventional apical toxicity endpoints. However, the relationship is not uniform. Null, non-monotonic and occasionally protective effects have also been reported, and most direct evidence remains confined to laboratory studies in fish and shrimp. Evidence for transmission, commercial production systems, molluscs and parasitic diseases is comparatively scarce. Environmental contaminants should therefore be regarded as context-dependent modifiers of infectious-disease risk rather than universal causes of disease outbreaks. Where contaminant-associated susceptibility is demonstrated, disease control may need to address both the relevant contaminant exposure and the pathogen. This evidence supports exploring dual-function interventions that restore or mitigate contaminant-induced host dysfunction while directly inhibiting the pathogen.
10.1111/emr.70074: ABSTRACT Tropical oyster reefs are ecologically important ecosystems that support significant ecosystem services across coastal seascapes. Yet their current distribution and conservation needs remain poorly understood, limiting the effectiveness of management. In tropical Queensland, Australia, historical oyster reef declines and current threats have not been evaluated within a standardised risk-assessment framework. Here, we apply the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) criteria to assess the conservation status of tropical eastern Australian Saccostrea (TEAS) reef ecosystems. We synthesised historical records, contemporary satellite imagery and field surveys to delineate TEAS reef ecosystem characteristics, define functional and collapsed states and quantify changes in distribution. Our analysis reveals a reduction in reef ecosystem occurrences since 1750, restricted contemporary distributions, pervasive environmental degradation driven by increased catchment modification and sediment loads and identifies ongoing climate change and declining water quality as continuing and persistent risks to their conservation. We conclude that TEAS reef ecosystems are Vulnerable to extinction under three of five criteria (A: reduction in geographic distribution, B: restricted geographic range and C: environmental degradation). Criterion D (disruption of biotic processes and interactions) and Criterion E (quantitative risk analysis) were Data Deficient and not assessed. Formal recognition of TEAS reefs within state and federal conservation frameworks, alongside integrated catchment management, climate-adaptive restoration approaches and improved species-level taxonomic resolution, is essential for safeguarding these ecosystems. This assessment establishes the first baseline conservation evaluation for tropical oyster reefs in the world and provides a foundation for future regional and international assessments.
10.3390/su182211535: Environmental governance in socio-ecological systems requires coordination among actors and institutions operating across different territorial and administrative scales. This study develops a multi-level environmental governance framework for recreational fisheries in the Toltén River Basin, southern Chile. A mixed-methods case study combined a socioeconomic survey of 188 stakeholders, semi-structured interviews with public-sector representatives, and participatory workshops conducted across the basin. Quantitative and qualitative evidence were integrated to identify governance challenges, territorial priorities, stakeholder roles, and opportunities for institutional coordination. The results identified resource-use pressures alongside institutional fragmentation, limited inter-municipal coordination, weak organisational capacity, and the limited availability of permanent mechanisms for collective action. Participatory mapping identified 61 priority areas for recreational fisheries and 74 conflict hotspots, highlighting the spatial extent of these challenges beyond municipal boundaries. Based on these findings, a governance framework was structured around municipal, river basin, and regional scales, linking local priorities with basin-scale coordination and regional planning. The framework builds on existing municipal and regional coordination mechanisms, while proposing basin-level coordination as a subsequent stage to strengthen cross-municipal articulation. The study illustrates how participatory processes can inform the development of place-based, multi-level governance arrangements for complex river basin systems and provides a case-based contribution to the study of recreational fisheries governance in territorially fragmented socio-ecological contexts.
10.52998/trjmms.2042258: Commercial marine fisheries face growing pressure to cut carbon emissions while struggling with fleet overcapacity and volatile fuel prices. This study examines the Turkish Black Sea fleet (6584 vessels across 34 ports) by combining vessel registry records, long-run catch and cost accounts, hull-resistance estimates, port-level spatial patterns, fleet efficiency comparisons, and policy simulations. Registry data show that installed engine power is heavily concentrated in industrial purse seiners and trawlers, with nearly half of trawlers and one-fifth of purse seiners exceeding gear-specific power-to-tonnage reference ranges. Theoretical resistance estimates indicate that wave-making drag accounts for most hull resistance during free-running transit (58-79%) but becomes negligible during low-speed towing and net setting. Across the coast, vessel engine intensity clusters regionally, whereas total installed power is concentrated in major fishing ports. Financial accounts for 2023 show that fuel absorbs roughly one-fifth of gross revenue, leaving a 29.5% net margin after capital costs and exposing operators to sharp margin compression when diesel prices rise, while efficiency comparisons point to moderate room for emission reductions across regional fleet segments. Against a realistic operational baseline of 366.98 kt CO2 yr-1 (784.92 kt yr-1 at theoretical full capacity), a hypothetical policy combining a 441 kW active-gear engine-power limit with the retirement of vessels over 35 years old cuts projected emissions by 29.3% (107.55 kt CO2 yr-1, or 166.95 kt against the upper bound). Even so, retiring older vessels on its own barely shifts surviving-fleet profitability unless lower fleet crowding is assumed to improve catch rates. Long-run multi-basin records further show that broader catch diversity is associated with steadier revenues in smaller fleets, a relationship that weakens as vessel numbers grow.
10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114726: Fisheries cooperatives are considered one of the most effective means of developing the fisheries sector and improving the living standards of poor fishermen. The current study maps research output on fisheries cooperatives during 1941-2023 using data retrieved from the Dimensions AI database, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate. A total of 310 publications were used for this investigation to evaluate the scientific productivity in the selected subject area. Thematic analysis was also used to review the global research landscape in fisheries cooperatives. Global publication shares, rankings and developments in research and bibliometric indices such as overall citations and average citation per paper were also analysed. In continent-specific publications, Asia ranked first (73.87%); in country-specific publications, Japan ranked first (26.13%), and within India, Kerala (20.59%) has the highest number. The journal Marine Policy (4.19%) carried the highest number of research papers. However, important gaps remain, particularly the under-representation of geographical regions. The thematic analysis revealed that studies predominantly focused on marine societies. Among all the studies, the principal areas of focus included the role of cooperatives and challenges (30.38%), socio-economic and financial analysis (29.75%), governance and management (26.58%), sustainability and conservation (7.59%), gender/women empowerment (3.48%), and technology integration (2.22%). Overall, this study highlights the importance of growth dynamics in fisheries cooperatives and identifies future research areas. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing research efforts in this area, which may help improve the performance of these societies and support their development.
10.37134/jadcm.vol1.2.1.2026: Fish sorting is an important aquaculture management practice for controlling size variation, feeding competition, and production efficiency. Conventional mechanical grading methods remain relevant because of their operational simplicity and relatively low technological requirements. However, labor demands, repeated fish handling, and variations in grading performance highlight opportunities for design improvement. This conceptual study critically synthesizes eight purposively selected publications published between 2016 and 2026 to examine developments in mechanical grading, electronic sensing, automation, machine vision, artificial intelligence, and digital connectivity. A focused narrative review was conducted using five analytical dimensions: functionality, usability, affordability, adaptability, and sustainability. Based on the literature synthesis, the Mechanical-Sensing-Automation-Intelligence-Connectivity (MSAIC) framework is proposed as a modular, problem-oriented approach to fish sorting equipment innovation. Catfish Sorter Pro, an existing manually operated mechanical grading prototype, is used to illustrate the potential application of the framework and opportunities for selective technological integration. The synthesis suggests that technological sophistication should not be considered independently of operational requirements, implementation costs, maintenance accessibility, and fish welfare. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for selecting technological capabilities according to specific design problems and resource constraints. However, neither the framework's practical effectiveness nor the performance of the proposed technological upgrades has been empirically established. Future research should validate the framework through comparative prototype testing, user-centered evaluation, economic assessment, and fish welfare monitoring.
10.3390/biology15222069: Thermal discharge from coastal nuclear power plants forms persistent temperature gradients in waters adjacent to outfalls, and is one of the typical anthropogenic disturbances in nearshore waters. However, whether fish community patterns under thermal discharge are consistent between water and sediment, and whether the two media provide complementary information, remain poorly understood. In October 2024, we collected water (n = 16) and sediment (n = 15) samples near the Hongyanhe Nuclear Power Plant, Liaodong Bay, and applied environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding to compare fish community composition and spatial patterns across media in near- and far-field zones. A total of 32 fish taxa were identified: 2 only in water, 6 only in sediment, and 24 in both media. α-Diversity calculated from OTU abundance data did not differ significantly among the four medium-zone groups, mean Shannon index was numerically higher in far-field water (1.64) than in near-field water (1.07), and Simpson index showed a similar non-significant trend. Water community similarity declined with both geographic and environmental distances (distance-decay pattern), and indicator taxon analysis identified Acanthopagrus schlegelii and Lateolabrax maculatus as near-field water indicators and Sardinella zunasi and Thryssa kammalensis as far-field water indicators. Sediment communities showed high within-group dispersion and no distance-decay pattern. PERMANOVA revealed a significant medium × zone interaction, indicating that near-far-field differences in fish community composition depended on sample medium. Water community structure was associated with seawater temperature, nitrate concentration, and salinity, whereas sediment community structure showed no significant associations with the measured environmental variables. Overall, water and sediment eDNA provided partially complementary information on fish detection; combined water-sediment sampling is recommended to broaden monitoring coverage. This single-survey study provides baseline data for multi-medium fish eDNA monitoring to support future management of thermal-discharge impacts.
10.3390/ijms272210154: Mussels are considered active biofilters that filter suspended and dissolved components of water and can be used in aquaculture. We studied the role of green mussels (Perna viridis) in filtering aquaculture effluent and its effects on gametogenesis and physiological processes. We established four experimental groups: G1, G2, G3, and G4. Groups G1 and G2 received fish-cultured wastewater and shrimp-cultured wastewater, respectively. Group G3 received low-nutrient seawater, whereas G4 served as a mussel-free control and received low-nutrient seawater under otherwise identical experimental conditions. The impact of biofiltration was evaluated by analyzing gonad morphology, gene expression, and physiological energetics. The results show a significant change in the gonadal structure, with low spermatozoa and spermatid content characterizing G1, and adipogranular cells becoming more prominent. G2 showed a comparatively high number of sperm cells, with spermatozoa becoming more prominent in the gonads. G3 is characterized by elevated sperm volume. CASA semen analysis showed low sperm counts and reduced motility and other kinematic parameters in G1 and G2. The Gonadosomatic Index (GSI) and Condition Index (CI) indicated better physiological condition in G2 and G3, with the highest survival rate in G2. Quantitative real-time PCR results revealed the expression of genes in the hepatopancreas, with high expression (p < 0.05) of Glutathione S-transferases (gst-o1), Heat shock protein 60 (hsp60), Heat shock protein 70 (hsp70), Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), superoxide dismutase (SOD1), and a key sensor of oxidative and electrophilic stress-1 (KEAP1). Ammonia excretion was high in the G1 and G2 groups, and oxygen consumption was initially high in G1 and G2, later declining until the 21st day, while in G3 a stable trend was observed. Despite P. viridis’s positive role in bioremediation, aquaculture effluents negatively impact reproductive functions; moreover, P. viridis filtration augmented the decrease in nutrient content along with other abiotic components in the recirculating aquaculture in the G1 and G2 groups, confirming its role as a biofilter and helping with the reuse of aquaculture effluents.
10.3389/fcell.2026.1925369: Endoreplication is a conserved cell-cycle modification in which cells undergo repeated rounds of DNA replication without mitosis or cytokinesis, generating cellular polyploidy. This process contributes to cell growth, metabolic expansion, and developmental specialization across plants, invertebrates, and mammals. In teleost fish, whose genomes have been shaped by ancestral whole-genome duplications, endoreplication may have particular evolutionary significance. In hybrid fish systems characterized by genomic incompatibility, premeiotic endoreplication may serve as a meiotic rescue mechanism in some hybrid lineages that enables homologous chromosome pairing and circumvents hybrid sterility, as suggested by cytological evidence in female hybrid Clarias catfish ( Clarias macrocephalus × Clarias gariepinus ), where endoreplicated oocytes were observed in 12 of 372 pachytene cells (3.2%) and 45 of 142 diplotene cells (31.7%) from different females. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular regulation of the endo-switch, for which suppression of Cyclin B/CDK1 and oscillatory Cyclin E/CDK2 activity are discussed as candidate regulatory features rather than an established Clarias mechanism, and discusses regulatory differences between pure endocycles and abortive endomitosis. We further evaluate approaches used to manipulate polyploidy in aquaculture, including physical shocks and chemical treatments used to induce polyploidy, while considering CRISPR/Cas9-based manipulation of CDK1 as an experimental functional approach rather than an established production method. Finally, we outline emerging multi-omics and artificial intelligence-based frameworks for predicting hybrid endoreplication potential and mitigating genomic instability, thereby bridging cell cycle regulation with precision aquaculture strategies. Collectively, these findings provide a mechanistic and applied framework that connects fundamental cell cycle mechanisms with the next-generation of polyploid-based aquaculture innovation.
10.3390/jmse14222145: Mechanically scanned sonar can support offshore aquaculture sensing, but acoustic candidate quality and biological identifiability must be evaluated before species modeling. We analyzed 70,421 frames from 22 records and 336 complete rotations acquired on one day in two cages, one per species. A historical top-20-per-rotation detector yielded 6647 candidates, of which 4801 passed morphology rules; an uncapped rerun yielded 27,980 candidates and 14,402 passes. The 5 m between-cage pass-fraction gap fell from 26.9 to 0.4 percentage points after uncapping, revealing selection amplification. A separate probability sample of 128 passes, failures, and lower-ranked candidates yielded 83.6% agreement (κ = 0.627) between two blinded reviewers. Rater-specific, sampling-weighted proportions of automatic passes judged visually isolated were 39.2% and 55.3%; these labels do not establish single-fish identity. In the historical capped 142-case matched cohort, the mixed acoustic/detector set showed a record-level domain association (balanced accuracy 0.919; six-test Holm-adjusted p = 0.0030), conditional on ranking and selection. Species effects cannot be separated from cage effects in this one-cage-per-species design. This case study audits design eligibility, candidate selection, and reviewer dependence before biological classifier development.
10.12991/jrespharm.1725886: Channa striata fish, commonly known as the “striped snakehead”, is a freshwater fish species widely distributed in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia. The aims of this study were to evaluate the physicochemical characteristics, fatty acids composition and antioxidant activity of Channa striata fish oil from Konda, Southeast Sulawesi affected of purification adsorbent. The Soxhlet method was used for fish oil extraction. The result was found that the purification of fish oil using bentonite and activated charcoal adsorbents resulted in a reduction of acid value, peroxide value, and refractive index, while no significant differences were observed in iodine value and saponification value across treatments. Purification of the oil using activated charcoal resulted in an increased relative percentage of saturated fatty acids, specifically heptadecanoic acid (5.76%) and arachidic acid (11.07%), accompanied by a decrease in monounsaturated fatty acids such as palmitoleic acid (23.33%) and the absence of polyunsaturated fatty acids, notably gamma-linolenic acid, which was not detected. The chelating agent activity of fish oil increased following purification with both bentonite and activated charcoal. However, an enhancement in DPPH radical scavenging activity was observed only in the samples purified with bentonite. In contrast, purification with activated charcoal led to a reduction in ABTS radical scavenging activity. The sPLS-DA technique, using FTIR spectral absorbance data as variables, effectively discriminated between crude fish oil and fish oil purified with bentonite and activated charcoal. In conclusion, oil purification enhances the physicochemical properties of snakehead (Channa striata) fish oil.
10.1088/1748-3190/aec1ad: Abstract Flying fish evade predatory threats through cross-medium gliding manoeuvres, in which the ventral fins play a pivotal regulatory role. Although previous studies have examined the influence of ventral fin configuration on gliding stability, the dynamic characteristics of escape trajectories and the regulatory effects of ventral fin posture on gliding attitude remain poorly understood. Here, we employ a biomimetic approach to elucidate the gliding patterns exhibited by flying fish during escape manoeuvres. We systematically investigate how ventral fin posture regulates gliding attitude and identify an optimal ventral fin mounting configuration. Combining full-factor experimental testing with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, we propose that flying fish adopt distinct gliding trajectories to evade predators in different media, with dynamic ventral fin adjustments acting as a key regulatory mechanism. Furthermore, by extending the parameter space beyond that accessible through biological observation, this study provides new theoretical guidance for the aerodynamic design and optimisation of multi-fin biomimetic robots.
10.26658/jmr.2072480: Representations associated with the sea are especially prominent in the Roman period villas of Antiocheia ad Orontem, Daphne, the port citys of Seleucia Pieria and Myriandros-Alexandretta. A total of 33 mosaics featuring marine and freshwater themes have been identified in Antiocheia ad Orontem. These include depictions of fishing Erotes, Tethys, Oceanus and Tethys, Thalassa, the marine thiasus, Nereids, Tritons, Nymphe, fishing scenes, the Birth of Aphrodite, Arethusa, the Abduction of Europa, and the Navigium Isidis, as well as other mythological themes. In addition, depictions of fish in banquet scenes and various marine creatures are also represented. Alongside the personification of Thalassa, the mosaics depict gods, goddesses and mythological figures associated with the sea, including Tethys, Oceanus, Psyche-Eros and Aphrodite. The presence of various species of fish, marine creatures, crustaceans and mollusks accompanying these figures demonstrates the richness of the marine-fauna repertoire represented in the mosaics of Antioch. Fishing scenes constitute another important component of this repertoire. Particularly noteworthy are scenes depicting fishing Erotes and putti using different fishing techniques. The earliest examples of maritime mythological narratives in the mosaics of Antioch date back to the 2nd C. CE. The marine fauna and mythological representations particularly evident in Roman period mosaics continued, in different forms, into the 5th and 6th C. CE., appearing in personifications and in representations of Paradise associated with Christian structures. During this period, fish also acquired an important symbolic meaning within Christian iconography. Thus, the mosaics of Antioch reveal an iconographic continuity extending from the sea gods and goddesses and mythological narratives of the pagan period to the symbolism of water and fish in the Christian period.
10.3390/biology15222068: Muscle-associated lipids influence fish flesh composition, nutritional value, and sensory quality, but inconsistent definitions obscure comparisons among studies. This review distinguishes adipose tissue between anatomically distinct muscles, adipocytes within muscle connective tissue, lipid droplets within myofibers, and chemically measured muscle lipid content. In salmonids, myoseptal adipose tissue occupies the partitions between adjacent myomeres, whereas perimysial adipocytes lie within myomeres. We examine how these compartments develop, how their lipid storage is regulated, and how genetic and nutritional approaches can improve flesh quality. Salmonid precursor cultures support adipogenic differentiation involving PPARγ and C/EBPs, while evidence for depot-specific progenitor lineages remains limited. Genetic studies identify heritable variation and associated genomic regions for muscle lipid traits, but association, expression, and functional evidence frequently address different phenotypes or tissues. Translating these findings requires standardized sampling, spatially resolved measurements, and functional testing of candidate mechanisms. Research priorities include distinguishing adipocyte recruitment from lipid loading, separating cell-composition changes from intracellular regulation, and connecting causal variants with depot-specific phenotypes. Breeding objectives should integrate lipid distribution and fatty acid composition with processing quality, growth, feed efficiency, and environmental robustness. Imaging and multi-omics can support this integration when calibrated against defined biological traits and validated across populations and production environments.
10.1111/rec.70605: Abstract Introduction Richardson et al. contest the identity of oyster species that historically constructed subtidal shellfish reefs in South-East Queensland, Australia, suggesting that “ historical drift/dredge oysters may have been misidentified as S. glomerata .” Objectives To provide historic scientific evidence pertaining to subtidal shellfish reefs along Australia's east coast, to help inform the conservation status of Saccostrea glomerata . Methods Evidence provided by Richardson et al. is reviewed and compared to historical evidence. Results Evidence provided by Richardson et al. remains consistent with historic evidence that S. glomerata is capable of recruiting to both intertidal and subtidal habitats. Increased historical survival of S. glomerata spat in subtidal areas prior to 1893 was probably due to what observers at the time described as “astronomical recruitment,” facilitated by a lack of sedimentation and eutrophication. In contrast, subtidal spat settlement today is severely constrained by sedimentation and algal turfs, Queensland Unknown disease, and possibly also by relatively increased predation due to a potential Allee Effect. Conclusions The misidentification hypothesis appears to be built on a logical fallacy arising from shifting baseline syndrome.
10.3390/phycology6040122: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of the biomass and taxonomic and morpho-functional composition of stranded macroalgae and seagrasses on a highly productive shellfish bank in NW Iberia (Galicia), frequently affected by green tides, based on a year-long monitoring program and multivariate analyses. Macroalgal biomass showed marked seasonal and spatial variability, with the highest values recorded in spring. Chlorophyta dominated stranded biomass, particularly Ulva lacinulata, which accounted for over 63% of the total. Thin foliose morphotypes also made a major contribution to biomass across seasons and sampling locations. Linear mixed-effects modelling revealed a significant interaction between transect and intertidal level, indicating that spatial biomass patterns varied across the intertidal gradient. An interaction between season and intertidal level was also detected, although its statistical support was less consistent in sensitivity analyses. The absence of a consistent vertical zonation pattern suggests that stranded biomass distribution may be influenced by detachment, transport and deposition processes, rather than solely reflecting local macroalgal production. These findings highlight the importance of considering taxonomic and morpho-functional groups composition, spatial variability and hydrodynamic context when monitoring and managing valuable estuarine environments affected by green tides.
10.3390/w18222827: High-altitude freshwater ecosystems are particularly vulnerable to anthropogenic impacts, yet spatial and seasonal variations in biological responses remain poorly understood. This study assessed the health status of narrow-clawed crayfish (Pontastacus leptodactylus) and habitat condition in two hydrologically and environmentally distinct bays of Lake Sevan, Armenia, using an integrated hydrochemical and multibiomarker approach. Water quality and crayfish populations were measured in Lichk and Lchashen Bays in May, July, and October 2024 and 2025. In total, 120 crayfish specimens were examined, and oxidative stress responses were assessed in the hepatopancreas, gills, and muscle using MDA, GSH, GST, KAT, and SOD. Lchashen Bay experienced more adverse environmental conditions, characterized by pronounced hypoxia in the summer (3.4-3.9 mg O2 L-1), higher biochemical oxygen demand and permanganate oxidation, and elevated K, Na, and Mg concentrations. Biomarker responses showed significant seasonal variation, typically with highest values in July. Crayfish from Lchashen Bay consistently demonstrated higher biomarker responses than crayfish from Lichk Bay across all tissues and sampling periods. Integrated biomarker response (IBR) values confirmed this spatial pattern, indicating greater physiological stress in Lchashen Bay. The combined hydrochemical and biomarker approach demonstrates the suitability of P. leptodactylus as an indicator species for assessing sublethal environmental stress in Lake Sevan.
10.3390/fishes11110665: This study assessed bycatch composition, nominal catch rates, capture mortality and release condition in the Cypriot pelagic longline fishery targeting swordfish and albacore tuna. Observations covered 142 fishing days across 16 vessels during 2018-2024 and 335,340 hooks, recording 643 bycatch individuals from 23 species. Bycatch comprised 10.7% of the total catch biomass, with pooled rates of 1.92 individuals and 14.20 kg per 1000 hooks. Elasmobranchs accounted for 63.5% of bycatch individuals, and pelagic stingray alone accounted for 60.0%. Mean fishing-day bycatch biomass, expressed per 1000 hooks and 12 h, was 2.75 times as high in swordfish fishing as in albacore fishing (95% vessel-bootstrap confidence interval [CI] 1.53-3.68). Overall capture mortality was 26.4% (95% CI 23.2-30.0%), including 2.7% in elasmobranchs, 69.1% in teleost fishes and 60.7% in sea turtles. The low pooled elasmobranch mortality masked substantial taxonomic variation: 11 out of 22 sharks were dead at haulback (50.0%), whereas no deaths were observed among the 386 pelagic stingrays. Of the 406 individuals released alive, 396 (97.5%) were classified as Good for vitality, nine as Fair and one as Poor; all were coded as having Minor injury. Release condition remains a descriptive, uncalibrated indicator, and post-release survival was not measured. Sampling was partly opportunistic, and target fishery was partly confounded with year; results therefore describe the observed sample rather than the whole fleet. However, these findings establish a baseline for fishery-specific monitoring and mitigation and highlight the importance of distinguishing shark and stingray capture mortality.
10.1371/journal.pbio.3004065: Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can reproduce either sexually or asexually, yet the mechanisms coordinating these developmental and reproductive transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive mode in the kelp Laminaria pallida , a multicellular organism with a complex life cycle. By combining gene expression analyses with developmental experiments and natural population-level approaches, we characterize the transcriptional signatures associated with developmental state transitions in both sexual and asexual contexts. We show that asexual reproduction is associated with endoreduplication and reduced fitness, while it is retained but rarely expressed in two natural populations. Moreover, we find that the presence of potential mating partners reduces asexual development, revealing that reproductive mode is adjusted in response to reproductive opportunities. Together, these findings suggest that asexual reproduction functions as a conditional alternative to sex, promoting persistence when sexual reproduction is constrained while preserving the long-term benefits of sexual reproduction when mates are available. More broadly, our results reveal how organisms integrate developmental, environmental, and reproductive cues to balance alternative reproductive strategies across complex life cycles.
10.3389/fpubh.2026.1933985: Background Dietary ingestion is a major exposure pathway for environmental radionuclides, and the radiological safety of seafood, an important component of the global diet, has attracted increasing public concern. As a Chinese coastal city where seafood is a traditional part of local residents’ daily diet, Ningbo lacks systematic baseline data on radionuclide levels in locally common edible seafood and associated dietary radiological risks for local residents. Methods Five categories of locally common edible seafood (fish, shrimp, crabs, mollusks and algae) were collected from the southern coastal area of Ningbo during 2022-2025. Specific activities of 11 target γ-emitting radionuclides were quantified via high-purity germanium γ spectrometry in accordance with GB/T 16145-2022, and annual effective ingestion dose (AED) was estimated using local per capita seafood consumption data and ingestion dose conversion coefficients recommended in ICRP Publication 119. Results Natural radionuclides dominated across all five seafood categories, with 40 K detected in 100% of samples. Algae had the highest detection rates of 238 U (77.8%) and 210 Pb (55.6%), crabs had the highest 228 Ra detection rate (100%), and 226 Ra was detected at the highest rate in both crabs and algae (77.8%). For specific activities, algae exhibited the highest specific activities of 238 U (median 0.78, maximum 12.80 Bq/kg), 40 K (284.10, 931.00 Bq/kg) and 210 Pb (0.41, 7.96 Bq/kg); crabs had the highest 226 Ra (0.54, 13.09 Bq/kg); shrimp had the highest median 228 Ra activity (1.26 Bq/kg) while algae had the highest maximum activity (7.90 Bq/kg). Mollusks had the lowest median specific activities overall, but a higher 238 U detection rate than fish, shrimp and crabs. Only trace 137 Cs was detected in one fish (0.05 Bq/kg) and one mollusk (0.02 Bq/kg) sample from 2025. The median total AED was 30.43 μSv/y, with a conservative constructed upper-bound maximum of 133.64 μSv/y. Conclusion For the measured γ-emitting radionuclides only, natural radionuclides dominate in seafood from the study area, and all regulated radionuclides meeting China’s food radiological safety requirements. Artificial radionuclides were negligible with no significant anthropogenic perturbation, and the dietary dose for local adults in the study area remains below the ICRP-recommended public dose limit.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1969343: Introduction Reef fish assemblages are widely used as indicators of coral reef condition. Yet, diver-based surveys provide limited temporal resolution and are constrained by logistical demands. We evaluated an autonomous underwater imaging system based on cameras programmed for unattended image acquisition to monitor reef fish assemblages in the southern Gulf of Mexico. Methods Five terrestrial trail cameras adapted for underwater deployment were operated at Bajo de Diez reef during two seasonal deployments in 2024 and 2025, yielding 191,758 valid underwater images at a nominal 3-min interval. Image quality, camera view, species diversity, and daily assemblage dynamics were evaluated using expert annotations of 27,471 images, iNEXT-4steps, multivariate analyses, and an RF-DETR Medium object-detection model applied to the complete valid underwater record. Results Across the expert-sampled record, the mean daily proportion of images containing at least one fish was 17%, and 65 species were recorded. Laplacian variance distinguished lower- from higher-quality images. Assemblage composition differed clearly between the two deployment contexts and showed smaller but statistically detectable heterogeneity among fixed camera views within each deployment, while daily observations revealed structured temporal variation. On the held-out image-level test set, RF-DETR Medium achieved mAP@50 = 0.741, mAP@50:95 = 0.545, precision = 0.794, and recall = 0.650. Across 68 dates shared by the expert and CV analyses, expert- and CV-derived Bray-Curtis temporal structure was positively correlated (ρ = 0.63; Mantel permutation test, p ≤ 0.0001), with similar concordance for daily richness and the image-based relative abundance index. Applied to nearly seven times the number of manually annotated images, RF-DETR expanded temporal support from 68 to 110 dates. Discussion Autonomous imaging can extend reef fish monitoring beyond discrete surveys through repeated acquisition, while computer vision can reduce manual processing within a human-supervised workflow. Within the site and deployment periods evaluated, combining sustained fixed imaging, expert annotation, and computer vision made fuller use of the image archive and provided daily information on reef fish assemblage structure and its variation through time.
10.1139/cjfas-2025-0391: In the Northwest Atlantic, acoustic telemetry is widely used to assess aquatic species movements and habitat use within and among conservation areas. We examined the contribution of acoustic telemetry to research and monitoring in St. Anns Bank Marine Protected Area (MPA) off Cape Breton Island (Mi’kmaq: Unama’ki), Nova Scotia. Acoustic telemetry receivers have been deployed within the MPA since 2015 (26 to 46 receivers per year), with tagging of Atlantic cod, Atlantic halibut, and Atlantic striped wolffish. Through integration with the Ocean Tracking Network (OTN), a dataset was assembled that included animals tagged within the MPA and animals tagged by other projects that subsequently passed through the area. This dataset directly informs biodiversity conservation objectives by documenting distinct spatial and temporal fluxes of migratory and seasonally resident species (15 species, 504 individuals). Findings demonstrated far reaching connectivity, strong affinity for a predominant shallow bathymetric feature (Scatarie Bank), and relationships with recorded bottom temperature and depth. This study demonstrates the utility of acoustic telemetry for long-term baseline monitoring of species occurrence, movement, and ecological change.
10.66073/refocus-conf/1311073: The article examines methods for preventing scoliosis in sturgeon species and the specific features of using specialized feed enriched with vitamin and mineral supplements. The research subjects were individuals of the ship sturgeon (Acipenser nudiventris). The main objective of the study was to evaluate the effects of specialized compound feed on the physiological condition, growth performance, and occurrence of scoliosis symptoms in fish. During the experiment, the body weight indicators, survival rate, hemoglobin concentration, and total protein content in the blood of fish from the experimental and control groups were examined. The results demonstrated that the use of feed enriched with vitamin and mineral supplements can improve fish growth performance and reduce the occurrence of scoliosis symptoms.
10.1002/aff2.70367: ABSTRACT The continued use of prohibited fishing gear in inland waters around the world poses a direct threat to the sound management of global fish stocks. This is also the case in Benin, where there has been a drastic decline in shrimp production since 2002, particularly in the Nokoué lagoon. This study aimed to compare the capture capacity (in space and time) of two types of fishing gear (traps and nets) that are less destructive on shrimp catches in the Nokoué lagoon and its inlet complex (North, South, Centre, East and West), as part of a sustainable exploitation strategy. In total, two genera of shrimp were sampled: Macrobrachium Spence Bate, 1868 and Penaeus Fabricius, 1798. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) analyses and Tukey's post hoc tests revealed a pronounced seasonal pattern in catches, particularly for Macrobrachium , with a peak in September and a low-catch period from March to June. Nets showed a prolonged period of low catches, whereas traps revealed four seasonal catch levels. For Penaeus , five seasonal catch levels were identified, corresponding to prolonged peaks in catches between January and June, followed by a gradual decline to the annual minimum in October and November. The spatial distribution of catches reflects significant heterogeneity between stations. For Macrobrachium , traps caught mainly at Western station, characterized by a high density of ‘Acadja’, whereas nets showed a peak at Eastern station. For Penaeus , Western station had the highest catches for both types of gear, whereas the other stations had intermediate or low yields, highlighting the importance of spatial configuration and artificial habitats in the distribution of populations. Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests confirmed that there were no significant differences between the seasonal effectiveness of traps and nets for both genera, indicating comparable overall performance. However, the chi-square test revealed a moderate but significant difference in the size frequencies of Penaeus , with nets capturing proportionally larger individuals 150-180 mm, whereas traps favoured intermediate sizes 90-120 mm. For Macrobrachium , no significant difference was observed, reflecting a population dominated by juveniles and adults. Chi-square residual analysis corroborated these observations, showing an overrepresentation of large Penaeus sizes in nets and intermediate sizes in traps. For Macrobrachium , differences in catch according to size class remain limited to individuals measuring 90-120 mm, mainly caught by traps. These results highlight the complex interaction between gear selectivity, seasonal dynamics, and spatial heterogeneity, underscoring the importance of these factors for the sustainable management of shrimp populations in the Nokoué lagoon.
10.1002/aff2.70365: ABSTRACT The expansion of aquaculture has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives to fishmeal. The mopane worm, Gonimbrasia belina (syn. Imbrasia belina ), is a traditionally consumed southern African insect whose protein, lipid and micronutrient contents have prompted interest in its use as an aquafeed ingredient. This semi-systematic review evaluates the nutritional value and digestibility of mopane worm meal and its effects on growth, feed utilisation and physiological responses in fish. Several experimental studies on mopane worm meal in fish diets, reviews and related insect-meal research used to examine its nutritional potential were identified. The available evidence suggests species-specific and inclusion-dependent responses. Mozambique tilapia ( Oreochromis mossambicus ) tolerated partial fishmeal replacement and exhibited increased activity of some digestive enzymes, although the fishmeal-based control achieved the highest growth. By contrast, increasing replacement levels reduced growth, protein utilisation and digestibility in African catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ) and were associated with greater hepatic alteration. Dusky kob ( Argyrosomus japonicus ) showed favourable growth and feed-utilisation responses at moderate inclusion levels without major changes in digestive enzymes or haematological variables. Overall, the evidence supports mopane worm meal as a potentially valuable supplementary protein, particularly in locally formulated diets and when replaced in moderate proportions (18% for Dusky kob). Although there are studies suggesting replacements up to 60% for Mozambique tilapia, there is no scientific evidence regarding the optimal range. However, the small number of short-term feeding trials, variability in ingredient composition and processing, incomplete digestibility data and uncertain sustainability of wild harvesting prevent broad commercial recommendations. Standardised, long-term and independently replicated studies are required to establish species-specific inclusion thresholds and evaluate physiological, economic and ecological outcomes.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3526: Ophichthus remiger, commonly known as the common eel, is commercially important in Ecuador because Asian markets have high demand. Since industrial fishing began in 2004, no systematic population monitoring has been conducted, limiting understanding of the species' population dynamics and challenging sustainable management efforts. This study provides essential biological parameters of O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil, Ecuador, including size structure, sex ratio, length-weight relationship, and size at first sexual maturity (SFSM), estimated as the median length at sexual maturity (L50). Between August 2013 and December 2014, 17,186 specimens were sampled monthly using bottom longlines and traps. The results indicate a captured length range of 24 to 138 cm, with females comprising 61% of the population among sexed specimens (n = 5,876). Reproductive activity occurs year-round, with peak the gonadosomatic index in October and April. The condition index (K) is not different between females and males, there are no differences in the length-weight relationship; the specimens exhibit allometric growth. The SFSM, expressed as L50, was 56.7 cm for females (95% CI: 56.2-57.2 cm; n = 1,847) and 63.2 cm for males (95% CI: 62.6-63.8 cm; n = 1,109). Based on the estimated size at 50% sexual maturity (L50), minimum capture sizes of approximately 57 cm total length (TL) for females and 63 cm TL for males are recommended as a management reference for O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil. These data provide a robust basis for sustainable management measures, crucial to conserving this high-demand species in international markets.
10.3390/fishes11110659: This study provides a comprehensive situation analysis of Oman’s fisheries sector, which remains under-researched despite its strategic importance for economic diversification under Oman Vision 2040. Adopting an integrated PESTEL-SWOT framework, the research evaluates the political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal dimensions of the sector to identify systemic constraints and development opportunities. The methodology employs a mixed-methods approach, triangulating quantitative data from national and international repositories with qualitative insights from 382 semi-structured interviews conducted across all coastal governorates between 2023 and 2025. Findings reveal that while the sector contributed approximately OMR 521.6 million (1.1%) to the national GDP at constant prices in 2025, it remains characterized by significant inefficiencies. Internal weaknesses include low value addition, with less than 15% of landings undergoing domestic processing, and high post-harvest losses historically estimated at 20% of catch value, highlighting gaps in cold-chain infrastructure. Environmentally, while small pelagic stocks appear stable, high-value species such as kingfish and abalone face overexploitation, further complicated by climate-driven productivity shifts. The analysis highlights critical policy implications, emphasizing the need for a transition from wealth-maximization to welfare-maximization to protect the artisanal fleet, which accounts for approximately 90% of national fisheries production. Key recommendations include the adoption of risk-based food safety management to access high-value global markets, the integration of climate-resilient provisions into legal frameworks, and targeted programs to strengthen youth participation in artisanal fisheries. Ultimately, the study provides an evidence-based diagnostic baseline for an under-researched region, aligning Oman’s fisheries management with the global mandates of SDG 14 and the economic objectives of the “Blue Economy”.
10.3390/aquacj6040058: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied to crab research, yet no prior review has mapped this work or its progress toward real-world use. This scoping review maps artificial intelligence applications in true crabs (Brachyura) across aquaculture, fisheries, ecology, and processing. Following the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews, five databases were searched for records published from 2016 to 14 June 2026, yielding 11,172 records, most from databases whose broad field coverage returned papers mentioning crabs or artificial intelligence only in passing. Of these, 88 peer-reviewed English-language primary studies applying artificial intelligence to brachyuran data and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric were included. Each study was charted for species, task domain, model architecture, dataset, performance, and deployment maturity (Technology Readiness Level). The literature is young and expanding rapidly, with nearly half published since 2025, and heavily concentrated, with China contributing most affiliations and three species accounting for more than two-thirds of studies. Twelve task domains were identified, dominated by quality assessment and sex classification. The field has converged on object detectors with attention modules, but accuracy is rarely comparable because datasets and protocols are proprietary. Most systems remain at laboratory validation. Reported accuracy has therefore advanced faster than demonstrated deployment.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3674: Incidental capture of devil rays (Mobula spp.) occurs in several artisanal fisheries worldwide, yet biological information from many regions remains limited. This study examines species composition, morphometrics, sex ratio, and sexual maturity of devil rays incidentally captured in artisanal fisheries along Guatemala's Pacific coast. Fishing operations were monitored from February 2019 to February 2020 and from October 2022 to February 2024, including 246 fishing trips, 143 of which recorded mobulids. Data on species identification, disc width, total length, sex, and maturity stage were collected from landed individuals. A total of 453 devil rays were recorded. Of these, 447 were identified to species level: Mobula munkiana (n = 238), M. thurstoni (n = 205), M. mobular (n = 3), and M. birostris (n = 1); the remaining six individuals could only be identified to genus level (Mobula spp.). Of the total captures, 40.4% occurred in small-scale fisheries targeting Caranx caballus, 32.6% in fisheries targeting large pelagic species, and 27.0% could not be assigned to a specific fishery. In M. thurstoni, males exhibited a significantly larger mean disc width (131.78 ± 32.28 cm) than females (105.14 ± 26.46 cm; P < 0.05), with a male-biased M:F sex ratio of 2.01:1 (χ² = 22.56; P < 0.05). Similarly, in M. munkiana, males were significantly larger (89.27 ± 10.28 cm) than females (82.12 ± 10.52 cm; P < 0.05), and the sex ratio was also male-biased (1.64:1; χ² = 13.65; P < 0.05). These findings provide baseline information on species composition and morphometrics relevant to fisheries management and devil ray conservation.
10.3390/arts15110262: This article discusses paintings of the stories of two Catholic saints from the early modern period to late 19th- and early 20th-century art: St. Hubert of Liège (c. 656-727) and St. Anthony of Padua (1195-1231). The text first compares the 16th- and 17th-century works to more modern ones and then proceeds to discuss the developments to produce an analysis of the changes in human-animal relations that the works reflect. In the article, I determine (1) the type of human-animal communication represented in paintings of the stories of St. Hubert and St. Anthony, (2) the ideologies and relations to nature behind them, (3) the differences in representations between the two periods and the reasons for these differences, and (4) the possible reasons behind such a revival and changes. The article maintains that the changes in the representations of the two themes were deeply entangled with philosophical and economic developments that are behind our modern views of nature.
10.1111/jfb.70718: Abstract Estuarine wetlands are critical zones of land-sea interaction that play vital roles in maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. As the only remaining natural estuarine wetland in the Yangtze River Estuary, Jiuduansha's fish and macrobenthic diversity and community assembly mechanisms remain poorly understood due to limitations of traditional survey methods in protected areas. We conducted eDNA metabarcoding surveys at 11 sampling sites (6 intertidal zone and 5 riverine sites) in the Jiuduansha Wetland Nature Reserve during May and July of 2023-2024, combined with measurement of environmental variables, to systematically analyse the mechanisms of species composition, diversity patterns and community assembly of the Jiuduansha Wetland. A total of 64 fish species and 35 macrobenthos were detected. The eDNA approach identified approximately 40% more species than historical traditional surveys. Spatially, fish diversity was higher in riverine sites (average 18.6 ± 2.7 species/site), while macrobenthos were more concentrated in the intertidal zone (average 14.2 ± 2.5 species/site). Seasonal patterns differed: fish species richness was higher in May, whereas macrobenthos peaked in July. Generalized linear models (GLMs) indicated that total nitrogen (TN) and chemical oxygen demand (COD) were key environmental factors that have negative influence on both communities' richness. Beta diversity decomposition showed that species turnover was the dominant component of community variation within the study scale (70.7%-70.9% for fish, 60.0%-69.3% for macrobenthos). Neutral community model (NCM) fitting revealed increased migration rates, with Nm values increased from 4 in 2023 to 17 in 2024 for fish and from 9 to 18 for macrobenthos, based on samples collected in May and July of each year. This indicates enhanced dispersal between communities. Both βNTI analysis (|βNTI| 90% contribution of ecological drift) demonstrated that stochastic processes, particularly ecological drift, dominated community assembly.
10.70963/soc.v3i1.970: This study aims to identify and explain the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group in Bengkulu City in dealing with the decline in fish catches. This study employed a qualitative method with a case study approach. The research informants were selected using purposive sampling and consisted of the group leader, senior members, and active fishermen. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, while data analysis employed the interactive model of Miles and Huberman, which includes data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The study was analyzed using Hafied Cangara’s (2016) communication strategy theory, which encompasses five elements: communicator, message, media, receiver, and effect. The findings show that the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach The findings show that the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group involved open communication, deliberation, and a family-oriented approach. The group leader and senior members acted as communicators in directing the members, while the messages conveyed included information about fishing locations, weather conditions, wind direction, sea conditions, and appeals to maintain group solidarity. The communication media used included face-to-face communication at the fishing base and mobile phones while at sea. Although mobile phone network connectivity posed a challenge, group members were able to adapt through direct communication.
