These communication strategies helped maintain coordination, strengthen cooperation, increase participation, and preserve group solidarity in dealing with the decline in fish catches.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3672: The Chilean silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) is an endemic freshwater species with emerging potential for aquaculture and conservation-oriented production. However, key bioengineering parameters required for system design and biomass management remain poorly defined. This study evaluated how body size and stocking density affect total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) excretion rates in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) under controlled conditions. Two stocking densities (1.1 and 1.8 kg m-3) and two size ranges (7.8-77.8 g and 80-297 g), as well as their interaction, were tested using a factorial design with triplicate tanks per treatment. Mean TAN excretion rates ranged from 24.5 to 30.6 mg TAN kg-1 fish h-1. A clear diurnal excretion pattern was observed, with peak TAN release occurring 2-4 h after feeding, followed by a gradual decline. Neither body size nor stocking density significantly affected TAN excretion within the evaluated ranges, indicating that these results provide bioengineering parameters for RAS design and scaling.
10.3390/toxins18110490: The analytical characteristics of Lyngbya wollei toxin 4 (LWTX4), a rare derivative of saxitoxin (STX), remain insufficiently documented due to its limited availability. In the present study, therefore, LWTX4 was synthesized using the previously reported synthetic route developed by Looper to elucidate its fundamental chromatographic behavior. Additionally, three other paralytic shellfish toxin analogues, STX, decarbamoyl saxitoxin (dcSTX), and 12-epi-LWTX4, were prepared from a common intermediate. Analysis of synthetic LWTX4 using the AOAC OMA 2011.02 HPLC-PCOX-FLD method yielded a retention time of 19.8 min, which overlapped with that of STX, and revealed that its FLD response was one-fourteenth that of STX. Meanwhile, under the AOAC 2021 HILIC-MS/MS conditions, LWTX4 eluted at 7.29 min, producing major product ions at m/z 205.1204, 182.0926, 164.0822, and 110.0720. These chromatographic and mass spectrometric characteristics provide useful reference data for assessing the possible presence of LWTX4 during PST profiling of biological samples. The synthetic STX and dcSTX exhibited chromatographic behavior consistent with that of their corresponding certified reference materials (CRMs) under the standard HPLC-PCOX conditions, supporting the potential use of synthesis as a complementary approach to the isolation of PSTs from dinoflagellates for the preparation of CRMs.
10.1111/rec.70597: Abstract Introduction Shellfish reef restoration occurs across diverse ecological settings. Techniques that perform well in one habitat or species assemblage may perform poorly elsewhere. Objectives We examined how field observations, constraints, and unexpected outcomes shaped restoration structures and developed Adaptive Restoration Engineering (ARE), a framework for iterative refinement and diversification of restoration systems. Methods We assessed 1081 remnant shellfish reef bommies across five Queensland sites and reviewed five restoration structures developed from 2018 to 2026 as practice-based design pathways: chicken-wire baskets, mild steel Robust Oyster Baskets, Stainless Steel Robust Oyster Baskets (SS ROBs), Quilted Oyster Doonas, and Living Oyster Gardens (LOGs). Project records, field observations, design modifications, and deployment outcomes were reviewed to identify constraints, drivers, and design responses. Results Remnant reef morphology showed reefs commonly formed discrete bommies rather than continuous platforms, supporting modular design. Field observations drove shifts from galvanized and woven mesh to mild steel and welded stainless steel. Observed burial and subsidence led to seeding racks, shell foundations, and LOGs, while mussel-dominated recruitment led to SS ROBs where cohesive reefs had not formed before mild-steel degradation. Handling, transport, and decentralized manufacture shaped unit size and fabrication techniques. These observations formed the basis of ARE, which links observation, driver identification, design response, implementation, and monitoring. Conclusions Multiple designs can be refined for contrasting settings rather than relying on a standard unit. ARE provides a restoration-specific application of adaptive management for translating field observations into context-specific design responses.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1892884: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. Across 32 dives at seven reef sites, we recorded 54 occurrence records belonging to four species: Hippocampus kuda , H. comes , Doryrhamphus janssi , and Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus . Species differed in their observed habitat associations, while size-depth relationships varied among species. A brooding male and two juvenile seahorses provided evidence of local reproductive activity during the survey period. To establish baseline genomic resources for Malaysian syngnathids, we generated high-quality PacBio HiFi genome assemblies for six individuals from three species, with genome sizes ranging from 0.45-0.61 Gbp and BUSCO completeness scores of 92.3-98.8%. The assemblies were characterized through repeat annotation, protein-coding gene prediction, orthology analysis, and phylogenomics. Complete mitochondrial genomes were generated for all six individuals. These genomic resources provide a foundation for future comparative and population genomic studies of genetic diversity, connectivity, and evolutionary relationships. Together, the ecological observations and genomic resources provide a baseline for future standardized monitoring and conservation research on Malaysian syngnathids.
10.3390/cimb48111198: Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio vulnificus biofilms pose a major challenge to seafood safety owing to their persistence on food-contact surfaces and increased tolerance to antimicrobial interventions. This study investigated the antibiofilm efficacy and mechanisms of quercetin using integrated structural, physiological, and molecular approaches. Quercetin exhibited concentration-dependent biofilm inhibition and reduced mature biofilms on abiotic surfaces, while its efficacy in inhibiting biofilm formation was evaluated on seafood. Quercetin suppressed early biofilm establishment by reducing cell surface hydrophobicity, bacterial adhesion, autoaggregation, motility, cellular respiration, and ATP production, thereby limiting bacterial attachment and microcolony formation. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy revealed changes in the EPS-associated spectral profiles of both species, indicating alterations in the biochemical composition of the biofilm matrix. These spectral changes varied between V. vulnificus and V. parahaemolyticus. Gene expression analysis demonstrated coordinated downregulation of quorum sensing (QS), adhesion, and EPS biosynthesis genes, accompanied by increased membrane permeability, intracellular protein leakage, and metabolic dysfunction. In a 6 h screen, 1/2 MIC caused only minor changes in the color and texture of shrimp and oyster, whereas MIC caused larger changes; no cytotoxicity was detected under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that quercetin disrupts Vibrio biofilms through coordinated mechanisms with limited short-term effects on seafood color and texture at 1/2 MIC, supporting further evaluation as a natural, industry-relevant strategy for controlling seafood-associated Vibrio biofilms and improving seafood safety.
10.1007/s00227-026-04950-2: Abstract Tropical reefs are among the most biodiverse and threatened marine ecosystems and face both local and global stressors. Understanding community dynamics and ecosystem functioning under these pressures requires long-term monitoring. Image-based surveys are increasingly used in reef ecology because they enable rapid data acquisition and storage. However, manual identification of benthic organisms is time-consuming and potentially subjective, creating a bottleneck between image collection and ecological analysis. Automated annotation tools represent promising solutions, but few studies have directly compared their performance with that of manual approaches, especially under varying image quality conditions. Here, we assess the usefulness of the CoralNet automated tool for classifying benthic cover in tropical reef images and evaluate how image quality influences both manual and automated annotations. Using expert-validated images, we trained and tested both approaches, measuring performance with Cohen’s Kappa coefficient and modeling the effects of image imperfections. We found that manual and automated annotators achieved similar performance across most taxonomic and morphofunctional groups, and both were similarly affected by image quality. Importantly, although the automated annotator showed a slightly lower performance than the manual annotator, image-quality imperfections had a stronger influence on annotation performance than annotator type itself. Our findings indicate that automated annotation can provide comparable performance to manual methods once appropriately trained, with strong potential to enhance large-scale monitoring, biodiversity assessments, and conservation strategies in reef ecosystems.
10.1111/jfb.70719: Abstract Tidal freshwater reaches may provide early-life habitat for diadromous fishes, but long-term evidence of their use remains limited. Size-resolved records are needed as a reference for monitoring under the Yangtze fishing ban introduced in 2021. We analysed monitoring data from Jingjiang, 240 km upstream of the river mouth (2002-2017; 519 effective surveys; 10,560 measured individuals), combining size-based catch indices, environmental-window analyses and otolith Sr/Ca profiles from 115 Japanese grenadier anchovy Coilia nasus . Individuals <120 mm standard length were classified operationally as juveniles during August-October, when scale readings supported an age-0 interpretation, whereas individuals ≥180 mm were treated as a descriptive large-fish category throughout the year. Juveniles occurred in every survey year; annulus-free individuals also occurred in winter and spring. The Juvenile Recruitment Index (JRI) showed negative associations with tidal range across the April-July spawning and larval-transport period, although none of the 72 environmental-window correlations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at a 5% false-discovery rate. Monthly models also showed a negative lagged association. None of the 40 autumn recruits sampled across four capture years had an accepted elevated Sr/Ca zone; such zones were more frequent in later developmental groups. Total catch obscured contrasting size structures: 2016 combined the series-high JRI with few large fish, whereas 2010 combined the series-high large-fish catch rate with a mid-range JRI. These findings document recurrent early-life use of a tidal freshwater reach and provide a size-resolved pre-ban reference, without establishing a disproportionate contribution to adult production.
10.1007/s12562-026-02050-0: Abstract Knowledge of gastric and intestinal food passage rates are useful to both the fish culture industry and for estimates of a species daily rations in the wild. This study compared gastric and intestinal food passage in two very different species, Mozambique tilapia Oreochromis mossambicus and rainbow trout Oncorhynchus mykiss . Both species were fed a common pelleted meal. The effects of meal size were investigated at temperatures at which each of the species is commonly cultured. Also, the two species were compared at a common water temperature. In addition, the use of chromic oxide as a measure of food passage through the intestine was evaluated. Meal size did not affect gastric emptying times in either species when expressed as a proportion of the meal consumed regressed on the natural log of time since fed. Gastric emptying in tilapia required 24 h at 25 °C and more than 45 h for trout at 13 °C. Chromic oxide was a good indicator for the progression of the meal through the intestinal tract in both species. Meal size did not affect intestinal emptying. Tilapia required 45 h compared with 65 h for trout. Gastric and intestinal emptying at 19 °C did not differ between the two species.
10.1007/s12562-026-02046-w: Abstract Stable hatchery production of yellowtail requires effective brood stock management, particularly control of vitellogenic progression. Although the absence of males impairs oocyte maturation and ovulation in several fish species, its influence on yellowtail reproduction remains unclear. This study compared female-only and mixed-sex groups over two reproductive seasons, referred to as year 1 and year 2, respectively. Oocyte diameter, ovarian histology, and gonadosomatic index were evaluated before human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) administration, and ovulation was assessed. In both years, maximum oocyte diameter before HCG administration was significantly lower in the female-only group than in the mixed-sex group. The female-only group exhibited individual variation, with some females progressing through vitellogenesis, whereas others showed arrested vitellogenic development. The proportion of ovulated HCG-treated females was significantly lower in the female-only group during year 1 and showed a similar numerical trend in year 2. However, some females with oocyte diameters > 600 μm ovulated under female-only conditions. These results indicate that the absence of males is associated primarily with delayed vitellogenic progression, whereas ovulation can be induced in females that complete vitellogenesis. Therefore, the absence of males should be considered a potential risk factor in brood stock management and may provide a foundation for future maturation control strategies.
10.1002/cjce.70632: Abstract Due to the highly continuous, complex energy coupling, and multi-energy synergy characteristics of chemical production processes, traditional experience-based or single-objective energy scheduling methods struggle to simultaneously address energy consumption, fluctuations, and carbon emission constraints. Therefore, this paper constructs a multi-objective energy scheduling model for chemical production, targeting operating costs, carbon emissions, and scheduling stability, and proposes an improved beetle foraging algorithm that integrates multiple swarming mechanisms. Experiments show that in a typical chemical energy system, the comprehensive energy utilization rate of this method was increased by 12.34% compared with the traditional method, the steam-power supply and demand balance deviation was reduced by 27.81%, and the system energy efficiency stability coefficient was increased to 0.93. The results show that the proposed model not only realizes the economic and low-carbon collaborative optimization of chemical energy dispatch, but also provides a generalizable technical path and engineering reference value for intelligent dispatch and green manufacturing of complex process systems.
10.9734/ajfar/2026/v28i111187: Background: Oyster-producing lagoons and estuaries are exposed to environmental pressures that may affect habitat condition and fishery sustainability. Study Design: Water and benthic macroinvertebrate samples were collected from four ecologically distinct zones selected to represent the major environmental gradients within the lagoon: (i) the upstream freshwater-influenced section, (ii) the central channel, (iii) the downstream section adjacent to the lagoon outlet, (iv) an area adjacent to agricultural lands/graveyards where diffuse runoff was expected to influence water quality (mapped using QGIS). These locations were selected to capture spatial variability in physicochemical conditions and benthic communities across the lagoon. The modified Delphi technique was adopted to identify priority water quality parameters affecting Crassostrea tulipa growth. Place and Duration of Study: The Densu Estuary and Anyanui Lagoon were studied from November 2023 to December 2024. Methodology: Physicochemical variables were analysed using the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment Water Quality Index (CCME-WQI), while benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages were used as biological indicators of ecological integrity. Expert consultation informed the selection and weighting of key physicochemical variables included in the index. Macroinvertebrate assemblages revealed greater taxonomic diversity and ecological integrity in the Anyanui Lagoon than in the Densu Estuary. Results: Macroinvertebrate assemblages revealed greater taxonomic diversity and ecological integrity in the Anyanui Lagoon than in the Densu Estuary. The occurrence of taxa such as Lithophaga lithophaga and Leptocerus sp. indicated relatively stable environmental conditions in Anyanui, whereas the higher Hilsenhoff Biotic Index in Densu (5.06), compared with Anyanui (3.82), suggested greater organic pollution pressure in the Densu Estuary. CCME-WQI scores classified the Anyanui lagoon as marginal (47.14) and the Densu estuary as poor (38.69), indicating environmental conditions that may limit oyster growth, recruitment and long-term fishery productivity. Although both approaches provided complementary information, benthic macroinvertebrates offered a more integrative assessment of ecological condition than physicochemical measurements alone. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the value of integrating biological and physicochemical indicators for ecosystem assessment and provide a scientific basis for prioritising habitat restoration, long-term ecological monitoring and adaptive management to sustain Ghana's brackish-water oyster fisheries.
10.55885/jucep.v6i2.1232: Coastal fishing communities often depend on selling fresh catches, limiting opportunities to increase product value through processing. In Tanjung Binga, Belitung, this highlights the need to strengthen Koperasi Konsumen Usaha Mandiri (KUM) 's processing capacity. This community service programme aimed to develop skills in producing natural fish stock powder and support the cooperative’s product development capacity. Conducted from March to July 2026, it involved 20 women from fishing households and adopted a participatory technology-transfer approach. Activities included socialisation on fisheries downstreaming, processing training, product application, laboratory nutritional analysis, and assistance with packaging, labelling, branding, and business management. The resulting product, Formio, was made from laisi fish and vegetables without added MSG through grinding, cooking, dehydration, and dry milling. Laboratory analysis recorded 52.00% protein, 1,268 mg/100 g calcium, and 855 mg/100 g phosphorus. However, moisture content reached 21.00%, indicating the need to optimise drying and assess water activity, microbiological quality, and storage stability. Overall, the programme established a foundation for valorising local fish resources and strengthening cooperative-based enterprise capacity. The results demonstrate progress in product development and skills transfer, while identifying product standardisation and market assessment as priorities for subsequent development.
10.54254/2753-8818/2026.38927: The aquatic ecosystems of the rivers maintain aquatic biodiversity, and freshwater fish are important bioindicators for the ecological health of a river. Benthic resident fish had higher tolerance to composite stress while pelagic and migratory fish had higher sensitivity to hydrological/water quality co-stress. Single factor regulation would hardly be enough to restore fish communities, coordinated regulation of flow regime and water environment was needed. This paper offers scientific evidence for watershed ecological controls and fish biodiversity conservation under various human disturbances.
10.56201/ijaes.vol.12.no10.2026.pg137.14: This research investigated the effects of digital extension and e-learning intervention and adoption among cassava and fish farmers in Bayelsa State. A quasi-experimental design incorporating pre test and post-test assessments was employed, involving 240 active smallholder farmers selected from Yenagoa, Ogbia and Sagbama Local Government Areas. Agricultural advisory content was delivered through WhatsApp groups, Interactive Voice Response (IVR) and YouTube videos over a twelve-week period. Cassava and fish farmers acknowledged the positive contributions of the interventions, with fish farmers expressing greater perceived benefits. The interventions also shaped production decisions and farm management practices, particularly in fertiliser and feed application, input selection, disease control and weed management. Technology adoption emerged as a significant predictor of changes in farmers’ practices after the interventions. Nevertheless, inconsistent mobile network connectivity, expensive data subscriptions, unreliable electricity and inadequate digital literacy limited effective engagement. The research concluded that digital extension and e-learning interventions offer opportunities for enhancing agricultural knowledge dissemination and improving farming practices. It recommended the establishment of public-private partnerships to improve rural network infrastructure and provide subsidised data packages for farmers.

Food-based supplementation using locally available nutrient-dense ingredients, such as foxtail millet (Setaria italica) and mackerel fish, may provide a sustainable strategy to improve maternal nutrition. To evaluate the effectiveness of foxtail millet flour cookies fortified with mackerel fish flour in improving body weight, mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and hemoglobin levels among pregnant women with CED. 10.56201/ijaes.vol.12.no10.2026.pg173.19: Tidal rivers that pass through growing Niger Delta towns sustain artisanal fisheries, but surveys rarely collect fish and water quality data at the same places and times. We sampled three stations on the Egbelu reach of the New Calabar River, Rivers State, Nigeria, each month from May to July 2026. On every visit we measured eleven physico-chemical variables and caught fish with gill nets, cast nets and hooks. Salinity, conductivity and total dissolved solids differed among stations (p < 0.001), while only temperature and pH changed from month to month. Dissolved oxygen (6.50-6.80 mg L-1) and BOD5 (2.50-2.80 mg L-1) pointed to well oxygenated water with modest organic loading. We caught 1,533 fish belonging to 20 species and 11 families. Cichlidae made up 28.6% of individuals, Clupeidae 16.0% and Alestidae 11.4%, and Sarotherodon melanotheron was the most abundant species (12.5%). Every species turned up at every station, diversity was almost the same everywhere (H′ = 2.91-2.93; J′ = 0.97-0.98), and Bray-Curtis similarity was above 92%. Sampling month, on the other hand, explained 81% of the variation in assemblage composition (PERMANOVA, pseudo-F = 11.04, p = 0.028), against only 4% for station (p = 0.861). Mugil cephalus, Neochelon falcipinnis, Elops lacerta and other marine-associated species declined from May to July, as Brycinus spp., Hemichromis fasciatus and Chrysichthys nigrodigitatus became more common. In the early rainy season, then, the assemblage changed far more over time than across space, and monitoring of the reach should follow the seasonal cycle rather than add stations.
10.2478/contagri-2026-0019: Abstract Aquaculture has become an essential sector in Nigeria’s agriculture, significantly contributing to food security, rural employment, and economic diversification. Despite the sector’s rapid growth, Nigeria’s aquaculture industry operates below its potential, with technical efficiency levels far from optimal. This study assesses the determinants of technical efficiency among catfish farmers in Nigeria, using secondary data from a survey of 604 farmers. The result indicate that, despite significant growth in Nigeria’s aquaculture sector, technical efficiency remains suboptimal, with farmers operating at about 67% of their potential output. Using a stochastic frontier production function, we identify key factors affecting productivity and efficiency, including fish stock, household size, culture type, management system, and membership in farmers’ associations. The study highlights the need for targeted policies to enhance resource utilization, promote diversified farming practices, and support farmer associations to optimize technical efficiency in Nigeria’s catfish farming sector. These findings have important implications for improving productivity and ensuring food security in the country.
10.3390/fishes11110655: Integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) combines fed and extractive species, yet appropriate biomass allocation among trophic groups remains poorly defined. This study investigated water quality regulation and stocking biomass ratios in a black seabream (Acanthopagrus schlegelii)-mussel (Mytilus coruscus)-seaweed (Ulva lactuca) IMTA system. Sequential monoculture, two-species, and three-species experiments were conducted in 300 L aquaria over 15 days, with three replicates per treatment. Black seabream monoculture increased NH4+-N and PO43--P accumulation relative to controls, whereas U. lactuca reduced dissolved nutrient concentrations. Fish-mussel co-culture did not prevent nutrient accumulation, while increasing fish biomass in fish-seaweed co-culture was associated with greater nutrient accumulation and lower seaweed RGR, which may have also been influenced by direct grazing by black seabream. Conversely, seaweed relative growth rate (RGR) increased with mussel biomass in mussel-seaweed co-culture. Among three-species treatments, FMU1 (80 g fish, 600 g mussels, and 150 g seaweed; initial biomass ratio 1:7.5:1.875) showed the best overall balance among the three tested fish biomass levels under the experimental conditions. 10.3390/aquacj6040057: Aquaculture is an important source of food, employment and economic development, but maintaining appropriate water quality remains a major challenge for farmers. Parameters like temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), turbidity and salinity have significant effects on the growth, health, feeding efficiency and survival of aquatic organisms. The system receives the registered GPS coordinates of an aquaculture pond and automatically navigates the UAV to the pond for measurement. When the UAV arrives at the pond, it visits several preselected sites and submerges a detachable multi-parameter sensing module to collect the water-quality parameters. An embedded controller processes the sensor data and transmits the measurements, GPS coordinates and time stamps to a cloud database via wireless communication. One mobile sensing unit can monitor multiple ponds and form a spatially indexed historical database of water quality. The architecture lays a foundation for AI-based anomaly detection, water-quality prediction, disease-risk assessment, and intelligent decision support for precision aquaculture.
10.1139/er-2026-0153: The ocean, the world's largest carbon pool, plays a critical role in regulating the global climate. Within this system, the microbial carbon pump (MCP) is a key mechanism for long-term carbon sequestration, converting organic carbon into diverse and structurally complex dissolved molecules that persist in the environment. Despite the dramatic expansion of bivalve aquaculture in recent decades, its contribution to carbon sequestration through the MCP remains poorly understood and understudied. This article critically assesses the impact of bivalve aquaculture on the carbon cycle, particularly its role in enhancing the MCP. Bivalve aquaculture influences the carbon cycle in several ways. First, it increases dissolved organic carbon (DOC) in surrounding waters through direct excretion by bivalves and enhances primary productivity, particularly in oligotrophic waters. These changes boost microbial biomass and may potentially accelerate the production of recalcitrant dissolved organic carbon (RDOC), a key component of long-term carbon storage; however, increased DOC release and microbial activity do not by themselves demonstrate RDOC production, and direct evidence from bivalve aquaculture is currently lacking. Second, intensive bivalve aquaculture alters phytoplankton community structure, shifting dominance from diatoms to cyanobacteria and picophytoplankton. These smaller phytoplankton groups tend to release more RDOC into the environment compared to diatoms and microphytoplankton, further contributing to carbon sequestration. By elucidating the mechanisms through which bivalve aquaculture enhances carbon sequestration via the MCP, this article provides valuable insights for developing sustainable bivalve fisheries and aquaculture management strategies. Such strategies can harness the potential of bivalve aquaculture to mitigate climate change impacts while supporting global food security.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1924894: Located in the Gulf of Honduras between Guatemala and southern Belize, Cayman Crown (Corona Caimán) is a recently documented offshore coral reef system of high geomorphological complexity lying at the terminus of the deep Cayman Trench. Following the 2019 bleaching, corals recovered nearly completely, demonstrating strong short-term post-disturbance resilience. In contrast, consecutive bleaching during the Fourth GCBE resulted in approximately 29% overall coral mortality and persistent residual bleaching extending into the February 2025 post-disturbance survey (BSI: 4-10%). The 2023-24 bleaching caused pronounced live coral cover losses, particularly at Corona Caimán Valle de Aga CC01 (50.3% to 34.1%) and Corona Caimán Bajón GT008 (35.7% to 22.5%), while Corona Caimán 2 CC02 showed a slight increase (24.7% to 28.3%), indicating variability in site-level responses. These findings are consistent with projections of increasing marine heatwave frequency, under which reefs would experience repeated bleaching with shorter recovery windows. The transition from near-complete recovery following a single acute bleaching disturbance to measurable colony mortality under consecutive bleaching events suggests that repeated heat stress may erode the resilience of even offshore reefs.
10.1108/jadee-04-2026-0301: Purpose This study examines aquaculture households' intentions to transition to organic aquaculture in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the hypothesized direct, indirect and moderating relationships. The model also does not fully account for socio-demographic, structural and institutional factors that may affect the intention-behavior gap. Third, by applying this framework to aquaculture households in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam, the study provides context-specific insights for policymakers, extension agencies and other stakeholders in designing policies and support programs for organic aquaculture transition.
10.1073/pnas.2600502123: In a thermally stratified lake, freshwater fish select habitats that align with their thermal preferences. Applying our model to 877,927 Canadian and Alaskan lakes predicted a roughly even split between warm and cold winter conditions; however, 73% of the 66,500 known Lake Trout lakes exhibited warmer winter conditions, where Lake Trout would occupy the upper water column during winter.
10.3897/neotropical.21.e212775: Tropical freshwater fisheries support both biodiversity and human livelihoods, yet long-term fishery characteristics data remain scarce across much of the Amazon Basin. 10.1139/cjz-2026-0108: Intestinal disaccharidases are key determinants of carbohydrate assimilation in fish. 10.55885/jucep.v6i2.1231: The Consumer Cooperative Usaha Mandiri in Tanjung Binga Village, Belitung Regency, encounters challenges in valorizing underutilized grade C fish catches, while local livestock farmers remain reliant on relatively expensive commercial feed sourced externally. 10.46989/001c.173408: Mandarin fish ( Siniperca chuatsi ) is an economically important freshwater aquaculture species in China, yet the maternal genetic composition of cultured stocks from different regions remains insufficiently characterized. 10.56201/ijaes.v10.no10.2024.pg162.176: This study assessed the socioeconomic characteristics and constraints confronting fish farmers in three agricultural zones (Owerri, Orlu and Okigwe), of Imo State, Nigeria. Besides, 83% and 92% of the respondents ascribed high cost of feed and inadequate capital respectively as major challenges confronting aquaculture activities in these area. The state government through the Imo State Ministry of Agriculture can establish Fish Demonstration Farms in the three agricultural zones to serve as fish skill acquisition farms, for regular training of fish farmers in the state. All these will definitely assist in the development of aquaculture in Imo State
10.3390/sci8110361: Background: The Arieș River basin in Romania is historically mining-impacted, and data on metal accumulation in its fish and the associated risk to consumers are scarce. Results: Multivariate statistical analysis revealed distinct species- and tissue-related patterns in elemental composition. Conclusions: Elemental contamination in fish from the Arieș River was generally low, and species and tissue type influenced elemental composition and dietary relevance. 10.3390/fishes11110654: South Korea’s olive flounder aquaculture industry predominantly relies on raw fish-based moist pellets (MP), raising concerns regarding marine resource use and environmental sustainability. 10.3390/pathogens15111176: Viral nervous necrosis (VNN), caused by nervous necrosis virus (NNV), is a devastating viral disease affecting marine fish aquaculture worldwide, particularly during larval and juvenile stages. 10.56557/upjoz/2026/v47i215945: Rainwater-harvesting ponds offer opportunities for freshwater aquaculture by enabling the additional productive use of existing water-storage structures. 10.3897/bdj.14.e209360: Maërl beds, also known as rhodolith beds, are biogenic benthic habitats formed by unattached coralline algae and support diverse macrobenthic assemblages. 10.3390/aquacj6040056: Expanded polystyrene floats have been identified as a significant source of marine microplastic in oyster aquaculture, yet no certification criterion assesses the material that the certified alternatives shed. 10.9734/ajriz/2026/v9i4330: African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) is an economically important aquaculture species in Nigeria, and sustainable hatchery production depends partly on the availability of suitable male broodstock and good-quality semen. 10.29165/ajarcde.v11i1.1511: Water quality largely determines the success of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) cultivation. Contribution to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):SDG 2 (Zero Hunger)SDG 4 (Quality Education)SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)
10.3389/fmars.2026.1943975: Seafood constitutes a major pathway for the transfer of naturally occurring and anthropogenic radionuclides from marine ecosystems to humans. 10.3389/fevo.2026.1960019: Background Tropical coastal seascapes rely on ecological connectivity between mangrove, seagrass, and coral reef habitats to sustain fish biodiversity and fisheries productivity. Our bipartite network analysis showed significant nestedness (NODF = 47.3, p < 0.001), indicating that generalist species disproportionately maintain seascape connectivity. Discussion These findings demonstrate that integrating eDNA with machine learning provides a scalable, high-resolution toolkit for defining functional connectivity and prioritizing species for ecosystem-based fisheries management in the Anthropocene.
10.1073/pnas.2616760123: Mollusks are able to secrete and repair the most diverse and complex calcareous tissues in the animal kingdom, yet the detailed molecular mechanisms of these biomineralization processes, especially for the deep-sea calcifiers, remain to be elucidated. Here, using an in situ experiment, we report a repair mechanism for acid-induced shell damage via biologically mediated vaterite formation in the deep-sea cold-seep mussel Gigantidas haimaensis . Interestingly, the mussels secreted and recrystallized amorphous calcium carbonate into vaterite to seal the acid-induced dissolution porosities within 30 h. Calcium and nucleation substrates were potentially supplied by the mantle, including calcium-binding proteins and hydroxyapatite. Calcium then reacted with readily available carbonate in the extrapallial space, whose precipitation can be promoted by the nucleation substrates. This rapid repair mechanism is likely an advantage in the habitat of these mussels, which are characterized by pulsed acidification events from the seeping fluids. Furthermore, our finding expands our understanding of the diverse biomineralization mechanisms by which mollusks maintain their protective shells.
10.1242/jeb.252974: ABSTRACT Freshwater habitats display highly diverse flow regimes and oxygen tension (PO2) dynamics, driving lentic and lotic fish to evolve distinct physiological strategies for sustaining oxygen supply capacity (α) under hypoxic stress and high energy demand. Pseudorasbora parva had superior hypoxia tolerance [lower critical PO2 at maximum and routine metabolic rate (Pcrit-MMR, Pcrit) and lower PO2 at loss of body equilibrium (PLOE)] via enhanced α, higher liver glycogen, and hypoxia-induced lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) upregulation, while A. fasciatus exhibited higher MMR, matching lotic aerobic demands. Within each species, elevated α correlated with lower Pcrit-MMR, Pcrit and PLOE. Unexpectedly, α was uncorrelated with MMR in both species. Biochemical analyses revealed brain LDH activity as a key determinant of hypoxia tolerance in P. parva, while interorgan transport inefficiency causing brain lactate accumulation and glucose depletion limited hypoxia tolerance in A. fasciatus. These findings demonstrate habitat-associated shifts in physiological and biochemical coping mechanisms, highlighting the complex environment-physiology adaptation interplay rather than categorical divergence.
